## 7.17 Deployment compatibility matrix

| Boundary                 | Risk                                              | Mitigation                                                                     |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| SQL DDL → Arrow arrays   | `Utf8View` vs `Utf8` mismatch                     | configure string mapping; test `arrow_typeof`; use DataFusion Arrow re-exports |
| Decimal analytics        | precision overflow / incompatible consumers       | enforce `p <= 76`; prefer `p <= 38` unless needed                              |
| Timestamp interchange    | unit/timezone ambiguity                           | `arrow_cast` to explicit `Timestamp(unit, tz)`                                 |
| Dirty CSV/JSON ingestion | cast failures                                     | `arrow_try_cast` + rejected-record query                                       |
| External SQL dialects    | unsupported `UUID`, `DATETIME`, `VARBINARY`, etc. | normalize types before DataFusion                                              |
| Generated SQL            | accidental `DOUBLE` for money                     | type intent policy: money → `DECIMAL`, metrics → `DOUBLE`                      |
| UDFs                     | concrete Arrow array mismatch                     | support `Utf8View`/`Utf8` as configured or force mapping                       |
| Parquet/Arrow export     | downstream type incompatibility                   | export schema audit using `arrow_typeof` / Arrow schema inspection             |

---

## 7.18 Best-practice policy for LLM agents

```text
1. Normalize source dialect types into DataFusion-supported SQL types.
2. Use VARCHAR/TEXT/STRING for strings; remember declared mapping defaults to Utf8View.
3. Use BIGINT for generic integer IDs; INTEGER only for Int32 contracts.
4. Use DECIMAL(p,s) for money; reject p > 76.
5. Use DOUBLE for approximate analytics; avoid FLOAT unless Float32 is required.
6. Use TIMESTAMP plus arrow_cast for explicit unit/timezone.
7. Use BYTEA and X'...' for binary; never generate VARBINARY/BINARY.
8. Replace DATETIME with TIMESTAMP.
9. Replace UUID with VARCHAR plus app validation unless custom Arrow metadata exists.
10. Verify generated schemas with arrow_typeof in tests.
11. Use arrow_try_cast for dirty ingestion; surface rejected rows.
12. Use arrow_cast for Arrow-exact output contracts.
13. Pin and test string mapping configuration across upgrades.
```

---

## 7.19 Anti-pattern inventory

* Generating `DATETIME` in DataFusion SQL.
* Generating `UUID` and expecting native support.
* Generating `VARBINARY` / `BINARY` instead of `BYTEA`.
* Assuming `VARCHAR` always maps to `Utf8`; default declared mapping is `Utf8View`.
* Assuming string literal type equals declared string column type.
* Using `DOUBLE` for financial values.
* Using `DECIMAL(100,2)` despite max precision 76.
* Casting timestamp values without specifying unit/timezone when output contract needs precision.
* Swallowing `arrow_try_cast` nulls without rejected-row audit.
* Exporting Arrow/Parquet without schema validation.
* Building Rust `StringArray`-only UDFs when SQL declarations may produce `Utf8View`.
* Treating unsupported SQL type list as equivalent to unsupported runtime nested data; DDL mapping and expression/source capabilities are different surfaces.
* Depending on exact type-string formatting without version-pinned tests.

---

## 7.20 Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Determine whether type appears in CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE, CAST, literal inference, UDF output, or Rust RecordBatch schema.
[ ] Use DataFusion SQL-to-Arrow mapping table for declarations and CAST.
[ ] Audit expression types with arrow_typeof.
[ ] Use arrow_cast for Arrow-specific type targets.
[ ] Use arrow_try_cast for dirty input and log rejected rows.
[ ] Set datafusion.sql_parser.map_string_types_to_utf8view deliberately.
[ ] Reject unsupported SQL type declarations before planning.
[ ] Enforce DECIMAL precision <= 76.
[ ] Specify timestamp unit/timezone for external contracts.
[ ] Use BYTEA / X'...' for binary payloads.
[ ] Validate Rust Arrow schemas against SQL output schemas.
[ ] Snapshot type-audit queries under pinned DataFusion version.
```

---

## 7.21 Comparison coercion changes in DataFusion 54

DataFusion 54 changed string-vs-numeric coercion for comparison contexts to **numeric-preferring** semantics. When one side of a comparison is a string and the other is numeric, the string side is now cast to the numeric type, so ordering and equality follow numeric semantics:

```sql
-- DataFusion 53: string comparison ('5' > '100' lexicographically) -> true
-- DataFusion 54: numeric comparison (5 > 100) -> false
SELECT 5 > '100';
```

Consequences to plan for:

* **Invalid numeric strings now error.** `SELECT 5 > 'abc'` fails with a cast error at runtime instead of silently comparing text. Filters that previously "worked" by lexicographic accident now surface data-quality problems as errors.
* **Mixed-type `IN` lists can fail to plan.** A list such as `str_col IN ('a', 1)` must coerce every element to one common type; with numeric-preferring comparison coercion this may produce a planning or cast error rather than a stringly-typed comparison.
* **Union-like contexts keep string-preferring behavior.** `UNION`, `CASE ... THEN/ELSE` branch unification, and `NVL2` are *type unification* contexts, not comparisons; they still prefer strings (`SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 'a'` coerces to string) because every number has a textual representation.

Under the hood, `datafusion_expr_common::type_coercion::binary` reorganized: the old `comparison_coercion_numeric` helper was **removed**, `comparison_coercion(lhs, rhs)` itself now implements numeric-preferring comparison semantics, and a new `type_union_coercion(lhs, rhs)` handles the string-preferring UNION/CASE-THEN/NVL2 contexts. Code that called `comparison_coercion_numeric` should call `comparison_coercion`; code that used `comparison_coercion` to unify UNION-like branches should call `type_union_coercion`.

```rust
use datafusion::logical_expr::type_coercion::binary::{
    comparison_coercion, type_union_coercion,
};
use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::DataType;

// comparison context: numeric wins
let cmp = comparison_coercion(&DataType::Int64, &DataType::Utf8);
assert_eq!(cmp, Some(DataType::Int64));

// unification context (UNION/CASE/NVL2): string wins
let uni = type_union_coercion(&DataType::Int64, &DataType::Utf8);
assert_eq!(uni, Some(DataType::Utf8));
```

Agent rules:

```text
Audit every filter comparing string columns to numeric literals before upgrading to 54.
Expect cast errors (not false/true) for non-numeric strings in numeric comparisons.
Quote consistently in IN lists; do not mix string and numeric elements.
Use comparison_coercion for predicates; type_union_coercion for UNION/CASE/NVL2 unification.
Add regression SQL tests for 5 > '100'-style predicates when migrating from 53.
```

[1]: https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/sql/data_types.html "Data Types — Apache DataFusion  documentation"
[2]: https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/sql/scalar_functions.html "Scalar Functions — Apache DataFusion  documentation"


# DataFusion Advanced — 8) DDL and catalog-affecting SQL

Style target follows the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

## 8.0 Mental model: DDL mutates the catalog graph

```text
SQL DDL
  → SessionContext::sql / sql_with_options
  → LogicalPlan::Ddl / DdlStatement-like plan
  → DataFrame action: collect / show / execute
  → catalog side effect
      CatalogProviderList
        → CatalogProvider
          → SchemaProvider
            → TableProvider
```

DataFusion’s catalog hierarchy is explicit: `CatalogProviderList` contains `CatalogProvider`s; a `CatalogProvider` contains `SchemaProvider`s; a `SchemaProvider` contains `TableProvider`s. The library guide states that DataFusion ships basic in-memory catalog implementations and supports DDL through this catalog API; custom catalogs/schemas/tables are implemented through traits. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 8.1 DDL support map

| SQL                                    | Current documented status                   | Catalog effect                                      |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `CREATE DATABASE`                      | documented                                  | creates catalog                                     |
| `CREATE SCHEMA`                        | documented                                  | creates schema under catalog/default catalog        |
| `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`                | documented                                  | registers file/object-store location as named table |
| `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT` / `AS VALUES` | documented                                  | creates in-memory table                             |
| `DROP TABLE`                           | documented                                  | removes table from DataFusion catalog               |
| `CREATE VIEW`                          | documented                                  | creates virtual table based on query/values         |
| `DROP VIEW`                            | documented                                  | removes view from catalog                           |
| `DESCRIBE` / `DESC`                    | documented                                  | introspection only                                  |
| `DROP SCHEMA`                          | **not listed in current SQL DDL reference** | use Rust catalog API / custom SQL layer if needed   |

The current DDL reference lists `CREATE DATABASE`, `CREATE SCHEMA`, `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`, `CREATE TABLE`, `DROP TABLE`, `CREATE VIEW`, `DROP VIEW`, and `DESCRIBE`; it does **not** list `DROP SCHEMA`. However, the Rust `CatalogProvider` trait has a provided `deregister_schema(name, cascade)` method, so schema removal is an API/custom-catalog concern rather than a currently documented SQL statement. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 8.2 Executing DDL through `SessionContext`

### Syntax pattern

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    ctx.sql("CREATE TABLE foo (x INTEGER)")
        .await?
        .collect()
        .await?;

    assert!(ctx.table_exist("foo")?);

    Ok(())
}
```

`SessionContext::sql` creates a `DataFrame` from SQL text and implements DDL statements such as `CREATE TABLE` / `CREATE VIEW` plus DML such as `INSERT INTO` using in-memory default implementations. The docs example for `CREATE TABLE foo` calls `collect().await?` and then checks `ctx.table_exist("foo")`. ([Docs.rs][3])

### Restrict DDL

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);

let result = ctx
    .sql_with_options("CREATE TABLE foo (x INTEGER)", options)
    .await;

assert!(result.is_err());
```

`sql_with_options` validates SQL against `SQLOptions` before producing a `DataFrame`; the docs show using `SQLOptions::new().with_allow_ddl(false)` to prevent `CREATE TABLE`. Use this path for user-supplied SQL, shared services, read-only endpoints, or any product surface where catalog mutation is not intended. ([Docs.rs][3])

---

## 8.3 `CREATE DATABASE`: catalog creation

### Syntax

```sql
CREATE DATABASE [ IF NOT EXISTS ] catalog_name;
```

### Example

```sql
CREATE DATABASE cat;
```

`CREATE DATABASE` creates a catalog with the specified name. In DataFusion terminology this is a catalog-level object, not a durable database engine instance with storage/transactions unless your catalog implementation provides those semantics. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Agent rules

```text
CREATE DATABASE = register/create CatalogProvider-like namespace.
Do not assume persistence.
Do not assume user/role/privilege semantics.
Use IF NOT EXISTS for idempotent setup scripts.
Use custom CatalogProvider for durable catalog metadata.
```

---

## 8.4 `CREATE SCHEMA`: schema namespace creation

### Syntax

```sql
CREATE SCHEMA [ IF NOT EXISTS ] [ catalog. ] schema_name;
```

### Examples

```sql
CREATE SCHEMA analytics;

CREATE DATABASE cat;
CREATE SCHEMA cat.emu;
```

`CREATE SCHEMA` creates a schema under the specified catalog, or under the default DataFusion catalog when no catalog is specified. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Rust-side catalog equivalent

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::{CatalogProvider, MemoryCatalogProvider, MemorySchemaProvider};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let ctx = SessionContext::new();

let catalog = Arc::new(MemoryCatalogProvider::new());
catalog.register_schema("analytics", Arc::new(MemorySchemaProvider::new()))?;

ctx.register_catalog("cat", catalog);
```

`MemoryCatalogProvider` is a simple in-memory catalog with `new()` creating an empty schema collection, while `MemorySchemaProvider` is a simple in-memory schema with `new()` creating an empty table collection. ([Docs.rs][5])

### `DROP SCHEMA` advisory

```sql
-- Do not generate this as portable/current DataFusion SQL without version testing:
DROP SCHEMA analytics;
```

Current DataFusion SQL docs do not list `DROP SCHEMA`; if schema removal is required, use `CatalogProvider::deregister_schema(name, cascade)` in Rust or add a custom SQL/planner layer. The trait-level method exists, but SQL-level support should be treated as absent unless verified against the pinned DataFusion version. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 8.5 `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`: file/object-store backed table registration

### Syntax

```sql
CREATE [UNBOUNDED] EXTERNAL TABLE
[ IF NOT EXISTS ]
<table_name> [ (<column_definition>) ]
STORED AS <file_type>
[ PARTITIONED BY (<column_list>) ]
[ WITH ORDER (<ordered_column_list>) ]
[ OPTIONS (<key_value_list>) ]
LOCATION <literal>
```

```text
file_type := CSV | ARROW | PARQUET | AVRO | JSON
column_definition := column_name data_type, ...
key_value_list := 'key' 'value', 'key' 'value', ...
```

`CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` registers a local filesystem or remote object-store location as a named queryable table. Supported file types in the documented syntax are `CSV`, `ARROW`, `PARQUET`, `AVRO`, and `JSON`; `LOCATION` can point to a file or a directory of partitioned files locally or on an object store. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Parquet: schema inferred from file metadata

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE taxi
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION '/mnt/nyctaxi/tripdata.parquet';
```

For Parquet external tables, DataFusion docs state it is not necessary to provide schema information. DataFusion may read files to gather statistics during table creation; this can accelerate subsequent queries but can be expensive, and `datafusion.execution.collect_statistics = false` disables statistics collection before table creation. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.collect_statistics = false;

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE taxi
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION '/mnt/nyctaxi/tripdata.parquet';
```

### CSV: schema inferred by scanning subset

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS CSV
LOCATION '/path/to/aggregate_simple.csv'
OPTIONS ('has_header' 'true');
```

For CSV external tables, the schema is inferred by scanning a subset of the file unless an explicit schema is supplied. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### CSV with explicit schema

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test (
    c1  VARCHAR NOT NULL,
    c2  INT NOT NULL,
    c3  SMALLINT NOT NULL,
    c4  SMALLINT NOT NULL,
    c5  INT NOT NULL,
    c6  BIGINT NOT NULL,
    c7  SMALLINT NOT NULL,
    c8  INT NOT NULL,
    c9  BIGINT NOT NULL,
    c10 VARCHAR NOT NULL,
    c11 FLOAT NOT NULL,
    c12 DOUBLE NOT NULL,
    c13 VARCHAR NOT NULL
)
STORED AS CSV
LOCATION '/path/to/aggregate_test_100.csv'
OPTIONS ('has_header' 'true');
```

Use explicit schema for stable production ingestion, deterministic type/nullability contracts, CSVs with dirty samples, partitioned datasets, or cases where inference can produce wrong integer/float/string/nullability choices. DataFusion’s DDL docs show the explicit-schema form for CSV. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Compressed CSV

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS CSV
COMPRESSION TYPE GZIP
LOCATION '/path/to/aggregate_simple.csv.gz'
OPTIONS ('has_header' 'true');
```

DataFusion’s DDL docs show compressed CSV registration with `COMPRESSION TYPE GZIP`. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

---

## 8.6 External table paths: file vs directory vs wildcard

### File

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE hits
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'hits.parquet';
```

### Directory

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE taxi
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION '/mnt/nyctaxi/';
```

For directory-backed Parquet registration, DataFusion CLI docs note that paths must end with `/`; otherwise the path is treated as a file rather than a directory. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

### Avoid wildcards

```sql
-- Not supported in DataFusion CLI docs:
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test (
  message TEXT,
  day DATE
)
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/*.parquet';
```

```sql
-- Preferred:
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test (
  message TEXT,
  day DATE
)
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/my_table/';
```

DataFusion CLI docs state that wildcards are not supported and recommend specifying a directory path directly so DataFusion reads compatible files within that directory; this is especially important because wildcard semantics are not universal across S3/GCS/object stores. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

---

## 8.7 Partitioned external tables

### Automatic Hive partition discovery

```text
hive_partitioned/
├── a=1
│   └── b=200
│       └── file1.parquet
└── a=2
    └── b=100
        └── file2.parquet
```

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE hive_partitioned
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION '/path/to/hive_partitioned/';

SELECT count(*)
FROM hive_partitioned
WHERE b = 100;
```

DataFusion DDL docs state that Hive-compliant partition columns and values are automatically detected and incorporated into schema/data when a top-level partitioned directory is registered as an external table. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Explicit `PARTITIONED BY`

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE taxi
STORED AS PARQUET
PARTITIONED BY (year, month)
LOCATION '/mnt/nyctaxi';
```

If data sources are already partitioned in Hive style, `PARTITIONED BY` can be used for partition pruning. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Agent rules

```text
Use directory root, not wildcard.
Use Hive-style partition dirs: col=value/col=value/file.parquet.
Declare PARTITIONED BY when partition pruning should be explicit.
Keep partition column types consistent and simple.
Do not duplicate partition columns inside files unless you intentionally handle conflicts.
```

---

## 8.8 `WITH ORDER` on external tables

### Syntax

```sql
WITH ORDER (
  sort_expression1 [ASC | DESC] [NULLS { FIRST | LAST }],
  sort_expression2 [ASC | DESC] [NULLS { FIRST | LAST }]
)
```

### Example

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test (
    c1  VARCHAR NOT NULL,
    c2  INT NOT NULL,
    c5  INT NOT NULL,
    c8  INT NOT NULL
)
STORED AS CSV
WITH ORDER (c2 ASC, c5 + c8 DESC NULLS FIRST)
LOCATION '/path/to/aggregate_test_100.csv'
OPTIONS ('has_header' 'true');
```

`WITH ORDER` specifies that the data source is already ordered by the given expressions. DataFusion’s docs warn that the clause only specifies the order in which data should be read from the external file; if the data is not actually sorted according to the specified order, results may be incorrect, and the clause does not change the order of the original file. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Agent rules

```text
WITH ORDER is a metadata assertion, not a sort operation.
Use only when upstream file order is guaranteed.
Never infer sortedness from filename/path.
For correctness-critical SQL, verify sortedness or omit WITH ORDER.
```

---

## 8.9 `CREATE UNBOUNDED EXTERNAL TABLE`

### Syntax

```sql
CREATE UNBOUNDED EXTERNAL TABLE events
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION '/mnt/events/input_fifo_or_stream_like_source';
```

`CREATE UNBOUNDED EXTERNAL TABLE` marks a data source as unbounded; DataFusion then tries to execute queries over that source in streaming fashion, and plan generation fails if the query cannot be executed in streaming mode. Queries supported for unbounded sources are a subset of bounded-source queries. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Agent rules

```text
Use UNBOUNDED only for streaming-like sources.
Expect fewer supported query shapes.
Avoid full sorts, global aggregations, and other pipeline breakers unless DataFusion supports the streaming variant.
Treat unbounded query planning failure as expected capability feedback, not a runtime bug.
```

---

## 8.10 External table `OPTIONS`

### Generic shape

```sql
OPTIONS ('key' 'value', 'key2' 'value2')
```

The `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` grammar accepts an `OPTIONS` clause with key/value literals, and format-specific options are documented separately. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### CSV

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS CSV
LOCATION '/path/to/file.csv'
OPTIONS ('has_header' 'true');
```

DataFusion docs show `has_header` for CSV external table registration. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

### Parquet encryption / decryption options

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE encrypted_parquet_table
(
  double_field DOUBLE,
  float_field FLOAT
)
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'pq/'
OPTIONS (
  'format.crypto.file_encryption.encrypt_footer' 'true',
  'format.crypto.file_encryption.footer_key_as_hex' '30313233343536373839303132333435',
  'format.crypto.file_encryption.column_key_as_hex::double_field' '31323334353637383930313233343530',
  'format.crypto.file_encryption.column_key_as_hex::float_field' '31323334353637383930313233343531',
  'format.crypto.file_decryption.footer_key_as_hex' '30313233343536373839303132333435',
  'format.crypto.file_decryption.column_key_as_hex::double_field' '31323334353637383930313233343530',
  'format.crypto.file_decryption.column_key_as_hex::float_field' '31323334353637383930313233343531'
);
```

DataFusion CLI docs show Parquet encryption/decryption settings through `OPTIONS` and note that binary keys are represented in hexadecimal. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

### S3 credentials and public buckets

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'aws.access_key_id' '******',
  'aws.secret_access_key' '******',
  'aws.region' 'us-east-2'
)
LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE nyc_taxi_rides
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://altinity-clickhouse-data/nyc_taxi_rides/data/tripdata_parquet/'
OPTIONS ('aws.skip_signature' 'true');
```

DataFusion CLI docs state that explicit S3 credentials in `OPTIONS` take precedence, followed by AWS SDK/environment configuration; if no credentials are specified, unsigned requests can read public buckets. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

### Agent security rules

```text
Do not place long-lived secrets in SQL strings for shared logs.
Prefer object-store registration or environment/secret-manager integration.
If OPTIONS credentials are allowed, redact SQL logs.
For multi-tenant systems, isolate catalogs/object-store registries by tenant.
Disable CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE for untrusted SQL unless path/credential policy is enforced.
```

---

## 8.11 `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT` / `AS VALUES`: in-memory tables

### Syntax

```sql
CREATE [OR REPLACE] TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] table_name AS [SELECT | VALUES LIST];
```

### Values table

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS valuetable
AS VALUES (1, 'HELLO'), (12, 'DATAFUSION');
```

### Values table with explicit columns

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS valuetable(c1 INT, c2 VARCHAR)
AS VALUES (1, 'HELLO'), (12, 'DATAFUSION');
```

### CTAS

```sql
CREATE TABLE memtable AS
SELECT *
FROM valuetable;
```

The DataFusion DDL docs state that `CREATE TABLE` creates an **in-memory table** from a query or values list and show `VALUES`, explicit column declarations, and `CREATE TABLE memtable AS SELECT * FROM valuetable`. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Agent rules

```text
CREATE TABLE in default DataFusion SQL = in-memory table unless custom catalog/provider changes semantics.
Use CTAS for temporary/session-local derived tables.
Use CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE for file/object-store backed data.
Use custom TableProvider/catalog for durable table semantics.
Do not assume CTAS writes Parquet/CSV files.
Use OR REPLACE intentionally; it changes existing catalog binding.
Use IF NOT EXISTS for idempotent setup.
```

---

## 8.12 `DROP TABLE`

### Syntax

```sql
DROP TABLE [ IF EXISTS ] table_name;
```

### Example

```sql
CREATE TABLE users AS VALUES (1, 2), (2, 3);

DROP TABLE users;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS nonexistent_table;
```

`DROP TABLE` removes the table from DataFusion’s catalog; `IF EXISTS` suppresses an error for missing tables. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### External table drop semantics

```text
DROP TABLE external_table_name
  → removes catalog registration
  → does not imply deleting source files/object-store objects
```

DataFusion’s DDL docs phrase `DROP TABLE` as removing the table from the catalog, not deleting external files. Treat file deletion as a separate storage-layer operation unless a custom catalog/table provider explicitly implements destructive behavior. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

---

## 8.13 `CREATE VIEW` and `DROP VIEW`

### Syntax

```sql
CREATE [ OR REPLACE ] VIEW view_name AS statement;

DROP VIEW [ IF EXISTS ] view_name;
```

### Query-backed view

```sql
CREATE TABLE users AS VALUES (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4), (4, 5);

CREATE VIEW test AS
SELECT column1
FROM users;

SELECT *
FROM test;
```

### Values-backed view

```sql
CREATE VIEW test AS VALUES (1, 2), (5, 6);

SELECT *
FROM test;
```

DataFusion defines a view as a virtual table based on the result of a SQL query; the DDL docs show views created from existing tables and from values lists. `DROP VIEW` removes the view from DataFusion’s catalog. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Agent rules

```text
View = catalog object wrapping query/values, not materialized rows.
Use views for stable logical names, reusable projections, masking, compatibility layers.
Do not assume view expansion result is persisted.
Use CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW for migration-style scripts.
Use DROP VIEW IF EXISTS for idempotent teardown.
Treat views as table-like objects in DESCRIBE and SELECT.
```

---

## 8.14 `DESCRIBE` / `DESC`

### Syntax

```sql
DESCRIBE table_name;
DESC table_name;
```

Output columns:

```text
column_name
data_type
is_nullable
```

`DESCRIBE` and `DESC` display table schema, including column names, data types, and nullable status; docs state it works with regular tables, external tables, views, and qualified names such as `schema_name.table_name`. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Agent type-audit pattern

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE taxi
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION '/mnt/nyctaxi/tripdata.parquet';

DESCRIBE taxi;
```

Use `DESCRIBE` in migrations/tests to verify schema inference, explicit schema declaration, view output, and catalog qualification.

---

## 8.15 Catalog side-effect matrix

| SQL                             | Catalog side effect                 | TableProvider relationship                                     |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CREATE DATABASE cat`           | registers/creates catalog namespace | creates/uses `CatalogProvider`-level object                    |
| `CREATE SCHEMA cat.s`           | creates schema under catalog        | creates/uses `SchemaProvider`-level object                     |
| `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE s.t ...` | registers table name in schema      | table is file/listing provider backed by location              |
| `CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT ...`  | registers in-memory table           | table is in-memory provider                                    |
| `CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT ...`   | registers view table                | view is a `TableProvider`-like virtual table over logical plan |
| `DROP TABLE t`                  | deregisters table                   | removes provider binding                                       |
| `DROP VIEW v`                   | deregisters view                    | removes view binding                                           |
| `DESCRIBE t`                    | none                                | inspects provider schema                                       |

The catalog guide states `SchemaProvider` methods register/get/list/deregister tables and check existence; `TableProvider` supplies the data source abstraction used for scans. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 8.16 Catalog and provider traits: DDL implementation boundary

### `CatalogProviderList`

```rust
pub trait CatalogProviderList: Debug + Sync + Send {
    fn register_catalog(
        &self,
        name: String,
        catalog: Arc<dyn CatalogProvider>,
    ) -> Option<Arc<dyn CatalogProvider>>;

    fn catalog_names(&self) -> Vec<String>;

    fn catalog(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Arc<dyn CatalogProvider>>;
}
```

`CatalogProviderList` registers catalogs, lists catalog names, and retrieves catalogs by name. ([Docs.rs][7])

### `CatalogProvider`

```rust
pub trait CatalogProvider: Debug + Sync + Send {
    fn schema_names(&self) -> Vec<String>;
    fn schema(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>>;

    fn register_schema(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        schema: Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>>>;

    fn deregister_schema(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        cascade: bool,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>>>;
}
```

`CatalogProvider` exposes schema names, schema lookup, schema registration, and schema deregistration hooks. ([Docs.rs][8])

### `SchemaProvider`

```rust
pub trait SchemaProvider: Debug + Sync + Send {
    fn table_names(&self) -> Vec<String>;

    async fn table(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>>;

    fn table_exist(&self, name: &str) -> bool;

    fn register_table(
        &self,
        name: String,
        table: Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>>;

    fn deregister_table(
        &self,
        name: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>>;
}
```

`SchemaProvider` is the SQL DDL boundary for table creation/removal/listing. The docs list required methods for table names, lookup, existence checks, and provided methods for table registration/deregistration. ([Docs.rs][9])

### `TableProvider`

```rust
pub trait TableProvider: Any + Debug + Sync + Send {
    fn schema(&self) -> Arc<Schema>;
    fn table_type(&self) -> TableType;

    async fn scan(
        &self,
        state: &dyn Session,
        projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>,
        filters: &[Expr],
        limit: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>;
}
```

`TableProvider` represents a source of data that can provide Arrow `RecordBatch`es. It supplies schema, filter-pushdown information, and a scan method that returns an `ExecutionPlan` to read the data; projection/filter pushdown can significantly improve scans for formats such as Parquet. In DataFusion 54 the trait declares `Any` as a supertrait instead of requiring a hand-written `fn as_any` method; downcast with trait upcasting, e.g. `provider.downcast_ref::<MyProvider>()` on a `&dyn TableProvider`. ([Docs.rs][10])

---

## 8.17 In-memory catalog vs custom catalog

### Built-in in-memory catalog

```text
MemoryCatalogProvider
  → schemas stored in memory

MemorySchemaProvider
  → tables stored in memory
```

DataFusion’s built-in memory catalog/schema providers are simple in-memory implementations. `MemorySchemaProvider` stores tables in a map-like in-memory structure; docs note the underlying state could instead be a different structure such as a file or transactional database. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Persistence implications

| Catalog implementation     | Metadata persistence     | Table data persistence                                                                                        |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| default/in-memory catalog  | process/session lifetime | external table data persists in files; CTAS table rows do not persist beyond memory catalog/provider lifetime |
| custom file-backed catalog | as implemented           | depends on provider                                                                                           |
| custom DB-backed catalog   | as implemented           | depends on provider                                                                                           |
| object-store catalog       | as implemented           | external objects persist independently                                                                        |

DataFusion docs state basic catalog functionality is in-memory and can be used as-is or extended with custom catalog implementations based on local files or remote object storage. Therefore, persistence is an implementation property, not a DDL guarantee. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Agent rules

```text
Default DDL is session/process-scoped metadata unless a durable custom catalog is installed.
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE persists a pointer in catalog; data remains at LOCATION.
CREATE TABLE AS creates an in-memory table by documented default.
Views are logical catalog entries, not materialized storage.
Production systems needing durable metadata must implement/register a custom catalog.
```

---

## 8.18 Custom catalog deployment pattern

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::{CatalogProvider, MemoryCatalogProvider, MemorySchemaProvider};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

pub fn build_context_with_catalog() -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let catalog = Arc::new(MemoryCatalogProvider::new());
    let schema = Arc::new(MemorySchemaProvider::new());

    catalog.register_schema("analytics", schema)?;
    ctx.register_catalog("prod", catalog);

    Ok(ctx)
}
```

Use this pattern for controlled namespace layout. Replace `MemoryCatalogProvider` / `MemorySchemaProvider` with durable implementations for production metadata persistence, tenancy isolation, governance, or external metastore integration.

---

## 8.19 External table deployment pattern

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

pub async fn register_external_tables(ctx: &SessionContext) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    ctx.sql(
        r#"
        CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS prod.analytics.events (
            event_id VARCHAR NOT NULL,
            event_type VARCHAR,
            user_id VARCHAR,
            event_date DATE
        )
        STORED AS PARQUET
        PARTITIONED BY (event_date)
        LOCATION 's3://company-lake/events/'
        "#,
    )
    .await?
    .collect()
    .await?;

    Ok(())
}
```

Production modifications:

```text
Register object store / credentials outside SQL when possible.
Use explicit schema for stable contracts.
Use partition directory root.
Disable collect_statistics if registration latency matters.
Use DESCRIBE after registration in integration tests.
Never expose arbitrary LOCATION to untrusted users.
```

---

## 8.20 Schema inference vs explicit schema

| Format  | Default schema behavior                                     | Agent recommendation                      |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Parquet | schema derived from Parquet metadata; no schema needed      | omit schema unless overriding/normalizing |
| CSV     | inferred by scanning subset unless explicit schema provided | explicit schema in production             |
| JSON    | infer or explicit depending options/use                     | explicit schema for stable APIs           |
| Avro    | use Avro schema/path behavior                               | test exact schema                         |
| Arrow   | Arrow schema available from source                          | verify expected field names/types         |

DataFusion DDL docs state Parquet does not require schema information and CSV schema is inferred from a subset of the file; CLI docs also state CSV can be inferred automatically or explicitly defined. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Explicit-schema production checklist

```text
[ ] column names normalized
[ ] SQL types map to expected Arrow types
[ ] nullability declared intentionally
[ ] partition columns declared/handled intentionally
[ ] DESCRIBE output captured in tests
[ ] downstream UDFs/providers tested against actual Arrow schema
```

---

## 8.21 DDL governance and read-only mode

### Disable DDL for untrusted SQL

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

pub async fn read_only_sql(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    sql: &str,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(false)
        .with_allow_dml(false)
        .with_allow_statements(false);

    let df = ctx.sql_with_options(sql, options).await?;
    df.show().await?;

    Ok(())
}
```

`sql_with_options` validates whether the query is allowed by `SQLOptions`; docs explicitly suggest this when you want to avoid creating tables, modifying data, or modifying the session. ([Docs.rs][3])

### Agent governance rules

```text
Public SELECT endpoint: allow_ddl=false, allow_dml=false, allow_statements=false.
Admin migration endpoint: allow DDL only for trusted principals.
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE requires path/credential/object-store policy.
DROP TABLE/DROP VIEW require ownership/authorization outside DataFusion core.
CREATE DATABASE/SCHEMA require namespace governance.
DDL auditing must log caller, SQL, affected catalog/schema/table, and previous binding when applicable.
```

---

## 8.22 Migration patterns

### Idempotent setup

```sql
CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS prod;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS prod.analytics;

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS prod.analytics.events (
  event_id VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  event_type VARCHAR,
  user_id VARCHAR,
  event_date DATE
)
STORED AS PARQUET
PARTITIONED BY (event_date)
LOCATION 's3://company-lake/events/';
```

### Replace view

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW prod.analytics.active_users AS
SELECT
  user_id,
  MAX(event_ts) AS last_seen_at
FROM prod.analytics.events
WHERE event_type = 'active'
GROUP BY user_id;
```

### Drop idempotently

```sql
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS prod.analytics.active_users;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS prod.analytics.tmp_users;
```

### Not portable/current

```sql
-- Not documented in current DataFusion DDL reference:
DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS prod.analytics;
```

Use Rust catalog API or custom migration tooling for schema removal.

---

## 8.23 Testing DDL side effects

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::test]
async fn create_table_registers_catalog_entry() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    ctx.sql("CREATE TABLE users AS VALUES (1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Bob')")
        .await?
        .collect()
        .await?;

    assert!(ctx.table_exist("users")?);

    let batches = ctx
        .sql("DESCRIBE users")
        .await?
        .collect()
        .await?;

    assert!(!batches.is_empty());

    ctx.sql("DROP TABLE users")
        .await?
        .collect()
        .await?;

    assert!(!ctx.table_exist("users")?);

    Ok(())
}
```

`SessionContext` exposes `table_exist`, `table`, and `table_provider` for checking registered tables; `DESCRIBE` works for regular tables, external tables, views, and qualified names. ([Docs.rs][3])

---

## 8.24 Best-practice deployment advisory

| Concern                 | Recommendation                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| durable metadata        | implement custom `CatalogProvider` / `SchemaProvider`; do not rely on default memory catalog |
| stable external schemas | prefer explicit schema, especially for CSV/JSON                                              |
| Parquet tables          | let Parquet metadata infer schema unless normalization required                              |
| partition pruning       | use Hive layout + `PARTITIONED BY` where useful                                              |
| object stores           | register object stores/credentials in runtime, not ad hoc SQL secrets                        |
| untrusted SQL           | `sql_with_options` with DDL/DML/statements disabled                                          |
| migrations              | run DDL only through trusted admin path                                                      |
| teardown                | `DROP TABLE` / `DROP VIEW` remove catalog entries; storage deletion is separate              |
| schema deletion         | use Rust catalog API; SQL `DROP SCHEMA` not in current docs                                  |
| tests                   | assert catalog existence and `DESCRIBE` output after DDL                                     |
| performance             | consider `collect_statistics=false` before expensive external table registration             |

---

## 8.25 Anti-pattern inventory

* Generating `DROP SCHEMA` as if it were documented portable DataFusion SQL.
* Assuming `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT` persists data durably.
* Assuming `DROP TABLE` deletes files at `LOCATION`.
* Exposing `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` to untrusted users without path allowlist.
* Logging SQL with inline object-store credentials in `OPTIONS`.
* Using CSV schema inference for production contracts.
* Registering wildcard file paths instead of directory roots.
* Using `WITH ORDER` when source data is not truly sorted.
* Treating `CREATE DATABASE` as a full DBMS database with roles, storage, transactions, and replication.
* Running DDL through `ctx.sql` in a public SQL endpoint.
* Forgetting to consume the returned DataFrame for DDL in Rust examples/tests.
* Relying on memory catalog metadata across process restarts.
* Mixing tenants in one catalog without authorization checks.
* Using `OR REPLACE` in migration scripts without recording previous object definition.

---

## 8.26 Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Identify DDL class: catalog / schema / external table / memory table / view / drop / describe.
[ ] Use ctx.sql(...).await?.collect().await? for DDL execution in Rust.
[ ] Use sql_with_options for untrusted SQL.
[ ] Disable DDL unless catalog mutation is intentional.
[ ] Use CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE for files/object stores.
[ ] Use CREATE TABLE AS for in-memory session tables.
[ ] Use CREATE VIEW for reusable logical query names.
[ ] Use DESCRIBE after DDL for schema verification.
[ ] Use explicit schema for CSV/JSON production inputs.
[ ] Use Parquet schema inference unless overriding/normalizing.
[ ] Use directory roots, not wildcards.
[ ] Use PARTITIONED BY for Hive-style pruning.
[ ] Treat DROP TABLE / DROP VIEW as catalog deregistration, not storage deletion.
[ ] Do not generate DROP SCHEMA unless verified/custom implemented.
[ ] Choose in-memory catalog only for session/local/testing use.
[ ] Implement custom CatalogProvider/SchemaProvider/TableProvider for durable/governed systems.
```

[10]: https://docs.rs/datafusion/latest/datafusion/catalog/trait.TableProvider.html "TableProvider in datafusion::catalog - Rust"


# DataFusion Advanced — 9) DML and write paths

Style target follows the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

## 9.0 Write-path mental model

```text
SQL write path:
  INSERT INTO table ...
  COPY query_or_table TO 'path' ...
    → SQL parser/planner
    → DmlStatement / CopyTo logical node
    → physical plan
    → DataSinkExec
    → DataSink::write_all(RecordBatchStream, TaskContext)
    → file(s), object store, memory table, or custom destination

DataFrame write path:
  DataFrame
    → write_table / write_csv / write_json / write_parquet
    → eager execution
    → RecordBatch stream into sink
    → single-row count RecordBatch result
```

DataFusion’s current DML reference uses **`COPY ... TO ...`** for exporting table/query contents to file(s), not Snowflake-style `COPY INTO <table>` loading syntax. The feature matrix uses “COPY .. INTO ..” wording, but the detailed DML syntax page defines `COPY { table_name | query } TO 'file_name' ...`; agents should generate the documented `COPY ... TO` syntax for current DataFusion unless a pinned downstream dialect adds `COPY INTO`. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 9.1 DML capability map

| Capability                   | SQL API                                                                                                               | DataFrame API                                                 | Lower-level trait/API                                            |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| append values/query to table | `INSERT INTO table VALUES ...` / `INSERT INTO table SELECT ...`                                                       | `df.write_table("table", options)`                            | `TableProvider::insert_into`                                     |
| export table/query to files  | `COPY table_or_query TO 'path' ...`                                                                                   | `write_csv`, `write_json`, `write_parquet`                    | `DataSink`, `DataSinkExec`, `CsvSink`, `JsonSink`, `ParquetSink` |
| write CSV                    | `COPY ... STORED AS CSV`; `INSERT INTO` external CSV table                                                            | `write_csv`                                                   | `CsvSink`                                                        |
| write JSON                   | `COPY ... STORED AS JSON`; `INSERT INTO` external JSON table                                                          | `write_json`                                                  | `JsonSink`                                                       |
| write Parquet                | `COPY ... STORED AS PARQUET`; `INSERT INTO` external Parquet table                                                    | `write_parquet`                                               | `ParquetSink`                                                    |
| write Arrow IPC              | `COPY ... STORED AS ARROW`                                                                                            | no top-level `write_arrow` method in current `DataFrame` docs | file-format sink path                                            |
| write Avro                   | feature matrix says data insert includes Avro; current detailed DML page lists COPY formats as parquet/csv/json/arrow | no `write_avro` method in current `DataFrame` docs            | version/feature/custom sink dependent                            |

Current DataFrame docs list `write_parquet`, `write_csv`, `write_json`, and `write_table`; the current DML page lists `COPY` output formats as `parquet`, `csv`, `json`, and `arrow`; the feature matrix lists Avro under Data Insert, so Avro write support should be treated as **version/feature-surface dependent** and verified with the pinned crate/docs/tests before generating Avro write SQL. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 9.2 `INSERT INTO`

### Syntax

```sql
INSERT INTO table_name
{ VALUES ( expression [, ...] ) [, ...] | query };
```

### Values insert

```sql
INSERT INTO target_table
VALUES
  (1, 'Foo'),
  (2, 'Bar');
```

### Query insert

```sql
INSERT INTO target_table
SELECT
  id,
  name
FROM staging_table
WHERE valid = true;
```

The DML docs define `INSERT INTO table_name { VALUES ... | query }` and show a values insert returning a one-row `count` result. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Rust execution

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    ctx.sql("CREATE TABLE target_table (id BIGINT, name VARCHAR)")
        .await?
        .collect()
        .await?;

    let result = ctx
        .sql("INSERT INTO target_table VALUES (1, 'Foo'), (2, 'Bar')")
        .await?
        .collect()
        .await?;

    println!(
        "{}",
        datafusion::arrow::util::pretty::pretty_format_batches(&result)?
    );

    Ok(())
}
```

The result shape is a single count row:

```text
+-------+
| count |
+-------+
| 2     |
+-------+
```

`TableProvider::insert_into` is the trait hook behind table writes; its returned execution plan should return a single `UInt64` column named `count`, matching the SQL and DataFrame write-table result contract. ([Docs.rs][4])

---

## 9.3 `INSERT INTO` target semantics

`INSERT INTO` is only as capable as the target table provider. For built-in external file tables, `INSERT INTO` writes using the table’s file-format options; for custom storage, `TableProvider::insert_into` must be implemented by the provider. The DataFrame API confirms `write_table` uses `TableProvider::insert_into` and the same underlying implementation as SQL `INSERT INTO`. ([Docs.rs][2])

Target classes:

| Target                 | Expected behavior                                                                       |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| memory table           | append/replace behavior depends on provider implementation and insert operation         |
| external CSV table     | write new CSV file(s) using table format options                                        |
| external JSON table    | write JSON file(s) using table format options                                           |
| external Parquet table | write Parquet file(s) using table/table/session/option writer settings                  |
| custom table provider  | provider-defined semantics; must document append/overwrite/replace/transaction behavior |

Agent rule:

```text
INSERT INTO is not a universal storage mutation primitive.
It is a planner path that delegates write semantics to the target TableProvider.
For production correctness, inspect/test the target provider’s insert_into implementation.
```

---

## 9.4 `COPY ... TO ...`

### Syntax

```sql
COPY { table_name | query }
TO 'file_name'
[ STORED AS format ]
[ PARTITIONED BY column_name [, ...] ]
[ OPTIONS( option [, ... ] ) ];
```

`COPY` exports the contents of a table or query to file(s). `STORED AS` chooses the output format; if absent, the format is inferred from filename extension where possible; supported formats listed on the DML page are `parquet`, `csv`, `json`, and `arrow`. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Copy table to JSON by extension inference

```sql
COPY source_table
TO 'file_name.json';
```

### Copy table to Parquet directory

```sql
COPY source_table
TO 'dir_name'
STORED AS PARQUET;
```

### Copy query to Parquet file with writer option

```sql
COPY (
  SELECT *
  FROM source
  ORDER BY time
)
TO 'output.parquet'
OPTIONS (MAX_ROW_GROUP_SIZE 10000000);
```

DataFusion’s DML examples show JSON extension inference, Parquet directory output, partitioned output, and query export with `MAX_ROW_GROUP_SIZE`. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Agent rules

```text
Use COPY ... TO for export.
Use INSERT INTO for writing into an existing registered table.
Use COPY (SELECT ...) TO ... when the write source is a query.
Use STORED AS when path extension is ambiguous or path is a directory.
Use ORDER BY inside the copied query when output ordering matters.
Do not generate COPY INTO <table> for current DataFusion unless a custom dialect supports it.
```

---

## 9.5 Format options precedence

Format/write options can be specified at several levels. DataFusion’s format-options guide states the precedence order, from higher to lower, as: `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` syntax, `COPY` option tuples, then session-level defaults. It also says `INSERT INTO my_table ...` respects the format options from the table definition, such as compression, delimiter, and header configuration. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

```text
highest precedence:
  dedicated CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE syntax / table-specific options
  COPY OPTIONS(...)
  session-level config defaults
lowest precedence
```

Example table-level options respected by `INSERT INTO`:

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE my_table(a BIGINT, b BIGINT)
STORED AS CSV
LOCATION '/tmp/my_csv_table/'
OPTIONS(
  NULL_VALUE 'NAN',
  'has_header' 'true',
  'format.delimiter' ';'
);

INSERT INTO my_table VALUES (1, 2);
```

This yields CSV output using `;` and a header according to the documented example. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

---

## 9.6 CSV write options

CSV options apply when reading or writing CSV. Unsupported options cause query failure. Important write-relevant options include `COMPRESSION`, `HAS_HEADER`, `DELIMITER`, `QUOTE`, `TERMINATOR`, `ESCAPE`, `DOUBLE_QUOTE`, date/time/timestamp formats, and `NULL_VALUE`; `SCHEMA_INFER_MAX_REC`, `NULL_REGEX`, and `COMMENT` are primarily read-side. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

### CSV `COPY`

```sql
COPY (
  SELECT
    id,
    name,
    amount
  FROM clean_orders
  ORDER BY id
)
TO '/tmp/orders.csv'
STORED AS CSV
OPTIONS (
  HAS_HEADER true,
  DELIMITER '|',
  NULL_VALUE ''
);
```

### CSV external table + insert

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE out_csv (
  id BIGINT,
  name VARCHAR,
  amount DOUBLE
)
STORED AS CSV
LOCATION '/tmp/out_csv/'
OPTIONS (
  'has_header' 'true',
  'format.delimiter' '|',
  'null_value' ''
);

INSERT INTO out_csv
SELECT id, name, amount
FROM clean_orders;
```

### DataFrame CSV write

```rust
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

ctx.read_csv("input.csv", CsvReadOptions::new())
    .await?
    .sort(vec![col("id").sort(true, true)])?
    .write_csv(
        "out/orders.csv",
        DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
        None, // Option<CsvOptions>
    )
    .await?;
```

`DataFrame::write_csv` eagerly executes the DataFrame and writes CSV file(s). ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 9.7 JSON write options

JSON format options include `COMPRESSION`, with supported values `GZIP`, `BZIP2`, `XZ`, `ZSTD`, and `UNCOMPRESSED`; unsupported options cause query failure. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

### JSON `COPY`

```sql
COPY (
  SELECT
    id,
    event_type,
    event_ts
  FROM events
  WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22'
)
TO '/tmp/events.json'
STORED AS JSON
OPTIONS (
  COMPRESSION UNCOMPRESSED
);
```

### DataFrame JSON write

```rust
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

ctx.sql(
    "SELECT id, event_type, event_ts
     FROM events
     WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22'"
)
.await?
.write_json(
    "out/events.json",
    DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
    None, // Option<JsonOptions>
)
.await?;
```

`DataFrame::write_json` eagerly executes the DataFrame and writes JSON file(s). ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 9.8 Parquet write options

Parquet writer options are the densest write surface. DataFusion supports global and column-specific Parquet options; column-specific keys use `OPTION::COLUMN.NESTED.PATH`. Parquet options include compression, encoding, dictionary encoding, statistics, bloom filters, max row group size, page size limits, write batch size, writer version, Arrow metadata, custom key-value metadata, and parallel writer controls. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

### Parquet `COPY` with row group sizing and compression

```sql
COPY (
  SELECT *
  FROM source
  ORDER BY time
)
TO 'output.parquet'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  MAX_ROW_GROUP_SIZE 1000000,
  COMPRESSION zstd(3),
  STATISTICS_ENABLED page
);
```

### Parquet `COPY` with column-specific compression

```sql
COPY source_table
TO 'out_parquet/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  COMPRESSION snappy,
  'compression::large_text_col' 'zstd(5)',
  'dictionary_enabled::category' 'true',
  'bloom_filter_enabled::id' 'true'
);
```

The format-options guide explicitly shows global `compression snappy` plus column override `'compression::column1' 'zstd(5)'` and states that Parquet column-specific options use `OPTION::COLUMN.NESTED.PATH`. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

### DataFrame Parquet write

```rust
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

ctx.read_csv("input.csv", CsvReadOptions::new())
    .await?
    .sort(vec![col("id").sort(true, true)])?
    .write_parquet(
        "out/orders.parquet",
        DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
        None, // Option<TableParquetOptions>
    )
    .await?;
```

`DataFrame::write_parquet` is available when the `parquet` feature is enabled and eagerly executes the DataFrame to Parquet file(s). ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 9.9 Row group and file sizing

Parquet `MAX_ROW_GROUP_SIZE` sets the maximum number of rows per row group; larger groups require more memory but can improve compression and scan efficiency. Other relevant writer knobs include `DATA_PAGESIZE_LIMIT`, `DATA_PAGE_ROW_COUNT_LIMIT`, `DICTIONARY_PAGE_SIZE_LIMIT`, and `WRITE_BATCH_SIZE`. Defaults shown in current docs include `MAX_ROW_GROUP_SIZE = 1048576`, `DATA_PAGESIZE_LIMIT = 1048576`, `DATA_PAGE_ROW_COUNT_LIMIT = 20000`, `DICTIONARY_PAGE_SIZE_LIMIT = 1048576`, and `WRITE_BATCH_SIZE = 1024`. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

Agent policy:

```text
Small files / low latency:
  lower max row group size
  lower write batch size
  easier downstream incremental reads
  worse compression / more metadata overhead

Large analytics scans:
  larger row groups
  page/statistics enabled
  column-specific compression
  fewer files when possible
  better pruning/compression, more writer memory

Service-safe default:
  keep default row group size unless measured
  set max temp/memory limits at RuntimeEnv
  add integration tests for output schema + row count + file count
```

---

## 9.10 Partitioned output

### SQL `COPY PARTITIONED BY`

```sql
COPY source_table
TO 'dir_name'
STORED AS PARQUET
PARTITIONED BY (column1, column2);
```

Partitioned `COPY` writes hive-style directories. DataFusion’s docs show output such as `dir_name/column1=x/column2=a/<file>.parquet`; by default, `PARTITIONED BY` columns are removed from the output files, and `execution.keep_partition_by_columns true` keeps them. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Keep partition columns

```sql
COPY source_table
TO 'dir_name'
STORED AS PARQUET
PARTITIONED BY (event_date)
OPTIONS (
  'execution.keep_partition_by_columns' 'true'
);
```

The docs state the keep-partition-columns behavior can be enabled through the `execution.keep_partition_by_columns` option or through `ExecutionOptions` within `SessionConfig`. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### DataFrame partitioned output

```rust
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let options = DataFrameWriteOptions::new()
    .with_partition_by(vec!["event_date".to_string(), "region".to_string()]);

ctx.sql("SELECT * FROM events")
    .await?
    .write_parquet("out/events/", options, None)
    .await?;
```

`DataFrameWriteOptions` exposes `with_partition_by(Vec<String>)` for output partitioning. ([Docs.rs][6])

Agent rules:

```text
Partition columns become directory keys.
Default COPY behavior removes partition columns from file payload.
Keep partition columns only when downstream consumers require them.
Partition by low/moderate-cardinality dimensions, not high-cardinality UUIDs.
Avoid tiny-file explosion: partition count × output partitions × writer parallelism.
```

---

## 9.11 Single-file vs directory output

`DataFrameWriteOptions::with_single_file_output(true)` forces single-file output at the exact path; `false` forces directory output with generated filenames. If not set, automatic mode uses an extension-based heuristic; when set to true, an output file is created even if the DataFrame is empty. ([Docs.rs][6])

```rust
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;

let single_file = DataFrameWriteOptions::new()
    .with_single_file_output(true);

let directory_files = DataFrameWriteOptions::new()
    .with_single_file_output(false);
```

Agent decision table:

| Output target                                | `single_file_output`           |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| exact `output.parquet` artifact              | `true`                         |
| dataset directory / parallel files           | `false`                        |
| unknown path policy                          | leave unset and test heuristic |
| empty output should still create marker file | `true`                         |
| large parallel export                        | `false`                        |

---

## 9.12 Output sorting

### SQL query sorting before write

```sql
COPY (
  SELECT *
  FROM source
  ORDER BY time
)
TO 'output.parquet'
OPTIONS (MAX_ROW_GROUP_SIZE 10000000);
```

DataFusion’s DML example explicitly shows `COPY (SELECT * FROM source ORDER BY time) TO 'output.parquet' ...` to maintain query output order in a Parquet file. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### DataFrame writer sorting option

```rust
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;
use datafusion::logical_expr::SortExpr;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let write_options = DataFrameWriteOptions::new()
    .with_sort_by(vec![
        SortExpr::new(col("time"), true, true),
    ]);
```

`DataFrameWriteOptions` provides `with_sort_by(Vec<SortExpr>)`, and `SortExpr` contains `expr`, `asc`, and `nulls_first` fields with a `new(expr, asc, nulls_first)` constructor. ([Docs.rs][6])

Agent rule:

```text
Use query ORDER BY for semantic output ordering.
Use writer sort_by when targeting sink-level layout/sorted output behavior.
Do not assume parallel multi-file output has a global order unless explicitly designed/tested.
```

---

## 9.13 Output file parallelism

DataFusion writes one Parquet file in parallel for each query partition in the documented `COPY` options example. Parquet writer controls include `ALLOW_SINGLE_FILE_PARALLELISM`, `MAXIMUM_PARALLEL_ROW_GROUP_WRITERS`, and `MAXIMUM_BUFFERED_RECORD_BATCHES_PER_STREAM`; the docs list defaults of `true`, `1`, and `2` respectively. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

```sql
COPY source_table
TO 'out/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'allow_single_file_parallelism' 'true',
  'maximum_parallel_row_group_writers' '4',
  'maximum_buffered_record_batches_per_stream' '4'
);
```

Agent deployment policy:

```text
For throughput:
  increase target_partitions
  allow directory output
  tune max parallel row group writers
  measure object-store multipart/write behavior

For exact single artifact:
  with_single_file_output(true) or path with file extension
  expect less output parallelism unless single-file parallelism applies
  verify deterministic row order if required

For object stores:
  prefer directory output
  avoid writing many tiny files
  isolate staging/commit behavior at application layer
```

---

## 9.14 Safe append / overwrite / replace semantics

`DataFrameWriteOptions` has `with_insert_operation(insert_op)` for selecting the insert operation, and `TableProvider::insert_into` receives that operation. Current DataFusion writer semantics are delegated to the target provider; the provider must decide what append, overwrite, or replace means for its backing storage, and whether it is atomic. ([Docs.rs][6])

```rust
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;
use datafusion::logical_expr::dml::InsertOp;

// Append-like table write
let options = DataFrameWriteOptions::new()
    .with_insert_operation(InsertOp::Append);

df.write_table("target_table", options).await?;
```

For version-pinned code, verify the exact `InsertOp` variants and SQL support in the pinned docs/crate; DataFusion’s logical write operation enum models inserts as one DML operation among insert/delete/update/CTAS/truncate, while the detailed SQL DML page currently documents basic `INSERT INTO` values/query syntax rather than a complete MERGE/overwrite SQL surface. ([Docs.rs][7])

Safe write patterns:

| Desired semantics                | Recommended pattern                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| append new files                 | `INSERT INTO external_table SELECT ...` or `df.write_table(... Append ...)`                                                                              |
| overwrite exact output directory | write to new temp/staging path, validate, then atomically swap pointer/catalog outside DataFusion                                                        |
| overwrite partition              | write to staging partition path, validate, then replace partition directory/catalog entry outside DataFusion unless provider implements atomic overwrite |
| replace by key/upsert            | implement custom `TableProvider::insert_into` / app-layer merge; do not assume core SQL MERGE                                                            |
| one-off export                   | `COPY query TO 'path'`                                                                                                                                   |
| durable transactional write      | use a storage system/provider with explicit commit/rollback semantics                                                                                    |

`DataSink::write_all` is called exactly once during each DML statement and must perform any needed commit or rollback before returning; this is the key contract for implementing safe custom sinks. ([Docs.rs][8])

---

## 9.15 DataFrame write APIs

### `write_table`

```rust
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;

let count_batches = df
    .write_table("target_table", DataFrameWriteOptions::new())
    .await?;
```

`write_table` eagerly executes the DataFrame and writes to a named table via `TableProvider::insert_into`; it returns a single `RecordBatch` containing one row and one column representing the count of total rows written. ([Docs.rs][2])

### `write_csv`

```rust
df.write_csv(
    "out/data.csv",
    DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
    None,
).await?;
```

### `write_json`

```rust
df.write_json(
    "out/data.json",
    DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
    None,
).await?;
```

### `write_parquet`

```rust
df.write_parquet(
    "out/data.parquet",
    DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
    None,
).await?;
```

DataFrame `write_csv`, `write_json`, and `write_parquet` execute eagerly and write file(s); `write_parquet` is feature-gated behind `parquet`. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 9.16 `DataFrameWriteOptions`

Current writer option methods:

```rust
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;

let options = DataFrameWriteOptions::new()
    .with_single_file_output(false)
    .with_partition_by(vec!["event_date".to_string(), "region".to_string()]);
```

Available methods include `new`, `with_insert_operation`, `with_partition_by`, `with_single_file_output`, and `with_sort_by`. The docs define `with_single_file_output(true)` as forcing single-file output at the exact path and `false` as forcing directory output with generated filenames. ([Docs.rs][6])

Option interaction rules:

```text
single_file_output(true) + partition_by(...) = conceptually conflicting for many sinks; test pinned version behavior.
partition_by(...) is dataset output layout.
sort_by(...) is output ordering/layout request.
insert_operation(...) is table-provider write semantics.
writer_options argument is format-specific.
```

---

## 9.17 `DataSink` concepts

`DataSink` implements writing streams of `RecordBatch`es to user-defined destinations. Required methods are `schema` and `write_all` (`Any` is a supertrait in DataFusion 54, replacing the removed `fn as_any`); `write_all` receives a `SendableRecordBatchStream` and `TaskContext`, returns `u64` count, and is called exactly once during each DML statement so the sink should commit or rollback before returning. Built-in implementors include `CsvSink`, `JsonSink`, `ParquetSink`, and `MemSink`. ([Docs.rs][8])

Trait shape:

```rust
pub trait DataSink: Any + DisplayAs + Debug + Send + Sync {
    fn schema(&self) -> &Arc<Schema>;

    async fn write_all(
        &self,
        data: Pin<Box<dyn RecordBatchStream<Item = Result<RecordBatch>> + Send>>,
        context: &Arc<TaskContext>,
    ) -> Result<u64>;

    fn metrics(&self) -> Option<MetricsSet> { ... }
}
```

Conceptual responsibilities:

```text
schema()     -> sink input schema contract
write_all()  -> consume entire stream, write destination, return row count
metrics()    -> expose sink metrics for explain/diagnostics
Any          -> supertrait; downcast via sink.downcast_ref::<T>() (DF 54 removed fn as_any)
DisplayAs    -> sink appears in EXPLAIN output
```

`ParquetSink` implements `DataSink` for Parquet files, is feature-gated on `parquet`, takes `FileSinkConfig` plus `TableParquetOptions`, can set sorting columns, and can retrieve metadata for written files keyed by path, including partitioned paths. ([Docs.rs][9])

---

## 9.18 Custom `TableProvider::insert_into` pattern

`TableProvider::insert_into` receives the current session, an input `ExecutionPlan`, and an `InsertOp`; it returns an `ExecutionPlan` for the insertion. The returned plan should produce a single-row count output. Docs point to `DataSinkExec` as the common pattern for inserting streams of `RecordBatch`es as files to an object store. ([Docs.rs][4])

Provider-level design sketch:

```rust
#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl TableProvider for MyWritableTable {
    async fn insert_into(
        &self,
        state: &dyn datafusion::catalog::Session,
        input: Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>,
        insert_op: InsertOp,
    ) -> datafusion::error::Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        // 1. validate schema compatibility
        // 2. select append/overwrite/replace behavior
        // 3. create DataSink for destination
        // 4. return DataSinkExec wrapping input + sink
        todo!()
    }

    // schema / scan / table_type ...
}
```

Implementation invariants:

```text
Validate input schema before writing.
Honor or explicitly reject unsupported InsertOp.
Return count RecordBatch.
Implement commit/rollback in DataSink::write_all.
Expose metrics.
Never partially publish files without recovery policy.
For object stores, use staging paths and manifest/catalog commit where possible.
```

---

## 9.19 SQL write examples: end-to-end patterns

### ETL export: CSV → Parquet

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE raw_orders (
  id BIGINT,
  customer_id BIGINT,
  amount DOUBLE,
  event_date DATE
)
STORED AS CSV
LOCATION '/data/raw/orders/'
OPTIONS ('has_header' 'true');

COPY (
  SELECT
    id,
    customer_id,
    amount,
    event_date
  FROM raw_orders
  WHERE amount IS NOT NULL
)
TO '/data/curated/orders/'
STORED AS PARQUET
PARTITIONED BY (event_date)
OPTIONS (
  COMPRESSION zstd(3),
  MAX_ROW_GROUP_SIZE 1048576,
  STATISTICS_ENABLED page
);
```

### Insert into external table with table options

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE curated_orders (
  id BIGINT,
  customer_id BIGINT,
  amount DOUBLE,
  event_date DATE
)
STORED AS PARQUET
PARTITIONED BY (event_date)
LOCATION '/data/curated/orders/'
OPTIONS (
  COMPRESSION zstd(3),
  MAX_ROW_GROUP_SIZE 1048576
);

INSERT INTO curated_orders
SELECT
  id,
  customer_id,
  amount,
  event_date
FROM raw_orders
WHERE amount > 0;
```

`INSERT INTO` respects table-specific format options defined at `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`, and `COPY` can specify writer options inline. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

---

## 9.20 Rust write-path harness

```rust
use datafusion::arrow::util::pretty::pretty_format_batches;
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    ctx.register_csv("source", "input.csv", CsvReadOptions::new().has_header(true))
        .await?;

    let count_batches = ctx
        .sql(
            "SELECT *
             FROM source
             WHERE amount IS NOT NULL
             ORDER BY id"
        )
        .await?
        .write_parquet(
            "out/orders.parquet",
            DataFrameWriteOptions::new()
                .with_single_file_output(true),
            None,
        )
        .await?;

    println!("{}", pretty_format_batches(&count_batches)?);

    Ok(())
}
```

DataFrame write methods return `Vec<RecordBatch>` just like SQL DML count outputs; `write_table` is documented as returning a single batch with a single count row, and file write methods use the same eager write execution model. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 9.21 Security and governance

DML is stateful and external-effecting. `SQLOptions::with_allow_dml(false)` should be used for read-only SQL endpoints. DML includes examples such as `INSERT INTO` and `COPY`, and DataFusion’s SQL options allow DML to be disabled separately from DDL and statement/config changes. ([Apache DataFusion][10])

Policy table:

| Environment              | DML stance                                                      |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| read-only analytics API  | `allow_dml(false)`                                              |
| internal ETL job         | allow DML, explicit output paths                                |
| admin migration tool     | allow DDL + DML, audited                                        |
| multi-tenant SQL service | DML disabled unless tenant-scoped writable catalog exists       |
| export endpoint          | prefer controlled DataFrame write API over arbitrary `COPY` SQL |
| custom lakehouse         | implement provider-level transaction/commit semantics           |

Required governance controls:

```text
path allowlist / prefix sandbox
object-store credential isolation
row-count / byte-count limits
max output partition/cardinality checks
temporary staging path
atomic publish / catalog commit
audit caller + SQL + destination + count
redact OPTIONS secrets in logs
disable arbitrary DML for untrusted SQL
```

---

## 9.22 Value case: why write through DataFusion

| Feature                             | Value                                                        |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `INSERT INTO`                       | engine-native write path to registered table providers       |
| `COPY query TO`                     | SQL-native export/transcoding path                           |
| DataFrame `write_*`                 | Rust API for controlled ETL without exposing SQL DML         |
| `DataSink`                          | extensible sink abstraction for files, memory, custom stores |
| partitioned output                  | Hive-style lake layout for pruning/downstream engines        |
| Parquet row group/page/stat options | control scan efficiency, compression, pruning metadata       |
| parallel file output                | high-throughput export from partitioned query execution      |
| count result                        | consistent DML observability primitive                       |
| table-provider hook                 | storage-specific commit/append/overwrite semantics           |

---

## 9.23 Best-practice deployment advisory

```text
Use COPY for ad hoc SQL exports.
Use DataFrame write_* for application-controlled exports.
Use INSERT INTO only when target table provider semantics are known.
Use explicit STORED AS for directory outputs.
Use explicit FORMAT/OPTIONS for reproducibility.
Use Parquet for analytics lake outputs.
Use CSV/JSON only for interoperability/debugging/external contracts.
Use partitioned output only with bounded cardinality.
Use staging directories for overwrite/replace.
Use count outputs as audit records.
Use EXPLAIN / metrics for production write diagnostics.
```

Format-specific defaults:

```text
CSV:
  set HAS_HEADER explicitly
  set DELIMITER explicitly for non-comma contracts
  set NULL_VALUE explicitly for downstream tools

JSON:
  set COMPRESSION explicitly when file size matters
  validate nested output with target consumer

Parquet:
  set COMPRESSION explicitly
  tune MAX_ROW_GROUP_SIZE only after measuring
  keep STATISTICS_ENABLED page unless compatibility says otherwise
  use bloom filters only for columns with lookup/filter value
  set CREATED_BY / metadata keys for lineage if needed
```

---

## 9.24 Anti-pattern inventory

* Generating `COPY INTO <table>` instead of current DataFusion `COPY ... TO`.
* Exposing arbitrary `COPY ... TO 's3://...'` to users.
* Assuming `INSERT INTO` is transactional for every `TableProvider`.
* Assuming `DROP/overwrite` semantics from `INSERT INTO`.
* Using `COPY` without `STORED AS` for directory paths.
* Partitioning by high-cardinality IDs.
* Overwriting production paths directly instead of staging + swap.
* Relying on output row order without `ORDER BY`.
* Writing many tiny Parquet files via excessive partitions.
* Setting huge Parquet row groups without memory testing.
* Disabling Arrow metadata without downstream compatibility reason.
* Treating Avro write as universally available despite current detailed DML/DataFrame docs.
* Logging SQL `OPTIONS` containing cloud credentials.
* Forgetting that partition columns are removed from payload by default in `COPY PARTITIONED BY`.
* Implementing `DataSink::write_all` without commit/rollback behavior.

---

## 9.25 Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Choose write surface: INSERT INTO / COPY TO / DataFrame write_* / custom DataSink.
[ ] For current DataFusion, generate COPY ... TO, not COPY INTO <table>.
[ ] Register source and target tables before SQL DML.
[ ] Use sql_with_options and disable DML for read-only endpoints.
[ ] Use explicit STORED AS for all directory outputs.
[ ] For CSV, set HAS_HEADER/DELIMITER/NULL_VALUE deliberately.
[ ] For JSON, set compression deliberately.
[ ] For Parquet, set compression and row group policy deliberately.
[ ] Use ORDER BY inside write query if row order matters.
[ ] Use PARTITIONED BY only for bounded-cardinality dimensions.
[ ] Decide whether partition columns should remain in file payload.
[ ] Use DataFrameWriteOptions for single-file/directory/partition/sort behavior.
[ ] Treat write_table and INSERT INTO as TableProvider::insert_into delegation.
[ ] Verify count RecordBatch output after every DML/write operation.
[ ] Stage and atomically publish for overwrite/replace semantics.
[ ] Implement DataSink::write_all with commit/rollback and metrics for custom sinks.
[ ] Pin DataFusion version before depending on Avro, InsertOp variants, overwrite, or custom writer behavior.
```

[4]: https://docs.rs/datafusion/latest/datafusion/catalog/trait.TableProvider.html "TableProvider in datafusion::catalog - Rust"
[5]: https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/sql/format_options.html "Format Options — Apache DataFusion  documentation"
[6]: https://docs.rs/datafusion/latest/datafusion/dataframe/struct.DataFrameWriteOptions.html "DataFrameWriteOptions in datafusion::dataframe - Rust"
