## 15.33 Parquet changes in DataFusion 54

### Nested leaf-level projection and struct-member filter pushdown

DataFusion 54 pushes **nested projections down to Parquet leaf columns**: selecting `payload.device.id` decodes only the leaf column(s) actually referenced instead of materializing the whole `payload` struct. Filters on struct members (`WHERE payload.device.id = 7`) likewise push down into Parquet decoding, so row-group/page pruning and late materialization apply to nested fields, not just top-level columns. Wide structs where queries touch a few members see the largest wins; no configuration is required — write nested field accesses and let the planner prune.

### Statistics-proven-true filter skipping

Pruning has historically used min/max statistics to skip row groups where a predicate is provably **false**. DataFusion 54 adds the dual: when statistics prove a predicate is **true for every row** in a container (for example `WHERE x > 0` on a row group with `min(x) = 5`), per-row predicate evaluation is skipped for that container entirely. Highly selective *and* highly non-selective filters both get cheaper; no new configuration is involved, but accurate Parquet statistics matter more than before.

### INT96 timezone coercion

`datafusion.execution.parquet.coerce_int96_tz` is new in 54 and complements the existing `coerce_int96` resolution option: it applies an optional timezone to coerced INT96 timestamps (`'UTC'` recommended for Spark `TimestampType` semantics). See §15.15 for the INT96 walkthrough.

### Content-defined chunking (experimental writer feature)

The 54 Parquet writer can use **content-defined chunking (CDC)** for data-page boundaries, which makes page splits content-stable so that unchanged data regions produce byte-identical pages across rewrites (deduplication-friendly for content-addressed storage):

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.content_defined_chunking.enabled = true;
-- tuning knobs (defaults shown):
--   content_defined_chunking.min_chunk_size = 262144   (256 KiB)
--   content_defined_chunking.max_chunk_size = 1048576  (1 MiB)
--   content_defined_chunking.norm_level = 0            (recommended range [-3, 3])
```

Caveats: CDC is **experimental and disabled by default**, and enabling it **disables parallel Parquet writing** — the writer falls back to serial page production. Do not enable it on hot write paths without benchmarking; it maps to `WriterProperties::content_defined_chunking` in parquet-rs.

### Encryption property conversions are now fallible

The conversions between config-level and parquet-rs encryption properties became `TryFrom`/`TryInto` in 54 (they were infallible `From` in 53): `FileEncryptionProperties::try_from(config_props)?` and `FileDecryptionProperties::try_from(config_props)?` return `Result`, surfacing invalid key/footer configurations as errors at conversion time. Code that used `.into()` must switch to `.try_into()?` and handle the error.

Agent rules:

```text
Use nested field access directly; leaf projection/pushdown is automatic in 54.
Keep Parquet statistics enabled; proven-true skipping depends on them.
Set coerce_int96_tz='UTC' for Spark-written INT96 files needing tz-aware timestamps.
Treat content_defined_chunking as experimental; it disables parallel writes.
Replace .into() with .try_into()? for Parquet encryption property conversions.
```

# DataFusion Advanced — 16) Object stores and remote locations

Style target follows the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

## 16.0 Remote-source mental model

```text
SQL / DataFrame path
  → LOCATION / path / URL
  → ObjectStoreRegistry lookup by URL prefix
  → ObjectStore implementation
      file://
      https://
      s3://
      gs://
      oss://
      cos://
      custom://
  → ListingTable / file source
  → schema inference / listing / partition discovery / scan
  → Arrow RecordBatch stream
```

DataFusion’s built-in `ListingTable` reads Parquet, JSON, CSV, or Avro files from one or more local or remote directories, supports Hive-style partitioning, optional compression, directly reading from remote object stores, file metadata caching, and related listing behavior. DataFusion’s `RuntimeEnv` owns an `ObjectStoreRegistry`, which maps URLs to object-store instances used during query execution. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 16.1 Location surfaces

| Surface                 | Syntax / API                                                             | Use                               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| direct path SQL         | `SELECT * FROM 's3://bucket/path/'`                                      | trusted CLI/ad hoc                |
| external table SQL      | `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE t STORED AS PARQUET LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/'` | named SQL table                   |
| Rust direct read        | `ctx.read_parquet("s3://bucket/path/", ...)`                             | Rust DataFrame path               |
| Rust table registration | `ctx.register_parquet("t", "s3://bucket/path/", ...)`                    | named table for SQL/DataFrame     |
| object-store registry   | `ctx.register_object_store(url, store)`                                  | custom stores/credentials         |
| listing table           | `ctx.register_listing_table(...)`                                        | advanced multi-file/table control |

DataFusion CLI docs show local/remote files queried directly in single quotes, including local CSV files, local directories, remote HTTPS Parquet files, and S3/GCS-style paths; embedded Rust direct path SQL requires explicitly enabling URL-table access, which DataFusion marks as security-sensitive because it permits SQL to access local files directly. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 16.2 `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` location syntax

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE table_name
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'scheme://bucket_or_host/path/';
```

Supported location classes documented by DataFusion CLI include local paths, HTTP(S), S3 (`s3://`), GCS (`gs://`), OSS (`oss://`), and COS (`cos://`) through `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` and/or direct quoted path access. The SQL DDL reference states that `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` registers a local filesystem or remote object-store location as a named table and accepts `CSV`, `ARROW`, `PARQUET`, `AVRO`, and `JSON` file types. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE hits
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'https://datasets.example.org/hits_1.parquet';

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE facts
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/facts/';

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE events
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/events/';
```

---

## 16.3 HTTP(S)

### Direct SQL path

```sql
SELECT count(*)
FROM 'https://datasets.example.org/path/file.parquet';
```

### External table

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE hits
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'https://datasets.example.org/path/file.parquet';

SELECT count(*)
FROM hits;
```

DataFusion CLI docs show reading a remote Parquet file via HTTP(S) both directly and as an external table. HTTP(S) is best for public static datasets or controlled endpoints; use explicit object-store registration for authenticated/custom HTTP stores in embedded applications. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
HTTP(S):
  good for public immutable files
  weak for directory-style listing unless the object store supports it
  avoid for private data unless auth layer is explicitly handled
  prefer external table registration for repeated queries
```

---

## 16.4 S3

### Explicit credentials in SQL

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'aws.access_key_id' '******',
  'aws.secret_access_key' '******',
  'aws.region' 'us-east-2'
)
LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

### Environment credentials

```bash
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-2
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=******
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=******
```

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

DataFusion CLI supports S3 through `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` options and standard AWS configuration methods via the AWS config crate. The documented S3 credential precedence is: explicit `OPTIONS`, then standard AWS configuration/environment mechanisms, then unsigned requests if no credentials are specified. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Unsigned public S3 bucket

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE nyc_taxi_rides
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://altinity-clickhouse-data/nyc_taxi_rides/data/tripdata_parquet/'
OPTIONS ('aws.skip_signature' 'true');
```

DataFusion documents `aws.SKIP_SIGNATURE true` / `aws.skip_signature` for unsigned public S3 reads; `aws.nosign` is an alias for `skip_signature`, and `AWS_SKIP_SIGNATURE` is the corresponding environment variable. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### S3 option / environment map

| Environment variable                     | SQL option              | Meaning                  |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`                      | `aws.access_key_id`     | access key               |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`                  | `aws.secret_access_key` | secret key               |
| `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`                     | `aws.region`            | region                   |
| `AWS_ENDPOINT`                           | `aws.endpoint`          | custom endpoint          |
| `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`                      | `aws.token`             | session token            |
| `AWS_SKIP_SIGNATURE`                     | `aws.skip_signature`    | unsigned requests        |
| `AWS_ALLOW_HTTP`                         | none listed             | permit non-TLS HTTP      |
| `AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI` | none listed             | ECS IAM role credentials |

This mapping is documented in the DataFusion CLI data-source guide. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Programmatic S3 object store registration

```toml
[dependencies]
datafusion = "54.1.0"
object_store = { version = "0.13", features = ["aws"] }
url = "2"
```

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::prelude::*;
use object_store::aws::AmazonS3Builder;
use url::Url;

fn register_s3(ctx: &SessionContext) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let s3 = AmazonS3Builder::new()
        .with_region("us-east-2")
        .with_bucket_name("my-bucket")
        .with_access_key_id("...")
        .with_secret_access_key("...")
        .build()
        .map_err(|e| datafusion::error::DataFusionError::External(Box::new(e)))?;

    ctx.register_object_store(
        &Url::parse("s3://my-bucket")?,
        Arc::new(s3),
    );

    Ok(())
}
```

`AmazonS3Builder` is available on the `object_store` crate’s `aws` feature and configures an S3 connection with region, bucket, and credentials. `SessionContext::register_object_store` registers an `ObjectStore` for a URL prefix so DataFusion can resolve matching locations. ([Docs.rs][5])

---

## 16.5 GCS

### SQL credentials via service account path

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'gcp.service_account_path' '/tmp/gcs.json'
)
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

### Environment variable

```bash
export GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT=/tmp/gcs.json
```

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

DataFusion CLI docs state that Google Cloud Storage data sources require configured connection credentials, show `gcp.service_account_path` in `OPTIONS`, and document `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` as an environment-variable path for credentials. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

Agent rules:

```text
GCS:
  use gs://bucket/path/
  prefer service account environment / runtime registration in services
  avoid embedding service-account paths in public SQL logs
  use directory roots for datasets
  validate Hive partition discovery on gs:// paths
```

---

## 16.6 OSS — Alibaba Cloud Object Storage Service

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'aws.access_key_id' '******',
  'aws.secret_access_key' '******',
  'aws.oss.endpoint' 'https://bucket.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com'
)
LOCATION 'oss://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

DataFusion CLI docs document Alibaba OSS support with `oss://` locations and require connection credentials; supported `OPTIONS` are access key ID, secret access key, and endpoint, with the OSS endpoint format `https://{bucket}.{oss-region-endpoint}`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
OSS:
  location scheme: oss://bucket/path
  endpoint option: aws.oss.endpoint
  endpoint includes bucket prefix
  treat credentials as S3-compatible options
  isolate tenants by endpoint/bucket/credential policy
```

---

## 16.7 COS — Tencent Cloud Object Storage

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'aws.access_key_id' '******',
  'aws.secret_access_key' '******',
  'aws.cos.endpoint' 'https://cos.ap-singapore.myqcloud.com'
)
LOCATION 'cos://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

DataFusion CLI docs document Tencent COS support with `cos://` locations and require credentials; supported `OPTIONS` are access key ID, secret access key, and endpoint, with endpoint format `https://cos.{cos-region-endpoint}`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
COS:
  location scheme: cos://bucket/path
  endpoint option: aws.cos.endpoint
  endpoint does not include bucket prefix in the same style as OSS
  treat credentials as S3-compatible options
  verify endpoint format under pinned DataFusion/object_store version
```

---

## 16.8 Object store registry

### Runtime-level object-store registry

```text
RuntimeEnv
  memory_pool
  disk_manager
  cache_manager
  object_store_registry
```

`RuntimeEnv` manages execution resources, including memory, disk, cache, and `ObjectStoreRegistry`; the registry maps URLs to object-store instances. ([Docs.rs][6])

### Register object store with `SessionContext`

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::object_store::local::LocalFileSystem;
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use url::Url;

let ctx = SessionContext::new();

ctx.register_object_store(
    &Url::parse("file://")?,
    Arc::new(LocalFileSystem::new()),
);
```

`SessionContext::register_object_store(url, object_store)` registers an `ObjectStore` for a URL prefix; the docs show registering `LocalFileSystem` for the `file://` prefix. ([Docs.rs][7])

### Register object store with `RuntimeEnv`

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::execution::runtime_env::RuntimeEnv;
use datafusion::object_store::local::LocalFileSystem;
use url::Url;

let runtime_env = RuntimeEnv::default();

runtime_env.register_object_store(
    &Url::try_from("file://")?,
    Arc::new(LocalFileSystem::new()),
);
```

`RuntimeEnv::register_object_store` registers a custom store for a URL; the docs explicitly mention using this for schemes without built-in support, such as `hdfs://namenode:port/...`, and the method returns any previously registered store for that scheme/prefix. ([Docs.rs][6])

### Runtime builder customization

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::execution::runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_object_store_registry(my_registry)
    .build_arc()?;

let state = SessionStateBuilder::new()
    .with_runtime_env(runtime)
    .with_default_features()
    .build();

let ctx = SessionContext::from(state);
```

`RuntimeEnvBuilder::with_object_store_registry` customizes the registry used to get object stores by URL, which is the correct boundary for application-wide remote-storage policy. ([Docs.rs][8])

---

## 16.9 Directory paths over wildcards

### Do not generate

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/*.parquet';
```

### Generate

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/my_table/';
```

DataFusion CLI docs state that wildcards such as `*.parquet` or recursive wildcard patterns are not supported because wildcard semantics are not universal across storage backends such as S3 and GCS; instead, specify a directory path and DataFusion reads all compatible files in that directory. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
Remote dataset path:
  use directory root
  end directory paths with /
  ensure all files under root are compatible
  avoid glob/wildcard assumptions
  use Hive partition directories for pruning/filtering
```

---

## 16.10 Remote partition discovery

### Object paths

```text
gs://bucket/my_table/a=1/b=100/file1.parquet
gs://bucket/my_table/a=2/b=200/file2.parquet
```

### SQL

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE my_table
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/my_table/';

SELECT count(*)
FROM my_table
WHERE b = 200;
```

When a specified directory path has a Hive-compliant partition structure, DataFusion CLI automatically parses and incorporates the Hive columns and values into the table schema and data; the docs show `a=1/b=100` and `a=2/b=200` paths being queried with `WHERE b=200`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
Remote Hive partitioning:
  layout: col=value/col=value/file
  location points to table root
  partition columns become queryable fields
  filter partition columns for pruning
  keep partition cardinality bounded
  avoid schema conflicts between file columns and partition columns
```

---

## 16.11 Direct path SQL vs registered external table

| Mode                  | Example                                                     | Use                           | Risk                     |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| direct path           | `SELECT * FROM 's3://bucket/table/'`                        | trusted CLI/ad hoc            | ungoverned path exposure |
| external table        | `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE t ... LOCATION 's3://bucket/table/'` | stable SQL object             | DDL governance needed    |
| Rust registry         | `ctx.register_parquet("t", "s3://bucket/table/", ...)`      | application-controlled source | code-managed lifecycle   |
| object-store registry | `ctx.register_object_store(&url, store)`                    | custom credentials/stores     | operational complexity   |

DataFusion CLI docs support direct remote location queries without table registration, while the DDL docs support registering remote locations as external tables. In embedded contexts, direct URL-table access should be enabled only when intentionally allowing SQL path access. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 16.12 Credential policy

### SQL `OPTIONS` credentials

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'aws.access_key_id' '******',
  'aws.secret_access_key' '******',
  'aws.region' 'us-east-2'
)
LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

### Environment credentials

```bash
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-2
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=******
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=******
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=******
```

### Runtime / registry credentials

```rust
// Build provider-specific ObjectStore in code.
// Register store for a URL prefix.
// Keep credentials in app config / secret manager, not SQL text.
ctx.register_object_store(&url, store);
```

DataFusion docs allow credentials in SQL `OPTIONS`, but they also document environment-based credentials and standard SDK/provider resolution; because SQL strings are often logged or visible to users, production services should prefer environment/secret-manager/object-store registry configuration over inline credentials. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Credential precedence for S3 in the CLI is documented as explicit `OPTIONS`, then AWS config/environment mechanisms, then unsigned requests when no credentials are specified. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 16.13 Unsigned public buckets

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE public_dataset
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://public-bucket/path/'
OPTIONS ('aws.skip_signature' 'true');
```

DataFusion documents unsigned S3 access using `aws.SKIP_SIGNATURE true`; it also states that if no credentials are specified, the CLI uses unsigned S3 requests, enabling reads from public buckets. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
Unsigned reads:
  good for public datasets
  do not use for private buckets
  prefer explicit skip_signature=true when public-read behavior is intentional
  audit that paths are expected public sources
```

---

## 16.14 Remote object-store performance levers

### Listing and metadata caches

`RuntimeEnvBuilder` exposes object listing and metadata cache controls such as `with_metadata_cache_limit`, `with_object_list_cache_limit`, and `with_object_list_cache_ttl`, and `RuntimeEnv` includes a `cache_manager` for temporary cache data during a session. These are important for remote datasets where listing and footer metadata requests dominate query latency. ([Docs.rs][8])

```rust
use std::time::Duration;
use datafusion::execution::runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder;

let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_metadata_cache_limit(512 * 1024 * 1024)
    .with_object_list_cache_limit(128 * 1024 * 1024)
    .with_object_list_cache_ttl(Duration::from_secs(300))
    .build_arc()?;
```

Agent rules:

```text
Remote lake datasets:
  cache listings when table roots are stable
  cache metadata when Parquet files are reused
  invalidate/shorten TTL for frequently mutating prefixes
  avoid many tiny files
  prefer partition filters to reduce listing/scan breadth
```

---

## 16.15 Remote layout patterns

### Good

```text
s3://lake/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=us/part-000.parquet
s3://lake/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=eu/part-001.parquet
```

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE events
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://lake/events/';

SELECT count(*)
FROM events
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22'
  AND region = 'us';
```

### Bad

```text
s3://lake/events/*.parquet
s3://lake/events/user_id=<millions-of-values>/...
s3://lake/events/mixed_schema_files/
s3://lake/events/raw_json_blobs_only/
```

DataFusion’s remote path guidance favors directory roots over wildcards and automatically discovers Hive-style partitions in directory names; the Parquet directory rule also requires compatible schemas across files under the folder. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 16.16 Security posture by deployment

| Deployment              | Recommended remote-source policy                                                      |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| local CLI               | allow direct quoted paths; credentials through env                                    |
| internal batch job      | direct `read_parquet` / registered tables; credentials through runtime/env            |
| public SQL endpoint     | no direct path SQL; no DDL; registered tables only                                    |
| tenant-isolated service | separate `SessionContext` / `RuntimeEnv` / registry per tenant or credential boundary |
| governed lakehouse      | custom catalog + object-store registry + path allowlist                               |
| diagnostics CLI         | allow cache/metadata inspection; never expose secrets                                 |

DataFusion’s `enable_url_table` is explicitly security-sensitive because it allows SQL such as `SELECT * FROM 'my_file.parquet'` to access local files; the same principle applies to remote paths in untrusted SQL surfaces. ([Docs.rs][7])

---

## 16.17 Rust end-to-end: registered S3 table with read-only SQL

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

pub async fn query_registered_remote_table(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    ctx.register_parquet(
        "events",
        "s3://bucket/events/",
        ParquetReadOptions::default(),
    )
    .await?;

    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(false)
        .with_allow_dml(false)
        .with_allow_statements(false);

    let df = ctx
        .sql_with_options(
            "SELECT event_date, count(*) AS n
             FROM events
             WHERE event_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
             GROUP BY event_date
             ORDER BY event_date",
            options,
        )
        .await?;

    df.show().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

`register_parquet` registers a Parquet source as a named table, while `SQLOptions` can disable DDL, DML, and statement/config SQL when accepting query text from users. ([Docs.rs][7])

---

## 16.18 Rust end-to-end: custom scheme registration

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::execution::{
    runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder,
    session_state::SessionStateBuilder,
};
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use url::Url;

fn context_with_custom_store(
    scheme_url: Url,
    store: Arc<dyn datafusion::object_store::ObjectStore>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new().build_arc()?;
    runtime.register_object_store(&scheme_url, store);

    let state = SessionStateBuilder::new()
        .with_runtime_env(runtime)
        .with_default_features()
        .build();

    Ok(SessionContext::from(state))
}
```

`RuntimeEnv::register_object_store` is designed for custom URL-backed stores, including schemes without built-in support, and `RuntimeEnvBuilder` lets applications supply an object-store registry as part of the execution environment. ([Docs.rs][6])

---

## 16.19 Object-store option matrix

| Store   | URI scheme            | SQL credential/config options                                                                                 | Env vars                                                                                                                            |
| ------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| HTTP(S) | `http://`, `https://` | URL itself; custom auth requires custom store/HTTP config                                                     | app-dependent                                                                                                                       |
| S3      | `s3://`               | `aws.access_key_id`, `aws.secret_access_key`, `aws.region`, `aws.endpoint`, `aws.token`, `aws.skip_signature` | `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, `AWS_ENDPOINT`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`, `AWS_SKIP_SIGNATURE`, etc. |
| GCS     | `gs://`               | `gcp.service_account_path`                                                                                    | `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`                                                                                                            |
| OSS     | `oss://`              | `aws.access_key_id`, `aws.secret_access_key`, `aws.oss.endpoint`                                              | use configured app/env equivalents                                                                                                  |
| COS     | `cos://`              | `aws.access_key_id`, `aws.secret_access_key`, `aws.cos.endpoint`                                              | use configured app/env equivalents                                                                                                  |

The S3, GCS, OSS, and COS option names above are documented in the DataFusion CLI data-source guide. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 16.20 Best-practice deployment advisory

```text
Path governance:
  register known tables
  avoid arbitrary LOCATION from users
  avoid enable_url_table in services
  use catalog allowlists
  constrain object-store prefixes

Credentials:
  prefer env/secret manager/runtime registry
  avoid SQL OPTIONS secrets in logs
  isolate per-tenant credentials
  rotate keys outside SQL

Layout:
  use directory roots
  avoid wildcards
  use Hive partitions for common filters
  keep schemas compatible
  avoid tiny files
  avoid high-cardinality partitions

Performance:
  cache listings/metadata for stable prefixes
  tune cache TTL for mutating datasets
  use Parquet statistics/pruning
  filter partition columns
  project only needed columns

Safety:
  disable DDL/DML/statements for read-only SQL
  redact remote locations if they leak tenant/bucket names
  treat public unsigned buckets as explicit policy, not fallback surprise
```

---

## 16.21 Anti-pattern inventory

* Enabling `enable_url_table()` in a public SQL service.
* Accepting arbitrary `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... LOCATION ...` from users.
* Logging SQL that includes access keys or service-account paths.
* Using `gs://bucket/*.parquet` or `s3://bucket/**/*.parquet`.
* Registering directory datasets without trailing `/`.
* Mixing incompatible schemas in one table directory.
* Partitioning by high-cardinality IDs.
* Assuming unsigned S3 access is safe for private data.
* Using inline credentials instead of object-store registry/secret manager.
* Sharing one object-store registry across tenants with different credentials.
* Relying on HTTP(S) URLs for private authenticated data without explicit auth handling.
* Treating S3, GCS, OSS, and COS endpoint formats as interchangeable.
* Leaving listing-cache TTL high for rapidly changing prefixes.
* Forgetting that partition discovery derives values from path strings.

---

## 16.22 Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Choose access mode: direct path / CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE / register_* / custom ObjectStore.
[ ] Avoid direct path SQL for untrusted users.
[ ] Use LOCATION 'scheme://bucket/path/' for remote external tables.
[ ] Use directory roots, not wildcards.
[ ] Ensure directory paths end with `/` when intended as directories.
[ ] Use Hive-style partitions: col=value/col=value/file.
[ ] Verify partition columns appear and filter correctly.
[ ] For S3, choose explicit OPTIONS, env/AWS config, or unsigned policy.
[ ] For public S3, set aws.skip_signature intentionally.
[ ] For GCS, configure gcp.service_account_path or GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT.
[ ] For OSS, use oss:// and aws.oss.endpoint with bucket-qualified endpoint.
[ ] For COS, use cos:// and aws.cos.endpoint with COS endpoint format.
[ ] Register custom object stores through SessionContext or RuntimeEnv.
[ ] Put credentials in runtime/env/secret manager when possible.
[ ] Configure object-list / metadata caches for stable remote datasets.
[ ] Disable DDL/DML/statements when remote paths are not user-governed.
```

# DataFusion Advanced — 17) Catalogs, schemas, and tables

Style target follows the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

## 17.0 Mental model: metadata hierarchy

```text id="u4km6i"
CatalogProviderList
  └─ CatalogProvider               -- catalog / database-like namespace
      └─ SchemaProvider            -- schema namespace
          └─ TableProvider         -- queryable table / view / external source / memory source
              └─ scan(...) -> ExecutionPlan -> RecordBatch stream
```

DataFusion’s catalog hierarchy is explicit: a `CatalogProviderList` contains `CatalogProvider`s, each `CatalogProvider` contains `SchemaProvider`s, and each `SchemaProvider` contains `TableProvider`s. DataFusion ships basic in-memory catalog functionality, but custom catalog implementations are expected for systems backed by local files, remote object storage, metastores, lakehouse catalogs, or governed product metadata. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 17.1 Value case

| Problem                      | Catalog-layer value                                                                            |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SQL name resolution          | maps `catalog.schema.table` / `schema.table` / `table` to a `TableProvider`                    |
| metadata governance          | central table/schema existence, ownership, visibility, and schema control                      |
| multi-tenancy                | separate catalogs/schemas per tenant, workspace, org, or security domain                       |
| external storage integration | catalog entry points to Parquet/CSV/JSON/Avro/Arrow/object-store-backed tables                 |
| custom systems               | implement `CatalogProvider`, `SchemaProvider`, `TableProvider` for your database/lakehouse/API |
| DDL integration              | `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE SCHEMA`, `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`, `DROP TABLE`, views                  |
| introspection                | `SHOW TABLES`, `SHOW COLUMNS`, `information_schema.*`                                          |
| query planning               | optimizer/planner obtains table schemas, filters, statistics, constraints, scan plans          |

The `CatalogProvider` docs state that DataFusion needs catalog metadata to know which schemas/tables exist, their columns and data types, and how to access the data. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 17.2 Default catalog and schema

Default config keys:

```text id="co5kek"
datafusion.catalog.create_default_catalog_and_schema = true
datafusion.catalog.default_catalog = datafusion
datafusion.catalog.default_schema = public
datafusion.catalog.information_schema = false
```

The configuration reference documents these defaults: DataFusion automatically creates the default catalog/schema by default; unqualified SQL uses default catalog `datafusion` and default schema `public`; `information_schema` virtual tables are disabled unless enabled. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Configure defaults in Rust

```rust id="vqf1i7"
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .with_create_default_catalog_and_schema(true)
    .with_default_catalog_and_schema("prod", "analytics")
    .with_information_schema(true);

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);
```

### Configure defaults through low-level keys

```rust id="q6hoae"
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let mut config = SessionConfig::new();

config.set_bool("datafusion.catalog.create_default_catalog_and_schema", true)?;
config.set_str("datafusion.catalog.default_catalog", "prod")?;
config.set_str("datafusion.catalog.default_schema", "analytics")?;
config.set_bool("datafusion.catalog.information_schema", true)?;

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);
```

### SQL resolution examples

```sql id="gdb7w2"
-- resolves using default catalog + default schema
SELECT * FROM events;

-- explicit schema under default catalog
SELECT * FROM analytics.events;

-- explicit catalog + schema + table
SELECT * FROM prod.analytics.events;
```

Agent rules:

```text id="fdbm24"
Unqualified table name = default_catalog.default_schema.table.
Default names are config, not a universal database invariant.
Set defaults explicitly in services.
Use fully qualified names for generated SQL crossing tenant/schema boundaries.
```

## 17.3 Core traits and responsibilities

| Trait                 | Represents                 | Required / key operations                                          | Planning role                |
| --------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| `CatalogProviderList` | named catalog collection   | register catalog, list catalog names, get catalog                  | root lookup                  |
| `CatalogProvider`     | named schema collection    | list schemas, get schema, register/deregister schema               | catalog namespace            |
| `SchemaProvider`      | named table collection     | list tables, get table, table existence, register/deregister table | schema namespace             |
| `TableProvider`       | queryable/modifiable table | schema, table type, scan, filter pushdown, insert, statistics      | logical scan → physical plan |

The catalog guide describes the trait responsibilities: `CatalogProviderList` registers/gets/lists catalogs; `CatalogProvider` sets/gets/lists schemas; `SchemaProvider` sets/gets/lists/deregisters tables and checks table existence; `TableProvider` scans underlying data for use in DataFusion. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 17.4 `CatalogProviderList`

### Concept

```rust id="b21row"
pub trait CatalogProviderList: Debug + Sync + Send {
    fn register_catalog(
        &self,
        name: String,
        catalog: Arc<dyn CatalogProvider>,
    ) -> Option<Arc<dyn CatalogProvider>>;

    fn catalog_names(&self) -> Vec<String>;

    fn catalog(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Arc<dyn CatalogProvider>>;
}
```

`CatalogProviderList` represents a list of named `CatalogProvider`s; the docs.rs catalog module lists it as the root catalog collection trait. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Use cases

```text id="bqq6nv"
single app catalog list
multi-tenant catalog list
workspace catalog list
remote metastore snapshot
dynamic file catalog wrapper
```

### Agent rules

```text id="8lyxqu"
Implement CatalogProviderList only when you need to control catalog lookup globally.
Most apps can register catalogs on SessionContext instead.
Return deterministic catalog_names() for reproducible introspection.
Avoid network calls in catalog_names(); planning is latency-sensitive.
```

---

## 17.5 `CatalogProvider`

### Concept

```rust id="vg7vba"
pub trait CatalogProvider: Any + Debug + Sync + Send {
    fn schema_names(&self) -> Vec<String>;
    fn schema(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>>;

    fn register_schema(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        schema: Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>>> { ... }

    fn deregister_schema(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        cascade: bool,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>>> { ... }
}
```

`CatalogProvider` represents a catalog containing named schemas; DataFusion’s docs describe `CatalogProvider` as “sometimes called a database in other systems,” but in DataFusion it is metadata, not a storage engine by itself. In DataFusion 54, `Any` is a supertrait (the `fn as_any` boilerplate was removed); downcast via `catalog.downcast_ref::<MyCatalog>()`. ([Docs.rs][2])

### In-memory catalog

```rust id="j2jnx4"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::{CatalogProvider, MemoryCatalogProvider, MemorySchemaProvider};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let ctx = SessionContext::new();

let catalog = Arc::new(MemoryCatalogProvider::new());
catalog.register_schema(
    "analytics",
    Arc::new(MemorySchemaProvider::new()),
)?;

ctx.register_catalog("prod", catalog);
```

`MemoryCatalogProvider` is a simple in-memory catalog implementation; `new()` instantiates it with an empty collection of schemas. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Agent rules

```text id="jferao"
CatalogProvider = schema namespace, not table storage.
Use MemoryCatalogProvider for tests, session-local apps, examples.
Use custom CatalogProvider for durable/governed catalogs.
Implement deregister_schema only if schema deletion is product-supported.
```

---

## 17.6 `SchemaProvider`

### Concept

```rust id="55d5cb"
pub trait SchemaProvider: Any + Debug + Sync + Send {
    fn table_names(&self) -> Vec<String>;

    async fn table(
        &self,
        name: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>>;

    fn table_exist(&self, name: &str) -> bool;

    fn register_table(
        &self,
        name: String,
        table: Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>> { ... }

    fn deregister_table(
        &self,
        name: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>> { ... }
}
```

`SchemaProvider` represents a schema containing named tables. Its `table(name)` method is async and returns `Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>`; `table_exist` returns whether a table exists; `table_names` lists available tables. In DataFusion 54, `Any` is a supertrait (no `fn as_any` method to implement). ([Docs.rs][6])

### In-memory schema

```rust id="3jmkqu"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::{MemorySchemaProvider, SchemaProvider, TableProvider};

let schema = MemorySchemaProvider::new();

schema.register_table(
    "events".to_string(),
    table_provider as Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
)?;

assert!(schema.table_exist("events"));
```

The catalog guide describes `MemorySchemaProvider` as a simple `SchemaProvider` implementation storing tables in a `DashMap`, which is useful as a minimal in-memory schema implementation. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Agent rules

```text id="94ty6n"
SchemaProvider = table namespace.
Use table_exist for cheap existence checks.
Use table(name).await for provider retrieval.
Do not put expensive remote scans in table_names().
If remote table details require IO, batch/cache metadata before planning.
```

---

## 17.7 `TableProvider`

### Concept

```rust id="2q64wz"
pub trait TableProvider: Any + Debug + Sync + Send {
    fn schema(&self) -> Arc<Schema>;

    fn table_type(&self) -> TableType;

    async fn scan(
        &self,
        state: &dyn Session,
        projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>,
        filters: &[Expr],
        limit: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>;
}
```

`TableProvider` represents a queryable/modifiable table. Implementations provide the table schema, filter-pushdown capabilities, and a `scan` method that returns an `ExecutionPlan` capable of producing Arrow `RecordBatch`es. In DataFusion 54, `Any` is a supertrait — implementations no longer write `fn as_any`, and callers downcast with `provider.downcast_ref::<MyTable>()` via trait upcasting. ([Docs.rs][7])

### Built-in provider examples

```text id="wo8hqc"
MemTable             -- in-memory Vec<RecordBatch>
ListingTable         -- local/remote file datasets
ViewTable / view     -- logical-plan-backed view
StreamingTable       -- streaming partitioned dataset
TableFunction        -- table-valued function
```

The `datafusion::catalog` module lists `MemTable`, `MemoryCatalogProvider`, `MemoryCatalogProviderList`, `MemorySchemaProvider`, stream/streaming providers, view provider support, table functions, dynamic file catalog/schema providers, and listing schema provider support. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Agent rules

```text id="1q2xpe"
TableProvider is the main custom data-source boundary.
schema() must be stable and cheap.
scan() may build an execution plan with projection/filter/limit pushdown.
supports_filters_pushdown and statistics improve optimization.
insert_into implements DML/write behavior when supported.
```

## 17.8 `SessionContext` catalog APIs

`SessionContext` is the user-facing engine object that creates DataFrames, registers data sources as SQL tables, registers custom data sources, and executes SQL queries. ([Docs.rs][8])

### Register table

```rust id="q8j97k"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::TableProvider;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

fn register_table(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    provider: Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    ctx.register_table("events", provider)?;
    assert!(ctx.table_exist("events")?);
    Ok(())
}
```

### Deregister table

```rust id="2u7tzu"
let previous = ctx.deregister_table("events")?;
assert!(previous.is_some());
assert!(!ctx.table_exist("events")?);
```

### Retrieve table as DataFrame

```rust id="a1imcn"
let df = ctx.table("events").await?;
df.show().await?;
```

### Retrieve provider

```rust id="cs4dkb"
let provider = ctx.table_provider("events").await?;
let schema = provider.schema();
```

### Register catalog

```rust id="g9up8j"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::{CatalogProvider, MemoryCatalogProvider};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let catalog: Arc<dyn CatalogProvider> = Arc::new(MemoryCatalogProvider::new());
ctx.register_catalog("prod", catalog);
```

Agent rules:

```text id="kyhfal"
Use ctx.register_table for custom providers.
Use ctx.register_csv/parquet/json/avro/arrow for built-in file providers.
Use ctx.table for DataFrame access to registered sources.
Use ctx.sql for SQL access.
Use table_exist in idempotent registration/migration code.
```

## 17.9 In-memory catalog stack

### Build complete in-memory catalog hierarchy

```rust id="qilczb"
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::catalog::{
    CatalogProvider,
    MemoryCatalogProvider,
    MemorySchemaProvider,
    SchemaProvider,
};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

fn context_with_memory_catalog() -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let catalog = Arc::new(MemoryCatalogProvider::new());
    let schema = Arc::new(MemorySchemaProvider::new());

    catalog.register_schema("analytics", schema)?;
    ctx.register_catalog("prod", catalog);

    Ok(ctx)
}
```

### Add table into schema before registration

```rust id="lb7vw3"
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::catalog::{MemorySchemaProvider, SchemaProvider, TableProvider};

let schema = Arc::new(MemorySchemaProvider::new());

schema.register_table(
    "events".to_string(),
    events_provider as Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
)?;
```

### Value case

```text id="fmr8mp"
tests
unit fixtures
session-local scratch schemas
temporary in-memory query apps
embedded demos
migration harnesses
catalog-trait prototyping
```

### Limits

```text id="nvcj59"
no persistence across process/session lifecycle
no durable transactions
no external authorization
no remote metastore sync
no built-in multi-node metadata coherence
```

DataFusion docs state that `MemoryCatalogProvider` is used by default, has no persistence, and DataFusion does not include a complex general-purpose catalog implementation because catalog management is a key design choice for most data systems. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Remote catalog caveat

DataFusion’s planning APIs are not async, so network IO cannot be performed lazily for all catalog lookups during planning; the docs recommend providing an in-memory snapshot of required remote metadata, typically via caching or batched remote access, while noting that `SchemaProvider::table` is async to simplify cases where table details require non-trivial access. ([Docs.rs][2])

```text id="bspzt5"

  prefetch or cache schema/table names
  keep schema_names() and table_names() cheap
  batch remote metadata calls
  use async table(name) for table-detail resolution

```

## 17.11 Custom schema implementation

### Skeleton

```rust id="zgsdl0"
use std::any::Any;
use std::sync::Arc;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use dashmap::DashMap;
use datafusion::catalog::{SchemaProvider, TableProvider};
use datafusion::error::Result;

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct MySchema {
    tables: DashMap<String, Arc<dyn TableProvider>>,
}

#[async_trait]
impl SchemaProvider for MySchema {
    // DataFusion 54: no `fn as_any` — `Any` is a supertrait of SchemaProvider.

    fn table_names(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut names: Vec<_> = self.tables
            .iter()
            .map(|entry| entry.key().clone())
            .collect();
        names.sort();
        names
    }

    async fn table(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>> {
        Ok(self.tables.get(name).map(|entry| entry.value().clone()))
    }

    fn table_exist(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.tables.contains_key(name)
    }

    fn register_table(
        &self,
        name: String,
        table: Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>> {
        Ok(self.tables.insert(name, table))
    }

    fn deregister_table(
        &self,
        name: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>> {
        Ok(self.tables.remove(name).map(|(_, table)| table))
    }
}
```

The catalog guide’s example `MemorySchemaProvider` uses a `DashMap<String, Arc<dyn TableProvider>>` as the backing table store, matching the `SchemaProvider` trait’s table registration/listing/lookup responsibilities. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Agent rules

```text id="9vzuj1"
Return sorted table_names() for stable introspection.
Use Arc<dyn TableProvider> for provider sharing.
Make table_exist cheap.
Make register/deregister semantics explicit: replace? reject? audit?
Enforce ownership/authorization outside raw SchemaProvider unless provider includes policy.
```

---

## 17.12 Table existence and idempotent registration

### Pattern

```rust id="h01x1m"
async fn ensure_table(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    name: &str,
    provider: Arc<dyn datafusion::catalog::TableProvider>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    if ctx.table_exist(name)? {
        return Ok(());
    }

    ctx.register_table(name, provider)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Replace pattern

```rust id="tv26vs"
fn replace_table(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    name: &str,
    provider: Arc<dyn datafusion::catalog::TableProvider>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let _old = ctx.deregister_table(name)?;
    ctx.register_table(name, provider)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Safer replace with audit

```rust id="7937ae"
fn replace_table_with_audit(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    name: &str,
    provider: Arc<dyn datafusion::catalog::TableProvider>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let existed = ctx.table_exist(name)?;

    if existed {
        let previous = ctx.deregister_table(name)?;
        tracing::info!(table = name, had_previous = previous.is_some(), "replacing table");
    }

    ctx.register_table(name, provider)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

Agent rules:

```text id="boiofp"
Use IF NOT EXISTS in SQL DDL when appropriate.
Use table_exist before idempotent Rust registration.
Use deregister_table + register_table only when replacement is intentional.
Log/audit table replacement in service code.
```

---

## 17.13 DDL integration

DataFusion supports DDL using the catalog API: `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE SCHEMA`, `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`, views, and related catalog-affecting statements register catalog/schema/table/view metadata through provider traits. The catalog guide explicitly connects DDL support to the catalog API. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### SQL DDL examples

```sql id="2sv176"
CREATE DATABASE prod;

CREATE SCHEMA prod.analytics;

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE prod.analytics.events
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/events/';

CREATE VIEW prod.analytics.active_events AS
SELECT *
FROM prod.analytics.events
WHERE active = true;

DROP TABLE prod.analytics.events;
```

### Read-only SQL safety

```rust id="tfgw63"
let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);

let df = ctx.sql_with_options(user_sql, options).await?;
```

Agent rules:

```text id="nm7rzt"
DDL mutates catalog metadata.
Disable DDL for public/read-only SQL.
Custom catalogs must decide whether CREATE/DROP are supported.
DROP TABLE removes catalog binding; it does not necessarily delete remote data.
```

## 17.14 `information_schema`

### Enable

```rust id="2b11iv"
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .with_information_schema(true);

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);
```

or:

```rust id="eob9o3"
let mut config = SessionConfig::new();
config.set_bool("datafusion.catalog.information_schema", true)?;

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);
```

`datafusion.catalog.information_schema` controls whether DataFusion exposes `information_schema` virtual tables; it defaults to `false`. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Show tables

```sql id="kghycr"
SHOW TABLES;

SELECT *
FROM information_schema.tables;
```

DataFusion supports metadata introspection through ISO SQL `information_schema` views and DataFusion-specific `SHOW TABLES` / `SHOW COLUMNS` commands. ([Apache DataFusion][9])

### Show columns

```sql id="dck59c"
SHOW COLUMNS FROM events;

SELECT
  table_catalog,
  table_schema,
  table_name,
  column_name,
  data_type,
  is_nullable
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name = 'events';
```

`SHOW COLUMNS` or `information_schema.columns` exposes table schema metadata including data type and nullability. ([Apache DataFusion][9])

### Show config

```sql id="n125zx"
SHOW ALL;

SELECT *
FROM information_schema.df_settings;
```

DataFusion documents `SHOW ALL` and `information_schema.df_settings` as ways to inspect current session configuration options. ([Apache DataFusion][9])

### Show functions

```sql id="ip0xb1"
SHOW FUNCTIONS LIKE '%date%';

SELECT *
FROM information_schema.routines
WHERE function_name LIKE '%date%';
```

DataFusion’s `SHOW FUNCTIONS` maps to `information_schema.routines` and `information_schema.parameters`, exposing function names, descriptions, parameters, and examples. ([Apache DataFusion][9])

### Agent rules

```text id="3h4te2"
Enable information_schema for debugging, admin tools, and self-service introspection.
Consider disabling/hiding it for strict multi-tenant or least-privilege SQL endpoints.
information_schema can reveal table names, columns, functions, and settings.
Use catalog-backed authorization if exposing metadata to users.
```

## 17.15 Governance patterns

### Pattern A — one catalog per tenant

```text id="5df9gk"
CatalogProviderList
  tenant_a -> CatalogProvider
  tenant_b -> CatalogProvider
  tenant_c -> CatalogProvider
```

Use when tenants require separate object-store credentials, table namespaces, metadata visibility, lifecycle, or billing.

### Pattern B — one schema per workspace

```text id="5sk7e6"
datafusion catalog
  workspace_alpha schema
  workspace_beta schema
  workspace_gamma schema
```

Use when catalog-level policy is shared but table namespaces differ.

### Pattern C — curated / raw / temp schemas

```text id="o31w55"
prod catalog
  raw
  staging
  curated
  temp
  information_schema
```

Use for lakehouse-style pipelines where schema namespace reflects data lifecycle.

### Pattern D — read-only registered tables only

```rust id="40qs8v"
let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);

let df = ctx.sql_with_options(user_sql, options).await?;
```

Use for public SQL endpoints: register allowed tables in a governed catalog, deny DDL/DML/config statements, optionally deny `information_schema` or filter it.

### Pattern E — catalog-backed path allowlist

```text id="6gh2zr"
User SQL:
  SELECT ... FROM curated.events

Blocked:
  SELECT ... FROM 's3://arbitrary/path'
  CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... LOCATION 's3://unknown/path'
```

Use `CatalogProvider`/`SchemaProvider` as the only authorized path-to-table mechanism; do not enable arbitrary URL tables for untrusted SQL.

---

## 17.16 Custom catalog + remote metadata pattern

```text id="m4ly3p"
Startup / refresh loop:
  remote metastore / object store / DB
    → fetch table list, schemas, stats, locations
    → build immutable/cached metadata snapshot
    → expose CatalogProvider / SchemaProvider over snapshot

Planning:
  DataFusion calls schema_names(), table_names(), table(name).await
    → cheap local lookup
    → returns TableProvider

Execution:
  TableProvider::scan(...)
    → uses RuntimeEnv / ObjectStoreRegistry / provider metadata
```

DataFusion docs warn that lazy network IO during planning is not viable because planning APIs are not broadly async; remote catalogs should provide cached/in-memory snapshots or batch remote calls, with `SchemaProvider::table` async available for cases where table-detail loading is needed. ([Docs.rs][2])

Agent rules:

```text id="nrrq8u"
Remote catalog:
  separate metadata refresh from query planning
  use immutable snapshots for consistency
  batch remote calls
  expose cache version / refresh timestamp
  decide stale-read policy
  fail closed on auth metadata errors
```

---

## 17.17 Catalog-backed security controls

| Control                  | Catalog-layer enforcement idea                                             |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| table allowlist          | only register allowed providers                                            |
| column masking           | expose view/table provider with masked schema/scan                         |
| row policy               | expose provider that injects filters or views per tenant                   |
| path sandbox             | external tables only through catalog, not direct URL SQL                   |
| function restrictions    | custom `SessionState` function registry + plan validation                  |
| DDL authorization        | allow `register_schema` / `register_table` only through trusted admin path |
| metadata redaction       | filter `information_schema` or disable it                                  |
| object-store credentials | per-tenant `RuntimeEnv` / object-store registry                            |

Agent rule:

```text id="iggl56"
DataFusion catalog traits are metadata APIs, not a complete authorization system.
Authorization must be built around or inside catalog/table-provider implementations.
```

---

## 17.18 Information-schema leakage advisory

`information_schema.tables`, `information_schema.columns`, `information_schema.df_settings`, and function metadata are useful for agents and users, but they expose schema, function, and configuration information. DataFusion explicitly supports these views/commands for metadata introspection. ([Apache DataFusion][9])

Public service policy:

```text id="loj11e"
Option 1:
  disable information_schema
  expose curated metadata API instead

Option 2:
  enable information_schema only in admin contexts

Option 3:
  implement catalog/view filtering so users see only authorized objects
```

Agent-generated SQL policy:

```text id="dp8v2s"
Do not auto-query information_schema in a tenant/user context unless permitted.
Prefer server-provided schema manifests for LLM agents.
```

---

## 17.20 Catalog-backed custom table registration

### Register provider directly in default schema

```rust id="nozzy0"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::TableProvider;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

fn register_default_schema_table(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    table_name: &str,
    provider: Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    ctx.register_table(table_name, provider)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Register provider in explicit catalog/schema

```rust id="j1x1eb"
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::catalog::{CatalogProvider, MemoryCatalogProvider, MemorySchemaProvider, SchemaProvider, TableProvider};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

fn register_qualified_table(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    catalog_name: &str,
    schema_name: &str,
    table_name: &str,
    provider: Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let catalog = Arc::new(MemoryCatalogProvider::new());
    let schema = Arc::new(MemorySchemaProvider::new());

    schema.register_table(table_name.to_string(), provider)?;
    catalog.register_schema(schema_name, schema)?;
    ctx.register_catalog(catalog_name, catalog);

    Ok(())
}
```

SQL access:

```sql id="5qdbt9"
SELECT *
FROM prod.analytics.events;
```

---

## 17.21 DDL and custom provider behavior

DDL statements are routed through catalog/schema/table provider APIs; custom catalogs decide how much mutation is supported. DataFusion’s catalog guide states that DDL queries use the catalog API, and `TableProvider` is where DML such as `INSERT INTO` becomes relevant. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

Design matrix:

| SQL                      | Required support                                   |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `CREATE DATABASE`        | catalog list / catalog creation policy             |
| `CREATE SCHEMA`          | `CatalogProvider::register_schema`                 |
| `DROP SCHEMA`-like API   | `CatalogProvider::deregister_schema` if supported  |
| `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`  | schema table registration + file/provider factory  |
| `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT` | schema table registration + memory/custom provider |
| `DROP TABLE`             | `SchemaProvider::deregister_table`                 |
| `INSERT INTO`            | `TableProvider::insert_into`                       |
| `SELECT`                 | `TableProvider::scan`                              |

Agent rules:

```text id="8ty22v"
If custom catalog is read-only, reject register/deregister methods clearly.
If custom catalog supports DDL, define persistence and concurrency semantics.
If custom table supports DML, implement insert_into and count result contract.
```

---

## 17.22 TableProvider governance hooks

`TableProvider` includes more than `schema` and `scan`; it can expose filter-pushdown support, statistics, constraints, table type, and DML behavior. DataFusion’s docs call out `schema`, `supports_filters_pushdown`, and `scan` as important planning information. ([Docs.rs][7])

Governance patterns:

```text id="lgja33"
schema():
  hide unauthorized columns
  rename / normalize fields
  expose only stable contract

scan():
  inject required tenant filters
  enforce projection allowlist
  reject unsupported filters/limits
  return custom ExecutionPlan with audit

supports_filters_pushdown():
  advertise pushdown accurately
  avoid claiming exact pushdown if provider will re-check incorrectly

statistics():
  expose row counts / column stats for optimizer
  avoid leaking sensitive distribution info if metadata is protected

insert_into():
  enforce write permissions
  implement append/overwrite semantics safely
```

---

## 17.23 Catalog testing matrix

```text id="lr5gfy"
[ ] default catalog/schema names are expected
[ ] fully qualified table resolution works
[ ] unqualified table resolution uses configured defaults
[ ] register_table makes table visible to ctx.table and SQL
[ ] deregister_table removes table from SQL resolution
[ ] table_exist matches table lookup
[ ] catalog_names/schema_names/table_names sorted or stable enough for snapshots
[ ] information_schema.tables lists expected objects when enabled
[ ] information_schema.columns lists expected schema
[ ] SHOW TABLES / SHOW COLUMNS match information_schema results
[ ] DDL CREATE TABLE / DROP TABLE mutates expected schema
[ ] DDL disabled through SQLOptions for read-only contexts
[ ] custom catalog denies/permits register_schema as designed
[ ] custom schema denies/permits register_table as designed
[ ] remote catalog cache refresh behavior is deterministic
```

---

## 17.24 Production deployment advisory

```text id="s9wq76"
Small CLI / script:
  default SessionContext catalog is sufficient
  MemoryCatalogProvider is acceptable

Batch ETL:
  explicit catalog/schema names
  register external tables programmatically or through trusted DDL
  enable information_schema for diagnostics if safe

SQL service:
  disable DDL/DML for user SQL
  register only governed tables
  avoid direct URL table access
  disable or filter information_schema
  use custom catalogs for tenant isolation

Lakehouse engine:
  implement custom CatalogProvider / SchemaProvider over metastore
  TableProvider per table format
  cached remote metadata snapshot
  object-store registry per credential domain

Multi-tenant SaaS:
  separate catalogs or schemas per tenant
  per-tenant SessionContext / RuntimeEnv if credentials differ
  metadata visibility controlled at catalog/schema layer
```

---

## 17.25 Anti-pattern inventory

* Treating default `MemoryCatalogProvider` as durable metadata.
* Sharing one default catalog across tenants with different table visibility.
* Enabling `information_schema` in a public endpoint without metadata-access policy.
* Performing remote network calls inside every `schema_names()` / `table_names()` call.
* Returning unstable order from `table_names()` and snapshot-testing it.
* Implementing `table_exist` inconsistently with `table(name).await`.
* Claiming filter pushdown support in `TableProvider` but not enforcing/validating it.
* Registering arbitrary user-provided external locations into a shared catalog.
* Using unqualified SQL table names in generated multi-catalog/multi-tenant SQL.
* Replacing tables without audit.
* Assuming `DROP TABLE` deletes external data.
* Assuming `CREATE DATABASE` creates a durable DBMS database.
* Implementing a custom catalog with no cache invalidation/refresh strategy.
* Letting `information_schema.df_settings` expose runtime configuration to untrusted users.
* Using catalog metadata as authorization without a security review.

---

```text id="lg0co3"
[ ] Understand hierarchy: CatalogProviderList → CatalogProvider → SchemaProvider → TableProvider.
[ ] Set default catalog/schema explicitly for services.
[ ] Use MemoryCatalogProvider only for in-memory/session-local metadata.
[ ] Use custom CatalogProvider/SchemaProvider for durable/governed metadata.
[ ] Keep catalog/schema name listing cheap and deterministic.
[ ] Use ctx.register_table for custom TableProvider in default schema.
[ ] Use ctx.register_catalog for explicit catalog namespace.
[ ] Use table_exist before idempotent registration.
[ ] Use deregister_table only when deletion/replacement is intentional.
[ ] Enable information_schema only where metadata visibility is allowed.
[ ] Use SHOW TABLES / SHOW COLUMNS for diagnostics.
[ ] Disable DDL/DML/statements with SQLOptions for read-only user SQL.
[ ] Implement/call TableProvider::scan for actual data access.
[ ] Implement TableProvider::insert_into only when write semantics are defined.
[ ] Build remote catalogs from cached metadata snapshots, not per-lookup RPCs.
[ ] Enforce tenant/table/column governance at catalog/provider boundaries.
```
