# DataFusion Advanced — 18) Custom `TableProvider`

Style target follows the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

## 18.0 Custom table provider mental model

```text id="vp8eul"
Catalog / SessionContext registration
  → Arc<dyn TableProvider>
      ├─ schema()                      -- logical table schema
      ├─ table_type()                  -- Base / View / Temporary / etc.
      ├─ supports_filters_pushdown()   -- predicate pushdown capability contract
      ├─ scan(...)                     -- planning-time: build ExecutionPlan
      ├─ statistics()                  -- table-level stats, if known
      ├─ constraints()                 -- table constraints, if supported
      └─ insert_into(...)              -- optional write path

scan(...)
  → Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>
      ├─ properties()                  -- partitioning / ordering / boundedness / emission
      ├─ children()
      ├─ with_new_children(...)
      └─ execute(partition, TaskContext)
            → SendableRecordBatchStream
                → poll()
                    → external API / DB / object store / generated data
                    → Arrow RecordBatch
```

DataFusion’s custom table provider guide identifies three collaborating layers: `TableProvider` describes the table and produces a physical plan, `ExecutionPlan` describes how to compute the result including partitioning and ordering, and `SendableRecordBatchStream` is the async stream that yields `RecordBatch` values one at a time during execution. The guide summarizes the call sequence: `TableProvider::scan()` is called once during planning, `ExecutionPlan::execute()` is called once per partition, and streams produce rows during execution. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 18.1 Value case: when a custom `TableProvider` is worth it

Use a custom provider when the data source is **not already best represented by built-in file readers, `MemTable`, `ListingTable`, or `StreamTable`**.

| Source shape                          | Prefer                                                             | Reason                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| already have `Vec<RecordBatch>`       | `MemTable`                                                         | no custom provider needed                                      |
| stream of batches                     | `StreamTable` / stream provider                                    | source already matches streaming model                         |
| SQL view / transformation             | `ViewTable` / logical plan                                         | no custom physical source                                      |
| standard Parquet/CSV/JSON/Avro files  | `ListingTable` / built-ins                                         | DataFusion already handles listing, partitioning, file pruning |
| custom file format                    | `ListingTable` + custom `FileFormat` / `FileSource` / `FileOpener` | reuse file-discovery and partition support                     |
| database/API/SaaS/index/custom source | `TableProvider + ExecutionPlan + stream`                           | complete source-specific pushdown/parallelism/auth/control     |

DataFusion’s guide explicitly recommends choosing the highest-level building block that fits: `MemTable` for in-memory batches, `StreamTable` for async streams, `ViewTable` for logical transformations, `ListingTable` plus file-format abstractions for file sources, and full `TableProvider + ExecutionPlan + stream` only when full control is needed. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 18.2 Trait import stance

Current released docs expose `TableProvider` through the DataFusion catalog/datasource surfaces; examples may use `datafusion::catalog::TableProvider`, while docs.rs pages are under `datafusion::datasource`. Use the path that compiles for your pinned version; keep all `datafusion-*` subcrates pinned to the same version if importing subcrate traits directly.

```rust id="qsm8uj"
// Common top-level imports in current examples/docs:
use datafusion::catalog::{Session, TableProvider};
use datafusion::datasource::TableType;

// Other core imports:
use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::{Schema, SchemaRef};
use datafusion::common::Result;
use datafusion::logical_expr::{Expr, TableProviderFilterPushDown};
use datafusion::physical_plan::ExecutionPlan;
```

The `TableProvider` docs describe the trait as a queryable/modifiable table source that provides Arrow `RecordBatch`es and communicates planning information such as schema, filter pushdown support, and a scan `ExecutionPlan`. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 18.3 Required `TableProvider` methods

### Minimal read-only provider shape

```rust id="adzn3m"
use std::{any::Any, sync::Arc};

use async_trait::async_trait;
use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::SchemaRef;
use datafusion::catalog::{Session, TableProvider};
use datafusion::common::Result;
use datafusion::datasource::TableType;
use datafusion::logical_expr::Expr;
use datafusion::physical_plan::ExecutionPlan;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MyTableProvider {
    schema: SchemaRef,
}

#[async_trait]
impl TableProvider for MyTableProvider {
    // DataFusion 54: no `fn as_any` — `Any` is a supertrait of TableProvider.

    fn schema(&self) -> SchemaRef {
        Arc::clone(&self.schema)
    }

    fn table_type(&self) -> TableType {
        TableType::Base
    }

    async fn scan(
        &self,
        state: &dyn Session,
        projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>,
        filters: &[Expr],
        limit: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        Ok(Arc::new(MyExecPlan::new(
            Arc::clone(&self.schema),
            projection.cloned(),
            filters.to_vec(),
            limit,
        )))
    }
}
```

`scan` creates an `ExecutionPlan` for scanning the table with optional projection, filter, and limit hints; the plan is responsible for scanning source partitions in a streaming, parallelized fashion. Projection indices refer to fields in `schema()`, and DataFusion passes projection information so sources can avoid reading unused columns. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 18.4 `schema()`: contract and constraints

### Purpose

```text id="d7yc0p"
schema() -> Arc<Schema>
  = authoritative logical output schema for this table
  = column order used by projection indices
  = source of field names/types/nullability for SQL/DataFrame planning
  = schema all produced RecordBatches must conform to, after projection
```

### Schema construction

```rust id="b9ctvk"
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::{DataType, Field, Schema, SchemaRef};

let schema: SchemaRef = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("id", DataType::Int64, false),
    Field::new("region", DataType::Utf8, true),
    Field::new("amount", DataType::Float64, true),
]));
```

### Projected schema helper pattern

```rust id="8nhtah"
use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::SchemaRef;
use datafusion::common::Result;

fn project_schema(schema: &SchemaRef, projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>) -> Result<SchemaRef> {
    match projection {
        Some(indices) => Ok(Arc::new(schema.project(indices)?)),
        None => Ok(Arc::clone(schema)),
    }
}
```

### Agent rules

```text id="8ld1j1"
schema() must be cheap and stable.
schema() must not call remote APIs on every planning pass.
schema field order defines projection index semantics.
Every RecordBatch returned by the stream must match the output schema exactly.
If projection is pushed down, the ExecutionPlan stream schema should be projected.
If provider exposes dynamic schema, cache/snapshot it before planning.
```

`RecordBatchStream` implementors must guarantee every `RecordBatch` returned by the stream has the same schema returned from the stream’s `schema()` method. ([Docs.rs][3])

---

## 18.5 `scan(...)`: planning-time boundary

### Contract

```rust id="xbo37g"
async fn scan(
    &self,
    state: &dyn Session,
    projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>,
    filters: &[Expr],
    limit: Option<usize>,
) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>;
```

`scan()` receives three key pushdown hints: `projection` for needed columns, `filters` for predicates the optimizer wants the provider to evaluate during scan, and `limit` for row-count caps. The custom provider guide stresses that `scan()` runs during planning, should return quickly, and should build metadata/plan objects—not perform I/O, network calls, or heavy computation. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Correct `scan` behavior

```text id="xfi3q0"
DO:
  clone config/metadata handles
  compute cheap partition selection from already-known metadata
  store projection/filter/limit in ExecutionPlan
  build PlanProperties
  return Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>

DO NOT:
  fetch remote data
  open long-lived network streams
  block on API calls
  decode records
  allocate huge buffers
  perform scan execution
```

The guide explains why heavy `scan()` work is harmful: it slows planning, runs single-threaded before execution parallelism, prevents optimizer reductions from helping, and bypasses DataFusion’s execution-time concurrency and memory management. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 18.6 `scan_with_args(...)`: structured scan arguments

`scan_with_args(state, ScanArgs)` is the structured newer scan variant. It returns `ScanResult` and can carry additional information such as ordering preferences that may not be available through the legacy scan method. Providers can override it when they need structured scan arguments beyond projection/filter/limit. ([Docs.rs][2])

```rust id="79u1uc"
async fn scan_with_args<'a>(
    &self,
    state: &dyn Session,
    args: ScanArgs<'a>,
) -> Result<ScanResult> {
    // optional advanced override; default delegates to scan(...)
    todo!()
}
```

Agent rules:

```text id="vc1czj"
Implement scan first.
Override scan_with_args only when structured args add required capability.
Keep scan_with_args lightweight for the same reason scan must be lightweight.
```

---

## 18.7 Projection pushdown

### Meaning

```text id="2hy4dn"
projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>
  None          => all columns requested
  Some(indices) => return only schema fields at these positions, in this order
```

DataFusion passes projection information to let table providers scan only columns actually used in the query, which can substantially improve performance for columnar or remote sources. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Implementation pattern

```rust id="41trp7"
#[derive(Debug)]
struct MyExecPlan {
    full_schema: SchemaRef,
    projected_schema: SchemaRef,
    projection: Option<Vec<usize>>,
}

impl MyExecPlan {
    fn new(
        full_schema: SchemaRef,
        projection: Option<Vec<usize>>,
    ) -> datafusion::common::Result<Self> {
        let projected_schema = match &projection {
            Some(p) => Arc::new(full_schema.project(p)?),
            None => Arc::clone(&full_schema),
        };

        Ok(Self {
            full_schema,
            projected_schema,
            projection,
        })
    }
}
```

### Remote API mapping

```text id="6bs78x"
projection indices:
  [0, 3, 4]

full schema:
  0 id
  1 region
  2 event_type
  3 amount
  4 event_ts

remote API selected fields:
  ["id", "amount", "event_ts"]
```

### Agent rules

```text id="praw9y"
Use projection to reduce remote SELECT columns, API fields, JSON keys, DB columns.
Maintain output column order exactly as projection order.
If filters require extra columns internally, do not expose them unless requested.
If remote API cannot project fields, still return projected RecordBatches to DataFusion.
Test projection permutations, empty projection if possible, and duplicate/invalid indices defensively.
```

---

## 18.8 Predicate pushdown

### Capability declaration

```rust id="mw3urb"
fn supports_filters_pushdown(
    &self,
    filters: &[&Expr],
) -> Result<Vec<TableProviderFilterPushDown>> {
    Ok(filters
        .iter()
        .map(|expr| {
            if Self::is_source_filterable(expr) {
                TableProviderFilterPushDown::Exact
            } else {
                TableProviderFilterPushDown::Unsupported
            }
        })
        .collect())
}
```

`supports_filters_pushdown` must return one element per input filter. Each result is `Exact`, `Inexact`, or `Unsupported`; by default, DataFusion assumes all filters are unsupported and does not pass them to `scan`. `Exact` means the source fully evaluates the predicate and no remaining `FilterExec` is needed for that predicate; `Inexact` means the source reduces data but DataFusion still applies a filter above the scan; `Unsupported` means DataFusion handles it entirely. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Practical classification

| Source ability                                             | Return        | Example                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| API can fully evaluate `region = 'us'` server-side         | `Exact`       | SQL DB predicate, indexed API filter         |
| source can skip partitions/files but not rows inside files | `Inexact`     | file stats, partition pruning, metadata skip |
| source cannot evaluate predicate better than DataFusion    | `Unsupported` | arbitrary regex on text, complex UDF         |

### Filter matching skeleton

```rust id="pvdht1"
use datafusion::logical_expr::{Expr, Operator, TableProviderFilterPushDown};

fn classify_filter(expr: &Expr) -> TableProviderFilterPushDown {
    match expr {
        Expr::BinaryExpr(binary)
            if binary.op == Operator::Eq && references_column(&binary.left, "region") =>
        {
            TableProviderFilterPushDown::Exact
        }

        Expr::Between(between)
            if between.expr.try_as_col().is_some_and(|c| c.name == "event_date") =>
        {
            TableProviderFilterPushDown::Inexact
        }

        _ => TableProviderFilterPushDown::Unsupported,
    }
}
```

### Agent rules

```text id="w0ugox"
Only claim Exact when no false rows can remain for that predicate.
Use Inexact for partition/file/stat pruning.
Use Unsupported when DataFusion's vectorized FilterExec is not worse.
Never push down a filter and silently change SQL null semantics.
Never claim Exact for approximate remote filters.
Return vector length exactly equal to filters.len().
```

The guide cautions that DataFusion’s in-memory `FilterExec` is optimized, so filter pushdown should be implemented only when the source can avoid I/O or work more effectively than DataFusion itself. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 18.9 Limit pushdown

`limit: Option<usize>` tells the provider a row cap the optimizer wants to push into the scan. If specified, the provider must produce **at least** this many rows but may produce more; if any inexact filters are pushed down, the limit cannot be pushed down because doing so can produce too few final rows after DataFusion applies the residual filter. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Implementation rule

```rust id="bi20dg"
let rows_to_fetch = match limit {
    Some(n) if no_inexact_filters => Some(n),
    _ => None,
};
```

### Agent rules

```text id="s5j388"
Limit pushdown is safe for exact filters or no filters.
Limit pushdown is unsafe with inexact filters unless provider compensates by over-fetching.
Remote APIs with page_size/limit should map this carefully.
Never use limit as a hard final-output guarantee inside provider.
DataFusion may still enforce final LIMIT above scan.
```

---

## 18.10 Statistics

### Trait method

```rust id="q82f91"
fn statistics(&self) -> Option<Statistics> {
    Some(self.statistics.clone())
}
```

The `TableProvider::statistics()` method returns table statistics when available; docs.rs notes it is not presently used in mainline DataFusion but can be used by downstream repositories with specialized optimizer rules, for example join reordering. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Useful statistics

```text id="66tpz1"
row count
total byte size
column null counts
column min/max
distinct count estimates
partition/file counts
remote source cardinality estimates
```

### Agent rules

```text id="v4aq9j"
Statistics should be cheap, cached, and conservative.
Unknown is better than wrong.
Stale high-level estimates are acceptable for planning if marked approximate.
Never expose sensitive distribution stats to untrusted metadata users without policy.
Use stats to support custom optimizer rules and join ordering.
```

---

## 18.11 Constraints

### Trait method

```rust id="xtobk9"
fn constraints(&self) -> Option<&Constraints> {
    Some(&self.constraints)
}
```

`constraints()` returns `None` when a table does not support constraints, and `Some(&Constraints::empty())` when the table supports constraints but has none. Constraints can describe table-level invariants useful for validation and optimization. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Constraint examples

```text id="6whnwe"
primary key / unique key
not-null columns
foreign-key-like relationship metadata
check-like constraints
provider-level guaranteed ordering or partitioning
```

### Agent rules

```text id="sxetjh"
Return None if constraints are unsupported or unknown.
Return empty constraints only when provider intentionally supports the concept.
Do not advertise constraints not enforced by the source.
Constraints are metadata contracts; stale/false constraints can break optimizations.
```

---

## 18.12 Table definition, logical plan, defaults

`TableProvider` also exposes optional metadata methods such as `get_table_definition()`, `get_logical_plan()`, and `get_column_default(column)`. Table definitions help introspection; logical plans are relevant for views; column defaults matter for inserts and DDL-like behavior. ([Docs.rs][2])

```rust id="0k46e7"
fn get_table_definition(&self) -> Option<&str> {
    self.create_sql.as_deref()
}

fn get_column_default(&self, column: &str) -> Option<&Expr> {
    self.defaults.get(column)
}
```

Agent rules:

```text id="55h84x"
Use get_table_definition for DDL/introspection fidelity.
Use get_logical_plan for view-like providers.
Use get_column_default only when insert/default semantics are supported.
```

---

## 18.13 Partitioning and `ExecutionPlan` properties

### Why properties matter

`ExecutionPlan` properties tell DataFusion about output partitioning, ordering, boundedness, and emission. The custom provider guide stresses that output partitioning determines parallelism, and output ordering lets the optimizer avoid unnecessary `SortExec` nodes when the source is naturally sorted. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### PlanProperties construction pattern

```rust id="b8t3ub"
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::physical_expr::EquivalenceProperties;
use datafusion::physical_plan::{
    execution_plan::{Boundedness, EmissionType},
    Partitioning, PlanProperties,
};

let properties = Arc::new(PlanProperties::new(
    EquivalenceProperties::new(Arc::clone(&schema)),
    Partitioning::UnknownPartitioning(num_partitions),
    EmissionType::Incremental,
    Boundedness::Bounded,
));
```

### Natural partitioning strategies

| Source             | Natural partition            |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| object-store files | file / object / row-group    |
| sharded DB         | shard                        |
| partitioned API    | region / tenant / date range |
| queue/stream       | topic partition              |
| indexed source     | key range                    |
| generated data     | partition id                 |

The guide recommends matching the provider’s partitioning to natural layout: files, shards, regions, or key ranges; `execute()` is called once per partition, and partitions become async tasks scheduled by the runtime. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Agent rules

```text id="mej3fe"
Do not report one partition if source can parallelize naturally.
Do not report many partitions if they all serialize through one locked resource.
Expose natural ordering only when guaranteed.
Incorrect ordering metadata can yield wrong results by removing needed sorts.
Incorrect partitioning metadata can cause wrong joins/aggregates.
```

---

## 18.14 Custom `ExecutionPlan`

### Required conceptual methods

```rust id="0mhk1f"
impl ExecutionPlan for MyExecPlan {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "MyExecPlan" }

    fn properties(&self) -> &Arc<PlanProperties> {
        &self.properties
    }

    fn children(&self) -> Vec<&Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        vec![]
    }

    fn with_new_children(
        self: Arc<Self>,
        children: Vec<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        assert!(children.is_empty());
        Ok(self)
    }

    fn execute(
        &self,
        partition: usize,
        context: Arc<TaskContext>,
    ) -> Result<SendableRecordBatchStream> {
        // construct and return stream; do not fetch data here
        todo!()
    }
}
```

`ExecutionPlan` nodes represent physical-plan operators. `execute(partition, context)` returns an async `SendableRecordBatchStream` that incrementally computes a partition of the output. Methods such as `properties()` communicate optimizer-relevant output properties, and `children()` / `with_new_children()` allow physical optimizer rewrites. ([Docs.rs][4])

### `execute()` boundary

```text id="2jamxp"
execute() SHOULD:
  validate partition id
  clone schema/config handles
  construct stream
  set up bounded channels if needed
  return quickly

execute() SHOULD NOT:
  block on async operations
  read all data
  call remote API synchronously
  allocate full output
```

The guide states that `execute()` should construct and return a stream without heavy work; data production happens when the stream is polled. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 18.15 Custom `RecordBatchStream`

### Type alias

```rust id="dtmobf"
pub type SendableRecordBatchStream =
    Pin<Box<dyn RecordBatchStream<Item = Result<RecordBatch, DataFusionError>> + Send>>;
```

`SendableRecordBatchStream` is a specialized async stream of `RecordBatch`es that can be passed between threads and knows its schema even if it has no data; after a stream returns an error, callers should not poll it again, and returning `Ready(None)` after error/end is recommended. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Easiest stream: `RecordBatchStreamAdapter`

```rust id="ki7wtr"
use datafusion::execution::SendableRecordBatchStream;
use datafusion::physical_plan::stream::RecordBatchStreamAdapter;
use futures::stream;

fn make_stream(schema: SchemaRef) -> SendableRecordBatchStream {
    let s = stream::iter(vec![
        Ok(make_batch_1(schema.clone())),
        Ok(make_batch_2(schema.clone())),
    ]);

    Box::pin(RecordBatchStreamAdapter::new(schema, s))
}
```

The custom provider guide recommends `RecordBatchStreamAdapter` as the easiest way to bridge any `futures::Stream<Item = Result<RecordBatch>>` into a `SendableRecordBatchStream`. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Async API stream pattern

```rust id="k3bwyy"
use async_stream::try_stream;
use datafusion::physical_plan::stream::RecordBatchStreamAdapter;

fn api_stream(
    schema: SchemaRef,
    client: Arc<MyApiClient>,
    request: MyRequest,
) -> SendableRecordBatchStream {
    let schema_for_stream = Arc::clone(&schema);

    let s = try_stream! {
        let mut cursor = None;

        loop {
            let page = client.fetch_page(&request, cursor.clone()).await?;
            if page.rows.is_empty() {
                break;
            }

            let batch = convert_api_rows_to_batch(Arc::clone(&schema_for_stream), page.rows)?;
            yield batch;

            cursor = page.next_cursor;
            if cursor.is_none() {
                break;
            }
        }
    };

    Box::pin(RecordBatchStreamAdapter::new(schema, s))
}
```

### Blocking source pattern

```rust id="zfdy6p"
use datafusion::physical_plan::stream::RecordBatchStreamAdapter;
use tokio_stream::wrappers::ReceiverStream;

fn blocking_stream(
    schema: SchemaRef,
    config: MyBlockingConfig,
) -> SendableRecordBatchStream {
    let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::channel(2);

    tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
        for result in blocking_read_batches(config) {
            if tx.blocking_send(result).is_err() {
                break; // receiver dropped: query cancelled
            }
        }
    });

    let stream = ReceiverStream::new(rx);
    Box::pin(RecordBatchStreamAdapter::new(schema, stream))
}
```

If stream work is blocking or CPU-bound for long periods, the custom provider guide says to avoid blocking the Tokio runtime; offload blocking work to a dedicated thread pool and send batches through a channel. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Agent rules

```text id="fgx7ct"
Stream poll is where I/O and computation belong.
Every yielded RecordBatch must match stream schema.
Use bounded channels for backpressure.
Stop producing when receiver is dropped.
Yield/await regularly; do not monopolize Tokio tasks.
Map source errors into DataFusionError.
```

---

## 18.16 Complete minimal generated table provider

```rust id="hytx1b"
use std::{any::Any, sync::Arc};

use async_trait::async_trait;
use datafusion::arrow::{
    array::{ArrayRef, Int64Array},
    datatypes::{DataType, Field, Schema, SchemaRef},
    record_batch::RecordBatch,
};
use datafusion::catalog::{Session, TableProvider};
use datafusion::common::Result;
use datafusion::datasource::TableType;
use datafusion::execution::{SendableRecordBatchStream, TaskContext};
use datafusion::logical_expr::Expr;
use datafusion::physical_expr::EquivalenceProperties;
use datafusion::physical_plan::{
    execution_plan::{Boundedness, EmissionType},
    stream::RecordBatchStreamAdapter,
    DisplayAs, DisplayFormatType, ExecutionPlan, Partitioning, PlanProperties,
};
use futures::stream;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct CountingTable {
    schema: SchemaRef,
    num_partitions: usize,
    rows_per_partition: usize,
}

impl CountingTable {
    pub fn new(num_partitions: usize, rows_per_partition: usize) -> Self {
        let schema = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
            Field::new("partition", DataType::Int64, false),
            Field::new("value", DataType::Int64, false),
        ]));

        Self {
            schema,
            num_partitions,
            rows_per_partition,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl TableProvider for CountingTable {
    fn schema(&self) -> SchemaRef {
        Arc::clone(&self.schema)
    }

    fn table_type(&self) -> TableType {
        TableType::Base
    }

    async fn scan(
        &self,
        _state: &dyn Session,
        projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>,
        _filters: &[Expr],
        limit: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        let projected_schema = match projection {
            Some(p) => Arc::new(self.schema.project(p)?),
            None => Arc::clone(&self.schema),
        };

        Ok(Arc::new(CountingExec {
            full_schema: Arc::clone(&self.schema),
            projected_schema,
            projection: projection.cloned(),
            num_partitions: self.num_partitions,
            rows_per_partition: limit
                .unwrap_or(self.rows_per_partition)
                .min(self.rows_per_partition),
            properties: Arc::new(PlanProperties::new(
                EquivalenceProperties::new(Arc::clone(&self.schema)),
                Partitioning::UnknownPartitioning(self.num_partitions),
                EmissionType::Incremental,
                Boundedness::Bounded,
            )),
        }))
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
struct CountingExec {
    full_schema: SchemaRef,
    projected_schema: SchemaRef,
    projection: Option<Vec<usize>>,
    num_partitions: usize,
    rows_per_partition: usize,
    properties: Arc<PlanProperties>,
}

impl DisplayAs for CountingExec {
    fn fmt_as(
        &self,
        _t: DisplayFormatType,
        f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>,
    ) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(
            f,
            "CountingExec: partitions={}, rows_per_partition={}, projection={:?}",
            self.num_partitions,
            self.rows_per_partition,
            self.projection,
        )
    }
}

impl ExecutionPlan for CountingExec {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "CountingExec"
    }

    fn properties(&self) -> &Arc<PlanProperties> {
        &self.properties
    }

    fn children(&self) -> Vec<&Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        vec![]
    }

    fn with_new_children(
        self: Arc<Self>,
        children: Vec<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        assert!(children.is_empty());
        Ok(self)
    }

    fn execute(
        &self,
        partition: usize,
        _context: Arc<TaskContext>,
    ) -> Result<SendableRecordBatchStream> {
        let full_schema = Arc::clone(&self.full_schema);
        let out_schema = Arc::clone(&self.projected_schema);
        let projection = self.projection.clone();
        let rows = self.rows_per_partition;

        let batch_stream = stream::once(async move {
            let partition_values = Int64Array::from(vec![partition as i64; rows]);
            let values = Int64Array::from((0..rows as i64).collect::<Vec<_>>());

            let full_batch = RecordBatch::try_new(
                full_schema,
                vec![
                    Arc::new(partition_values) as ArrayRef,
                    Arc::new(values) as ArrayRef,
                ],
            )?;

            match projection {
                Some(indices) => Ok(full_batch.project(&indices)?),
                None => Ok(full_batch),
            }
        });

        Ok(Box::pin(RecordBatchStreamAdapter::new(
            out_schema,
            batch_stream,
        )))
    }
}
```

This follows the official guide’s minimal provider shape: `scan()` builds a plan with metadata, `ExecutionPlan::execute()` builds a stream, and heavy work happens inside the stream when polled. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 18.17 Registering and using the provider

```rust id="blld9q"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let provider = CountingTable::new(4, 1_000);
    ctx.register_table("counting", Arc::new(provider))?;

    let df = ctx
        .sql(
            "SELECT partition, value
             FROM counting
             WHERE value < 10
             ORDER BY partition, value
             LIMIT 20",
        )
        .await?;

    df.show().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

Once a `TableProvider` is registered with a `SessionContext`, it becomes queryable through SQL and DataFrame APIs; the guide shows registering `CountingTable` under the name `counting` and querying it with SQL. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 18.18 Remote API provider design

### Provider architecture

```text id="0449vu"
MyApiTableProvider
  schema: SchemaRef
  client: Arc<MyApiClient>
  table_config: MyTableConfig
  static_metadata: MyTableMetadata

scan(...)
  parse projection -> requested fields
  parse filters -> API filter request
  parse limit -> page cap / row cap
  create MyApiExec

MyApiExec::execute(partition)
  create request for partition/shard/range
  return stream

stream poll
  async fetch page
  convert rows -> Arrow arrays
  yield RecordBatch
  continue next cursor
```

### Remote API pushdown mapping

| DataFusion hint | API mapping                                                    |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| projection      | selected fields / sparse response / GraphQL field list         |
| exact filter    | API query parameter, SQL predicate, index search               |
| inexact filter  | partition selection, approximate search, server-side prefilter |
| limit           | page size / max rows / early stop                              |
| partition       | shard, region, tenant, key range, date range                   |
| ordering        | remote `ORDER BY` only if guaranteed stable                    |

### Agent rules

```text id="4023oy"
Remote API providers must be cancellation-aware.
Use bounded page sizes.
Respect DataFusion limit but do not over-claim final cardinality.
Map rate-limit errors into retryable/clear DataFusionError.
Use TaskContext / RuntimeEnv resources when applicable.
Avoid one HTTP call per row.
Batch rows into Arrow arrays before yielding.
```

---

## 18.19 Non-file source patterns

### SQL database federation

```text id="5q9me7"
filter pushdown:
  exact for SQL-translatable predicates

projection pushdown:
  SELECT only requested columns + filter columns

limit pushdown:
  LIMIT/OFFSET if exact filters or DB handles predicates

partitioning:
  key ranges / shards / partitioned SQL queries

execution:
  async DB client cursor -> batches
```

### Search/index provider

```text id="9v80tq"
filter pushdown:
  exact for indexed fields
  inexact for text/full-text/vector search candidate sets

projection pushdown:
  stored fields only

limit pushdown:
  top-k candidate cap, but preserve residual filter semantics

execution:
  query index -> candidate docs -> convert to Arrow
```

### SaaS REST provider

```text id="iqaz55"
filter pushdown:
  exact only for API-supported query parameters

projection pushdown:
  sparse fieldsets if API supports them

limit pushdown:
  page size and max pages

partitioning:
  endpoint partition, account, region, date ranges

execution:
  async paginated requests -> batches
```

### Message/streaming source

```text id="lw9aex"
provider:
  StreamTable or custom unbounded TableProvider

boundedness:
  Unbounded if stream never naturally ends

partitioning:
  topic partitions

execution:
  consumer stream -> RecordBatchStream
```

DataFusion’s catalog stream module describes `StreamProvider` as a generic interface for reading/writing streaming sources such as FIFO, WebSocket, Kafka, and similar sources. ([Docs.rs][6])

---

## 18.20 Pushdown correctness matrix

| Pushdown          | Correctness risk                          | Required tests                                      |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| projection        | wrong column order/type                   | all projection permutations; no projection          |
| exact filter      | false positives/negatives                 | compare provider output vs DataFusion filter output |
| inexact filter    | too few rows if combined with limit       | inexact + limit queries                             |
| limit             | final result too short                    | limit with filters/sorts/projections                |
| partition pruning | dropped partitions                        | partition filter boundary cases                     |
| ordering metadata | missing SortExec causes wrong top-N/order | `ORDER BY LIMIT` comparisons                        |
| statistics        | bad join/order planning                   | stats stale/wrong/unknown fallback                  |

---

## 18.21 EXPLAIN-driven validation

```sql id="kx9bbl"
EXPLAIN
SELECT *
FROM events
WHERE region = 'us-east-1'
  AND event_type = 'click';
```

Expected progression:

```text id="kg2ceb"
No pushdown:
  FilterExec: region = ... AND event_type = ...
    MyExec: partitions=50

Exact region pushdown:
  FilterExec: event_type = ...
    MyExec: partitions=5, filter=[region = ...]

Exact region + event_type pushdown:
  MyExec: partitions=5, filter=[region = ... AND event_type = ...]
```

The guide recommends `EXPLAIN` as the first diagnostic tool for custom providers because it shows whether DataFusion inserted `FilterExec`, `SortExec`, or `RepartitionExec` above the scan. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

Rust:

```rust id="dbem94"
let explain = ctx
    .sql(
        "EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM counting WHERE partition = 1 LIMIT 10",
    )
    .await?;

explain.show().await?;
```

---

## 18.22 Memory, cancellation, and resource management

### Rules

```text id="nyhlvz"
Use bounded channels for producer/consumer streams.
Stop background work when receiver drops.
Do not spawn untracked tasks that outlive the query.
Do not block Tokio worker threads.
Use dedicated blocking pool for blocking APIs.
Yield periodically in CPU-heavy stream code.
Use TaskContext runtime resources when available.
Avoid buffering full result sets.
```

The `ExecutionPlan` docs say `execute` returns a stream, any execution error is returned as an `Err` item, DataFusion execution should cancel additional work once an error occurs, and the returned stream must free allocated resources when dropped; it also warns that streams must not block the CPU indefinitely and should yield to the Tokio runtime regularly. ([Docs.rs][7])

---

## 18.23 Testing strategy

### Unit: schema and projection

```rust id="ldiqxb"
#[tokio::test]
async fn projection_schema_matches() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let table = CountingTable::new(2, 10);

    let plan = table
        .scan(&session_state, Some(&vec![1]), &[], None)
        .await?;

    assert_eq!(plan.schema().fields()[0].name(), "value");
    Ok(())
}
```

### Integration: compare pushdown vs no pushdown

```text id="956y8t"
same table/provider data
  query A: provider pushdown enabled
  query B: provider pushdown disabled
  assert equal RecordBatches after sort
```

### Required tests

```text id="kp78z8"
[ ] schema() cheap and stable
[ ] scan() does not perform remote read
[ ] projection: all / subset / reordered columns
[ ] filters: exact / inexact / unsupported
[ ] limit with no filters
[ ] limit with exact filters
[ ] limit with inexact filters
[ ] partition count and partition IDs
[ ] empty partitions
[ ] remote API error becomes DataFusionError
[ ] stream cancellation stops background work
[ ] EXPLAIN plan shows expected pushdown
[ ] RecordBatch schemas match stream schemas
[ ] table registration + SQL query path works
```

---

## 18.24 Deployment advisory

### Remote APIs

```text id="mepg7z"
Cache schema/metadata.
Push projection into remote request.
Push only exact server-side filters as Exact.
Use Inexact for partition/stat/candidate pruning.
Batch remote pages into RecordBatches.
Respect rate limits.
Use bounded concurrency.
Implement timeout/retry/circuit-breaker policy.
```

### Databases

```text id="vp23we"
Translate pushdown filters to parameterized SQL.
Never concatenate untrusted literal SQL.
Use remote EXPLAIN or indexes for performance.
Partition by key ranges/shards for parallel scans.
Preserve DataFusion null and type semantics.
```

### Search/vector sources

```text id="4ahliw"
Treat vector/top-k retrieval as inexact unless final predicate semantics are guaranteed.
Return score columns explicitly.
Limit pushdown must not hide matches after residual filters.
```

### Object/non-file sources

```text id="vdwzty"
Use object-store registry if source is file-like.
Use TableProvider only when source is not representable as ListingTable/FileFormat.
```

---

## 18.25 Anti-pattern inventory

* Fetching data in `scan()`.
* Blocking on async work in `execute()`.
* Returning batches whose schema differs from stream schema.
* Claiming `Exact` filter pushdown for approximate remote predicates.
* Applying limit before inexact filters.
* Ignoring projection and returning full schema batches.
* Reporting natural ordering that is not guaranteed.
* Reporting one partition for a sharded/partitioned source.
* Spawning background tasks that continue after stream drop.
* Buffering all remote rows before yielding first batch.
* Performing one remote call per row.
* Hiding provider errors as empty result sets.
* Returning stale/wrong constraints.
* Advertising statistics as exact when approximate.
* Using direct `TableProvider` for file formats when `ListingTable` + `FileFormat` is enough.
* Failing to test with `EXPLAIN`.

---

## 18.26 Agent checklist

```text id="9yr5wl"
[ ] First decide if MemTable, StreamTable, ViewTable, or ListingTable is enough.
[ ] Implement full TableProvider only when complete custom source control is needed.
[ ] schema() returns Arc<Schema> cheaply.
[ ] table_type() returns correct table category.
[ ] scan() builds ExecutionPlan only; no heavy I/O.
[ ] projection maps to output schema and remote selected fields.
[ ] supports_filters_pushdown returns Exact/Inexact/Unsupported accurately.
[ ] scan() uses pushed filters only according to declared support.
[ ] limit pushdown is safe with exact/no filters; careful with inexact filters.
[ ] statistics() returns conservative cached stats or None.
[ ] constraints() returns None unless constraints are supported.
[ ] ExecutionPlan properties correctly describe partitioning/order/boundedness.
[ ] execute() constructs stream quickly.
[ ] stream polling performs I/O/computation and yields RecordBatches.
[ ] blocking work is offloaded and cancellation-aware.
[ ] custom provider is registered with SessionContext and query-tested.
[ ] EXPLAIN confirms pushdown, partitioning, and absence/presence of FilterExec/SortExec/RepartitionExec.
```

# DataFusion Advanced — 19) Logical plans

Style target follows the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

## 19.0 Mental model: `LogicalPlan` = semantic relational program

```text
SQL / DataFrame / custom query language
  → Expr + LogicalPlan
      ├─ TableScan / EmptyRelation / Values
      ├─ Projection
      ├─ Filter
      ├─ Aggregate / Window
      ├─ Join / CrossJoin / Union / Distinct
      ├─ Sort / Limit / Repartition
      ├─ Ddl / Dml / Copy / Explain / Analyze / DescribeTable
      ├─ Unnest / RecursiveQuery / SubqueryAlias
      └─ Extension(custom node)
  → analyzer + logical optimizer
  → physical planner
  → ExecutionPlan
```

A `LogicalPlan` is a tree of relational operators such as `Projection` and `Filter`; each node transforms an input relation into an output relation with a potentially different schema, and data conceptually flows from leaves up to the root. Logical plans can be created by the SQL planner, the DataFrame API, or programmatically, such as from a custom query language. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 19.1 Value case

| Need                     | Logical-plan value                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| SQL compiler target      | `SqlToRel` lowers SQL AST into `LogicalPlan`                                               |
| DataFrame implementation | DataFrame methods delegate to `LogicalPlanBuilder`                                         |
| custom query language    | emit `LogicalPlan` directly, bypass SQL                                                    |
| optimizer input          | logical optimizer rewrites tree while preserving results                                   |
| authorization/policy     | inspect table refs, columns, filters, functions before execution                           |
| custom operators         | use `LogicalPlan::Extension`                                                               |
| testing                  | snapshot/compare semantic plan before physical algorithms                                  |
| portability              | logical plans do not encode hash join vs sort-merge join, file openers, runtime partitions |

The library guide says DataFrame is a higher-level API that delegates to `LogicalPlanBuilder`; it also states that logical plans must be compiled into physical `ExecutionPlan`s before execution because physical plans contain algorithmic and execution-specific details. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 19.2 Creation paths

| Path        | API                                                                | When to use                                       |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| SQL         | `ctx.sql("SELECT ...").await?` → `DataFrame` → `df.logical_plan()` | user-authored query text                          |
| DataFrame   | `ctx.table(...).await?.filter(...).select(...)`                    | typed Rust plan construction                      |
| Builder     | `LogicalPlanBuilder::scan(...).filter(...).project(...).build()?`  | custom compilers, optimizer tests, extension code |
| Direct enum | `LogicalPlan::Filter(Filter::try_new(...))`                        | rare low-level tests / exact node construction    |
| Extension   | `LogicalPlan::Extension(Extension { node })`                       | custom logical operators                          |

DataFusion docs explicitly say it is possible to create logical plans by directly constructing the `LogicalPlan` enum, but it is usually easier to use `LogicalPlanBuilder`; the builder supports roots such as `empty`, `values`, `scan`, and `scan_with_filters`, then transformation methods such as `filter`, `limit`, `sort`, `distinct`, and `join`. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

---

## 19.3 Core imports

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::{DataType, Field, Schema, SchemaRef};
use datafusion::common::{DFSchema, DFSchemaRef, Result};
use datafusion::logical_expr::{
    col, lit, Expr, JoinType, LogicalPlan, LogicalPlanBuilder, LogicalTableSource,
};
use datafusion::prelude::*;
```

Prefer `datafusion::logical_expr::*` re-exports for app code. Use direct subcrates such as `datafusion-expr` only when building lower-level extension crates and pin all DataFusion subcrates to the same version.

---

## 19.4 `LogicalPlan` variants: map of major nodes

Current `LogicalPlan` variants listed in docs include: `Aggregate`, `Analyze`, `Copy`, `Ddl`, `DescribeTable`, `Distinct`, `Dml`, `EmptyRelation`, `Explain`, `Extension`, `Filter`, `Join`, `Limit`, `Projection`, `RecursiveQuery`, `Repartition`, `Sort`, `Statement`, `Subquery`, `SubqueryAlias`, `TableScan`, `Union`, `Unnest`, `Values`, and `Window`. ([Docs.rs][1])

| Variant                | Semantic role            | SQL/DataFrame source                                 |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `TableScan`            | read table/source        | `FROM t`, `ctx.table`, `LogicalPlanBuilder::scan`    |
| `Projection`           | compute/select columns   | `SELECT expr`, `df.select`, `builder.project`        |
| `Filter`               | row predicate            | `WHERE`, `df.filter`, `builder.filter`               |
| `Aggregate`            | group + aggregate        | `GROUP BY`, `df.aggregate`, `builder.aggregate`      |
| `Window`               | window expressions       | `OVER (...)`, `builder.window`                       |
| `Join`                 | relational join          | `JOIN`, `df.join`, `builder.join`                    |
| `Sort`                 | ordering                 | `ORDER BY`, `df.sort`, `builder.sort`                |
| `Limit`                | skip/fetch               | `LIMIT/OFFSET`, `df.limit`, `builder.limit`          |
| `Union`                | set append               | `UNION`, `df.union`, `builder.union`                 |
| `Distinct`             | deduplication            | `SELECT DISTINCT`, `df.distinct`, `builder.distinct` |
| `Values`               | inline rows              | `VALUES (...)`, `builder.values`                     |
| `EmptyRelation`        | empty/one-row relation   | constants/planner internals, `builder.empty`         |
| `Extension`            | custom operator          | user-defined logical node                            |
| `Ddl` / `Dml` / `Copy` | catalog/write statements | `CREATE`, `INSERT`, `COPY`                           |
| `Explain` / `Analyze`  | explain/analyze plan     | `EXPLAIN`, `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`                         |
| `Unnest`               | nested expansion         | `UNNEST`, `builder.unnest_*`                         |

Agent rule:

```text
LogicalPlan expresses "what"; ExecutionPlan expresses "how".
Never infer physical algorithm, parallelism, or file I/O behavior from LogicalPlan alone.
```

---

## 19.5 Logical plan root construction

### `empty`

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::empty(false).build()?;
```

`LogicalPlanBuilder::empty(produce_one_row)` creates an empty relation; `produce_one_row=true` means the node produces a placeholder row. ([Docs.rs][4])

Use cases:

```text
SELECT literal-only plans
optimizer tests
synthetic plans
existence/no-op plans
```

### `values`

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::values(vec![
    vec![lit(1i64), lit("alice")],
    vec![lit(2i64), lit("bob")],
])?
.build()?;
```

`values` creates a `VALUES`-style relation and infers schema from the data; the docs note default column names such as `column1`, `column2`, so it is usually better to override names with an alias list or supplied schema. ([Docs.rs][4])

### `values_with_schema`

```rust
let schema = Arc::new(DFSchema::try_from(Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("id", DataType::Int64, false),
    Field::new("name", DataType::Utf8, true),
]))?);

let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::values_with_schema(
    vec![
        vec![lit(1i64), lit("alice")],
        vec![lit(2i64), lit("bob")],
    ],
    &schema,
)?
.build()?;
```

Use `values_with_schema` when output names/types are part of the contract.

### `scan`

```rust
let schema = Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("id", DataType::Int32, true),
    Field::new("name", DataType::Utf8, true),
]);

let table_source = LogicalTableSource::new(SchemaRef::new(schema));

let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan(
    "person",
    Arc::new(table_source),
    None, // optional projection indices
)?
.filter(col("id").gt(lit(500)))?
.build()?;
```

The logical-plan guide shows this exact pattern: build a `LogicalTableSource`, call `LogicalPlanBuilder::scan`, apply `filter`, then `build`; at this stage no query execution happens. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Table-name normalization caveat

```rust
// Treated as SQL identifier and normalized.
LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("MyTable", table_source.clone(), None)?;

// Preserves mixed case by quoted identifier parsing.
LogicalPlanBuilder::scan(r#""MyTable""#, table_source.clone(), None)?;
```

`LogicalPlanBuilder::scan` treats string table names as SQL identifiers, so unquoted strings are normalized; use quoted identifiers or `TableReference` if case/name preservation matters. ([Docs.rs][4])

---

## 19.6 Relation operators: scan → filter → projection

### Builder chain

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("person", Arc::new(table_source), None)?
    .filter(col("id").gt(lit(500)))?
    .project(vec![
        col("id"),
        col("name"),
        (col("id") + lit(1)).alias("next_id"),
    ])?
    .build()?;
```

### Equivalent shape

```text
Projection: person.id, person.name, person.id + Int32(1) AS next_id
  Filter: person.id > Int32(500)
    TableScan: person
```

`filter` applies a predicate to the plan; `project` applies a projection expression list. The builder API has `project`, `select` by column indices, and `filter` as transformation methods. ([Docs.rs][4])

Agent rules:

```text
filter = WHERE-stage row predicate.
project = SELECT-stage output expression list.
Always alias computed expressions.
Use select(indices) only when you intentionally project by ordinal.
```

---

## 19.7 Aggregate plans

```rust
use datafusion::functions_aggregate::expr_fn::{sum, count};

let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("sales", Arc::new(table_source), None)?
    .filter(col("amount").gt(lit(0.0)))?
    .aggregate(
        vec![col("region")],
        vec![
            count(lit(1)).alias("row_count"),
            sum(col("amount")).alias("total_amount"),
        ],
    )?
    .build()?;
```

`LogicalPlanBuilder::aggregate(group_expr, aggr_expr)` groups by the supplied expressions and calculates aggregate expressions for each distinct group-expression value. ([Docs.rs][4])

Agent rules:

```text
group_expr = GROUP BY keys.
aggr_expr = aggregate output expressions.
Alias aggregate outputs.
Use Filter before Aggregate for WHERE semantics.
Use another Filter after Aggregate for HAVING-like semantics.
```

Post-aggregate filter:

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::from(plan)
    .filter(col("total_amount").gt(lit(1000.0)))?
    .build()?;
```

---

## 19.8 Sort and limit

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("events", Arc::new(table_source), None)?
    .sort(vec![
        col("event_ts").sort(false, false), // DESC NULLS LAST
        col("event_id").sort(true, true),   // ASC NULLS FIRST
    ])?
    .limit(0, Some(100))?
    .build()?;
```

`sort_by` sorts by expressions using default direction, `sort` accepts `Sort` expressions, `sort_with_limit` combines sort and optional fetch, and `limit(skip, fetch)` skips rows then fetches a maximum row count. ([Docs.rs][4])

Agent rules:

```text
Use sort before limit for deterministic top-N.
Use sort_with_limit for top-K-like plans where appropriate.
limit(skip, fetch): skip = offset, fetch = max rows after offset.
Do not assume output order without Sort.
```

---

## 19.9 Joins

### Explicit equijoin

```rust
let left = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("orders", Arc::new(orders_source), None)?
    .build()?;

let right = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("customers", Arc::new(customers_source), None)?
    .build()?;

let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::from(left)
    .join(
        right,
        JoinType::Inner,
        (
            vec![datafusion::common::Column::from_qualified_name("orders.customer_id")],
            vec![datafusion::common::Column::from_qualified_name("customers.id")],
        ),
        None,
    )?
    .build()?;
```

`join(right, join_type, join_keys, filter)` applies a join with explicitly specified equijoin columns and an optional filter expression; the docs note the optional filter is applied only to matched rows for outer joins. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Expression join

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::from(left)
    .join_on(
        right,
        JoinType::Inner,
        vec![
            col("orders.customer_id").eq(col("customers.id")),
            col("orders.region").eq(col("customers.region")),
        ],
    )?
    .build()?;
```

`join_on` accepts join expressions directly, and DataFusion automatically identifies and optimizes equality predicates, so there is no performance difference versus explicit `join` for equality predicates. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Detailed joins

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::from(left)
    .join_detailed(
        right,
        JoinType::Inner,
        (left_keys, right_keys),
        None,
        null_equality,
    )?
    .build()?;
```

`join_detailed` adds explicit null-equality behavior; `join_with_expr_keys` is a lower-level API where equijoin predicates and residual filters are supplied separately, and the docs recommend `join_on` for most users because it identifies predicates automatically. ([Docs.rs][4])

Agent rules:

```text
Prefer join_on for generated expression joins.
Prefer join for simple named equijoins.
Use join_detailed only when null equality semantics matter.
Alias/qualify duplicate columns before/after join.
Test outer-join filter semantics carefully.
```

---

## 19.10 Union, distinct, and set-like logical operators

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::from(left_plan)
    .union(right_plan)?
    .build()?;
```

`union` preserves duplicate rows; `union_by_name` preserves duplicate rows but aligns by column name; `union_distinct` removes duplicates; `union_by_name_distinct` aligns by name and removes duplicates. ([Docs.rs][4])

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::from(left_plan)
    .distinct()?
    .build()?;
```

`distinct` applies deduplication. `distinct_on(on_expr, select_expr, sort_expr)` selects first values by distinct-on expressions according to optional sort expressions. ([Docs.rs][4])

Static set functions:

```rust
let intersect = LogicalPlanBuilder::intersect(left_plan, right_plan, false)?;
let except = LogicalPlanBuilder::except(left_plan, right_plan, false)?;
```

`intersect` and `except` build set-operation logical plans, with an `is_all` flag. ([Docs.rs][4])

Agent rules:

```text
Use union for UNION ALL semantics with identical schemas.
Use union_by_name for schema-evolution/column-order mismatch.
Use distinct variants only when deduplication is required.
Normalize schemas explicitly before set operations.
```

---

## 19.11 Window and unnest

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("events", Arc::new(source), None)?
    .window(vec![
        // window expression built elsewhere
    ])?
    .build()?;
```

`window` applies window functions and extends the schema. ([Docs.rs][4])

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("users", Arc::new(source), None)?
    .unnest_column(datafusion::common::Column::from_name("tags"))?
    .build()?;
```

`unnest_column`, `unnest_column_with_options`, and `unnest_columns_with_options` add `Unnest` logical operations for nested columns. ([Docs.rs][4])

Agent rules:

```text
Window extends row-level output with analytic expressions.
Unnest can change row cardinality or expand struct columns.
Add LIMIT / filters before unnest where possible.
```

---

## 19.12 Display methods and plan diagnostics

### Human readable node only

```rust
println!("{}", plan.display());
```

`display()` returns a human-readable description of the current logical-plan node, not including children. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Indented tree

```rust
println!("{}", plan.display_indent());
```

`display_indent()` produces one line per node in an indented logical-plan tree. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Indented tree with schema

```rust
println!("{}", plan.display_indent_schema());
```

`display_indent_schema()` produces one line per node and includes each node’s output schema. ([Docs.rs][1])

### PostgreSQL JSON format

```rust
let pg_json = format!("{}", plan.display_pg_json());
```

`display_pg_json()` returns a PostgreSQL-style JSON plan representation that can be used with existing visualization tools. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Graphviz DOT

```rust
let dot = format!("{}", plan.display_graphviz());
std::fs::write("/tmp/plan.dot", dot)?;
```

`display_graphviz()` returns DOT-language output for graphical visualization; docs note it currently produces both a basic-structure graph and a graph with additional details such as schema. ([Docs.rs][1])

Agent rules:

```text
display_indent() = concise semantic snapshot.
display_indent_schema() = debugging schema evolution.
display_graphviz() = complex tree visualization.
display_pg_json() = plan visualization tooling.
Do not snapshot exact display strings across DataFusion upgrades unless pinned.
```

---

## 19.13 LogicalPlanBuilder vs SQL vs DataFrame

| Path                      | Strength                              | Weakness                                         |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| SQL                       | user-facing, compact, full SQL syntax | string validation, injection, dialect governance |
| DataFrame                 | typed Rust flow, simple to compose    | hides some logical-plan construction details     |
| `LogicalPlanBuilder`      | explicit semantic plan construction   | lower-level, less ergonomic than DataFrame       |
| direct `LogicalPlan` enum | exact node control                    | most fragile/verbose                             |
| custom `Extension` node   | new operators                         | requires physical planning + optimizer support   |

DataFusion’s top-level docs say projects can build their own query languages or plans with `LogicalPlanBuilder`, rather than using the built-in SQL planner `SqlToRel`. They list `LogicalPlanBuilder` alongside other extension points such as custom table providers, catalogs, UDFs, optimizer rules, and custom planner nodes. ([Docs.rs][5])

Agent decision rules:

```text
Human-authored query language -> SQL.
Rust-generated business logic -> DataFrame / Expr.
Custom compiler target -> LogicalPlanBuilder.
Custom relational operator -> LogicalPlan::Extension.
Optimizer rule tests -> LogicalPlanBuilder or direct enum.
```

---

## 19.14 Building logical plans directly

### Direct enum construction

```rust
use datafusion::logical_expr::{Filter, LogicalPlan, TableScan};

let projection = None;
let filters = vec![];
let fetch = None;

let table_scan = LogicalPlan::TableScan(TableScan::try_new(
    "person",
    Arc::new(table_source),
    projection,
    filters,
    fetch,
)?);

let filter_expr = col("id").gt(lit(500));

let plan = LogicalPlan::Filter(Filter::try_new(
    filter_expr,
    Arc::new(table_scan),
)?);

println!("{}", plan.display_indent_schema());
```

The logical-plan guide shows manual construction of `TableScan` and `Filter` variants, then `display_indent_schema()` output. It also says this is possible but `LogicalPlanBuilder` is easier in most cases. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Builder equivalent

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("person", Arc::new(table_source), None)?
    .filter(col("id").gt(lit(500)))?
    .build()?;
```

Use direct enum construction only when:

```text
testing a specific node constructor
constructing a variant not exposed ergonomically by builder
working inside optimizer/planner internals
debugging schema behavior at exact node boundary
```

---

## 19.15 Table sources: `LogicalTableSource` vs `TableProvider`

`LogicalTableSource` is useful for tests, docs, and building logical plans when you do not intend to use DataFusion’s physical planner. In normal applications, use a `TableProvider`; to turn a `TableProvider` into a `TableSource`, use `provider_as_source` or `DefaultTableSource`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Test-only / logical-only

```rust
let schema = Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("id", DataType::Int32, true),
]);

let source = LogicalTableSource::new(SchemaRef::new(schema));

let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("t", Arc::new(source), None)?
    .filter(col("id").gt(lit(10)))?
    .build()?;
```

### Application provider source

```rust
use datafusion::catalog::TableProvider;
use datafusion::datasource::provider_as_source;

let provider: Arc<dyn TableProvider> = Arc::new(my_provider);
let table_source = provider_as_source(provider);

let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("t", table_source, None)?
    .build()?;
```

Agent rules:

```text
LogicalTableSource = schema-only test/logical planning source.
TableProvider = real DataFusion scan/execution source.
If plan must execute through DataFusion physical planner, prefer TableProvider-backed source.
```

---

## 19.16 Preserving schemas

### Inspect builder schema during construction

```rust
let builder = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("events", table_source, None)?
    .filter(col("amount").gt(lit(0.0)))?;

println!("{:?}", builder.schema());
```

`LogicalPlanBuilder::schema()` returns the output schema of the plan built so far, while `plan()` returns the current `LogicalPlan` held by the builder. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Inspect final plan schema

```rust
let schema = plan.schema();
for field in schema.fields() {
    println!("{}: {:?}", field.name(), field.data_type());
}
```

`LogicalPlan` exposes `schema()` and schema-recomputing/normalization methods; schema is central to expression resolution and optimizer correctness. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Output schema contract

```text
Projection:
  output fields derived from select expressions and aliases

Filter:
  output schema unchanged from input

Aggregate:
  output fields = grouping expressions + aggregate expressions

Join:
  output fields = left + right fields according to join type/constraint

Sort:
  output schema unchanged from input

Limit:
  output schema unchanged from input

Union:
  output schema based on compatible inputs

Extension:
  schema is supplied by custom node
```

Agent rules:

```text
Preserve field names and types across rewrites.
Use alias() on computed expressions before projection/aggregate.
Never assume expression display name is stable enough for public schema.
Check plan.check_invariants() in tests when manipulating plans directly.
```

`LogicalPlan` exposes `check_invariants`, `with_new_exprs`, `recompute_schema`, and tree-node traversal/rewrite APIs, reflecting that schema/expression consistency is a first-class invariant. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 19.17 Preserving expression names

### Good

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("sales", source, None)?
    .project(vec![
        col("region"),
        (col("amount") * lit(1.08)).alias("amount_with_tax"),
    ])?
    .build()?;
```

### Bad

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("sales", source, None)?
    .project(vec![
        col("region"),
        col("amount") * lit(1.08), // output name likely expression-derived
    ])?
    .build()?;
```

Expression names affect parent references, output fields, error messages, and snapshot stability. Optimizer docs also emphasize that expression names must be preserved during rewrites; changing names while preserving semantic values can still break downstream plan references and output schema expectations. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

Agent rules:

```text
Alias every computed projection.
Alias every aggregate.
Alias every window expression.
When rewriting Exprs, preserve aliases unless intentionally changing output schema.
Use unalias only for semantic comparison, not output-building.
```

---

## 19.18 Plan traversal and rewrite

### Collect expressions

```rust
use std::collections::HashSet;
use datafusion::common::tree_node::TreeNodeRecursion;

let mut expressions = HashSet::new();

plan.apply(|node| {
    node.apply_expressions(|expr| {
        expressions.insert(expr.clone());
        Ok(TreeNodeRecursion::Continue)
    })?;
    Ok(TreeNodeRecursion::Continue)
})?;
```

The `LogicalPlan` docs show using the tree-node API to recursively walk the plan and collect expressions via `apply` and `apply_expressions`. ([Docs.rs][7])

### Top-down / bottom-up rewrite

```rust
use datafusion::common::tree_node::{Transformed, TreeNode};

let transformed = plan.transform_up(|node| {
    // inspect/replace node
    Ok(Transformed::no(node))
})?;

let plan = transformed.data;
```

`LogicalPlan` implements tree rewrite methods such as `transform_down` and `transform_up`, which recursively rewrite nodes top-down or bottom-up and return `Transformed<LogicalPlan>`. ([Docs.rs][7])

Agent rules:

```text
Use transform_up for child-aware rewrites.
Use transform_down for context/ancestor-aware rewrites.
Use apply/apply_expressions for analysis-only passes.
Maintain schema and aliases.
Do not duplicate volatile expressions unsafely.
```

---

## 19.19 Parameters / placeholders

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("t1", table_source, None)?
    .filter(col("id").eq(placeholder("$1")))?
    .build()?;

let plan = plan.with_param_values(vec![
    ScalarValue::from(3i32),
])?;
```

`LogicalPlan::with_param_values` replaces placeholder parameters such as `$1` or named parameters with `ScalarValue`s; docs show building a filter with `$1` and then replacing it with `Int32(3)`. `get_parameter_names`, `get_parameter_types`, and `get_parameter_fields` inspect placeholders. ([Docs.rs][1])

Agent rules:

```text
Use placeholders for prepared/generic plans.
Use with_param_values for binding.
Use get_parameter_types/fields for validation before binding.
Do not string-concatenate literal user values into SQL or logical expressions.
```

---

## 19.20 Extension nodes

### Purpose

```text
LogicalPlan::Extension
  = custom logical operator
  = unsupported by built-in relational algebra
  = requires custom planning/optimization rules if it should execute
```

`LogicalPlan` contains an `Extension` variant that lets projects add custom logical operators. `UserDefinedLogicalNodeCore` is the recommended trait for implementing custom nodes; it requires methods such as `name`, `inputs`, `schema`, `expressions`, `fmt_for_explain`, and `with_exprs_and_inputs`. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Skeleton

```rust
use std::{fmt, sync::Arc};
use datafusion::common::{DFSchemaRef, Result};
use datafusion::logical_expr::{Expr, LogicalPlan, UserDefinedLogicalNodeCore};

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
struct MyNode {
    input: LogicalPlan,
    schema: DFSchemaRef,
    predicate: Expr,
}

impl UserDefinedLogicalNodeCore for MyNode {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "MyNode"
    }

    fn inputs(&self) -> Vec<&LogicalPlan> {
        vec![&self.input]
    }

    fn schema(&self) -> &DFSchemaRef {
        &self.schema
    }

    fn expressions(&self) -> Vec<Expr> {
        vec![self.predicate.clone()]
    }

    fn fmt_for_explain(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "MyNode: predicate={}", self.predicate)
    }

    fn with_exprs_and_inputs(
        &self,
        exprs: Vec<Expr>,
        inputs: Vec<LogicalPlan>,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self {
            input: inputs.into_iter().next().expect("one input"),
            schema: self.schema.clone(),
            predicate: exprs.into_iter().next().expect("one expr"),
        })
    }
}
```

### Extension-node invariants

```text
inputs() returns child plans only.
expressions() returns node-local expressions only.
schema() is output schema, not input schema unless identical.
with_exprs_and_inputs must preserve semantic order.
fmt_for_explain must be stable enough for diagnostics.
Pushdown hooks must be conservative.
```

Custom extension nodes require a physical planner extension or custom query planner before they can execute; otherwise DataFusion can represent but not necessarily lower them to a runnable `ExecutionPlan`.

---

## 19.21 Logical plans to physical plans

```rust
let physical_plan = ctx
    .state()
    .create_physical_plan(&plan)
    .await?;
```

Logical plans cannot be directly executed; they must be compiled into a physical `ExecutionPlan`. The logical-plan guide says the easiest path is `SessionState::create_physical_plan`, and it emphasizes that physical plans include more detail such as specific algorithms and optimizations. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
LogicalPlan is not executable.
Use SessionState::create_physical_plan for explicit compile.
DataFrame collect/show/stream compile automatically.
Custom logical Extension needs custom physical planning.
```

---

## 19.22 End-to-end: direct logical plan → physical plan → stream

```rust
use futures::StreamExt;
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use datafusion::logical_expr::{LogicalPlanBuilder, LogicalTableSource};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let schema = Schema::new(vec![
        Field::new("id", DataType::Int32, true),
        Field::new("name", DataType::Utf8, true),
    ]);

    let source = Arc::new(LogicalTableSource::new(SchemaRef::new(schema)));

    let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("person", source, None)?
        .filter(col("id").gt(lit(500)))?
        .project(vec![col("name")])?
        .limit(0, Some(100))?
        .build()?;

    println!("{}", plan.display_indent_schema());

    let physical = ctx.state().create_physical_plan(&plan).await?;
    let task_ctx = ctx.task_ctx();

    let mut stream = physical.execute(0, task_ctx)?;

    while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await {
        let batch = batch?;
        println!("rows={}", batch.num_rows());
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

For real execution, use a `TableProvider`-backed source rather than `LogicalTableSource` where possible; the guide notes `LogicalTableSource` is suitable for tests/docs and for building logical plans without DataFusion’s physical planner, while `TableProvider` is the common path for actual planning/execution. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 19.23 Logical-plan policy validation

### Example: deny scans outside allowlist

```rust
use datafusion::common::tree_node::{TreeNode, TreeNodeRecursion};

fn validate_tables(plan: &LogicalPlan, allowed: &std::collections::HashSet<String>)
    -> datafusion::error::Result<()>
{
    plan.apply(|node| {
        if let LogicalPlan::TableScan(scan) = node {
            let name = scan.table_name.to_string();
            if !allowed.contains(&name) {
                return Err(datafusion::error::DataFusionError::Plan(
                    format!("table not allowed: {name}")
                ));
            }
        }
        Ok(TreeNodeRecursion::Continue)
    })?;

    Ok(())
}
```

### Example: collect column refs from expressions

```rust
let mut refs = std::collections::HashSet::new();

plan.apply(|node| {
    node.apply_expressions(|expr| {
        for col in expr.column_refs() {
            refs.insert(col.clone());
        }
        Ok(TreeNodeRecursion::Continue)
    })?;
    Ok(TreeNodeRecursion::Continue)
})?;
```

Use logical-plan inspection for:

```text
table allowlists
column allowlists
function allowlists
unbounded query rejection
DML/DDL detection
direct path table detection
tenant schema enforcement
extension-node denial/approval
```

---

## 19.24 Building plans directly vs via SQL/DataFrame

### Prefer SQL when

```text
humans write the query
CTEs/window syntax dominate
SQL dialect is the product interface
query text must be stored/audited
tooling emits SQL
```

### Prefer DataFrame when

```text
application code generates filters/projections
you want Rust type checking and no SQL string concatenation
policy filters/masks are appended after user SQL
query shape is simple relational composition
```

### Prefer LogicalPlanBuilder when

```text
writing a compiler from another language
testing optimizer rules
creating reusable plan templates
needing direct plan inspection/modification
building logical plans independent of SessionContext
```

### Prefer direct `LogicalPlan` enum when

```text
testing exact node behavior
constructing special variants manually
working in optimizer internals
creating extension nodes
```

Agent rule:

```text
Use the highest-level API that preserves required control.
Do not drop to direct enum construction just because it looks precise.
```

---

## 19.25 Plan names, qualifiers, and output identity

### Alias tables / subqueries

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("orders", orders_source, None)?
    .alias("o")?
    .build()?;
```

`LogicalPlanBuilder::alias` applies a relation alias using a `TableReference`. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Alias expressions

```rust
let plan = LogicalPlanBuilder::scan("sales", source, None)?
    .project(vec![
        col("region"),
        sum(col("amount")).alias("total_amount"),
    ])?
    .build()?;
```

### Rules

```text
Relation aliases affect column qualification.
Expression aliases affect output field names.
Computed expressions without aliases generate expression-derived names.
Optimizers and parent nodes may rely on output expression names.
```

---

## 19.26 Testing logical plans

### Snapshot semantic shape

```rust
assert_eq!(
    plan.display_indent().to_string(),
    "Projection: person.name\n  Filter: person.id > Int32(500)\n    TableScan: person"
);
```

### Snapshot schema evolution

```rust
insta::assert_snapshot!(
    plan.display_indent_schema().to_string()
);
```

### Validate invariants

```rust
plan.check_invariants()?;
```

### Test optimized plan

```rust
let optimized = ctx.state().optimize(&plan)?;
println!("{}", optimized.display_indent_schema());
```

Agent test matrix:

```text
[ ] unoptimized plan shape
[ ] optimized plan shape
[ ] schema at each critical node
[ ] aliases preserved
[ ] qualified columns after joins
[ ] parameters bind correctly
[ ] custom extension node reconstructs with_exprs_and_inputs
[ ] physical plan can be created if execution is expected
[ ] result batches match expected output
```

Snapshot warning:

```text
Plan display strings are diagnostics, not stable cross-version API.
Pin DataFusion version for golden plan snapshots.
Prefer semantic checks for long-lived tests.
```

---

## 19.27 Deployment advisory

```text
Query services:
  parse/build plan
  validate logical plan for table/function/policy
  add service filters/limits/masks as DataFrame/LogicalPlan rewrites
  optimize
  physical plan / execute stream

Custom query languages:
  emit LogicalPlanBuilder chains
  preserve aliases and schema
  validate output schema before execution
  add tests against equivalent SQL if possible

Optimizer extensions:
  use tree_node transform APIs
  maintain schema/name invariants
  check volatile expressions before duplication/reordering
  test with EXPLAIN and results

Catalog/source extensions:
  TableProvider first
  LogicalPlan::Extension only for new relational semantics
```

---

## 19.28 Anti-pattern inventory

* Treating `LogicalPlan` as executable.
* Inferring physical join algorithm from `LogicalPlan::Join`.
* Dropping aliases during optimizer rewrites.
* Using expression-derived field names as public API.
* Constructing `LogicalPlan` enum nodes directly when `LogicalPlanBuilder` suffices.
* Using `LogicalTableSource` for real execution when a `TableProvider` is required.
* Reporting extension-node schema incorrectly.
* Returning child expressions from `UserDefinedLogicalNodeCore::expressions()` instead of node-local expressions.
* Implementing `with_exprs_and_inputs` with changed ordering.
* Claiming pushdown/limit behavior for extension nodes without semantic proof.
* Snapshotting exact plan strings across DataFusion upgrades without pinning.
* Using unqualified column names after joins.
* Mutating logical plans without `check_invariants`.
* Running `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on expensive queries just to inspect logical shape.
* Building direct plans with normalized table names accidentally due to unquoted identifier strings.

---

## 19.29 Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Decide creation path: SQL / DataFrame / LogicalPlanBuilder / direct enum / Extension.
[ ] Treat LogicalPlan as semantic tree, not executable runtime.
[ ] Use LogicalPlanBuilder for programmatic construction.
[ ] Use scan with TableProvider-backed source for executable plans.
[ ] Use filter/project/aggregate/join/sort/limit builder methods for relation operators.
[ ] Alias computed, aggregate, window, and case expressions.
[ ] Preserve schemas and output names during rewrites.
[ ] Use display_indent for concise plan snapshots.
[ ] Use display_indent_schema for schema debugging.
[ ] Use display_graphviz for complex plan visualization.
[ ] Use tree_node apply/transform APIs for analysis and rewrites.
[ ] Validate allowed tables/functions/columns at logical-plan level.
[ ] Use UserDefinedLogicalNodeCore for custom logical operators.
[ ] Add physical planner support for Extension nodes that must execute.
[ ] Compile to ExecutionPlan with SessionState::create_physical_plan or via DataFrame actions.
[ ] Pin DataFusion version for plan snapshots and extension APIs.
```
