## 27.22 Configuration governance

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let read_only_sql_options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);

let df = ctx.sql_with_options(user_sql, read_only_sql_options).await?;
```

`SET` is a statement-level capability. If user SQL should not mutate execution behavior, disable SQL statements with `SQLOptions::with_allow_statements(false)` and construct all configuration in Rust or environment-controlled startup.

Agent governance rules:

```text
Untrusted SQL:
  disable statements.
  do not expose SET memory_limit / target_partitions / dialect changes.
  set time_zone, dialect, and parser limits server-side.

Admin SQL:
  allow SET/RESET deliberately.
  audit key/value changes.
  avoid letting user sessions change global shared RuntimeEnv unexpectedly.

Multi-tenant:
  isolate SessionContext/RuntimeEnv per tenant or policy domain.
  pin cache/memory/temp settings per tenant class.
```

---

## 27.23 Config inspection harness

```rust
use datafusion::arrow::util::pretty::pretty_format_batches;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let batches = ctx.sql("SHOW ALL").await?.collect().await?;
    println!("{}", pretty_format_batches(&batches)?);

    let batch_size = ctx
        .sql("SHOW datafusion.execution.batch_size")
        .await?
        .collect()
        .await?;
    println!("{}", pretty_format_batches(&batch_size)?);

    Ok(())
}
```

`SHOW ALL` lists available configuration options, and `SHOW <option>` returns a specific option’s current value; the CLI docs show both forms. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

---

## 27.24 Rust deployment template

```rust
use datafusion::execution::{
    runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder,
    session_state::SessionStateBuilder,
};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

pub fn build_production_context() -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let config = SessionConfig::new()
        .with_batch_size(8192)
        .with_target_partitions(num_cpus::get())
        .with_information_schema(false)
        .set_str("datafusion.execution.time_zone", "UTC")
        .set_bool("datafusion.execution.parquet.pruning", true)
        .set_bool("datafusion.execution.parquet.enable_page_index", true)
        .set_bool("datafusion.execution.parquet.bloom_filter_on_read", true)
        .set_bool("datafusion.optimizer.enable_dynamic_filter_pushdown", true)
        .set_str("datafusion.sql_parser.dialect", "generic")
        .set_usize("datafusion.sql_parser.recursion_limit", 50);

    let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
        .with_memory_limit(8 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024, 0.80)
        .with_temp_file_path("/mnt/fast-ssd/datafusion")
        .with_max_temp_directory_size(100 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)
        .build_arc()?;

    let state = SessionStateBuilder::new()
        .with_config(config)
        .with_runtime_env(runtime)
        .with_default_features()
        .build();

    Ok(SessionContext::from(state))
}
```

This pattern separates session/planning settings from runtime resource settings. The docs identify `SessionConfig` as the configuration object for `SessionContext`, and `RuntimeEnv` as the execution environment for object stores, memory manager, and disk manager. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 27.25 Testing matrix

```text
[ ] Rust SessionConfig values visible through SHOW
[ ] env vars applied through from_env at startup
[ ] invalid env var values fall back or error as expected
[ ] SQL SET changes option in same session
[ ] SQL RESET restores default
[ ] statements disabled for read-only SQL endpoint
[ ] target_partitions visible in EXPLAIN partition counts
[ ] batch_size affects output/intermediate batch behavior enough for tests
[ ] time_zone fixed in date/time function tests
[ ] Parquet pruning/page-index/filter flags covered by EXPLAIN ANALYZE tests
[ ] runtime memory_limit tested with spill-heavy query
[ ] temp_directory exists, writable, has capacity
[ ] metadata/list-files cache TTL tested on mutable prefixes
[ ] formatting settings pinned in snapshot tests
```

---

## 27.26 Anti-pattern inventory

* Relying on default timezone in services.
* Letting public SQL users run arbitrary `SET`.
* Setting `target_partitions` high for tiny data.
* Setting `target_partitions` high under tight memory and then blaming spilling.
* Enabling experimental optimizer flags globally without workload tests.
* Enabling Parquet `pushdown_filters` globally without benchmarking.
* Treating formatting settings as data-serialization contracts.
* Putting spill temp directory on a slow or full filesystem.
* Leaving list-files cache TTL unlimited for mutable object-store prefixes.
* Assuming environment variables update existing contexts.
* Mixing Rust config, env config, and SQL `SET` without precedence documentation.
* Disabling Parquet page index/pruning without compatibility reason.
* Forgetting that runtime memory and temp-directory settings are resource policy, not only performance settings.

---

## 27.27 Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Choose config surface: Rust / env / SQL.
[ ] Use SessionConfig for session/planning/execution defaults.
[ ] Use ConfigOptions::from_env for deployment overrides.
[ ] Use RuntimeEnvBuilder for memory/temp/cache/object-store resource domains.
[ ] Use SQL SET only when session-level user tuning is allowed.
[ ] Disable SQL statements for read-only/public SQL.
[ ] Set batch_size deliberately.
[ ] Set target_partitions deliberately.
[ ] Set time_zone explicitly.
[ ] Keep Parquet pruning/page-index/bloom reads enabled unless tested otherwise.
[ ] Benchmark Parquet pushdown_filters/reorder_filters before enabling.
[ ] Tune optimizer flags with EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE evidence.
[ ] Set parser dialect explicitly for product SQL.
[ ] Pin formatting settings in snapshot tests.
[ ] Set runtime memory_limit and temp_directory in services.
[ ] Size metadata/list-files/statistics caches for remote datasets.
[ ] Use SHOW ALL to capture final effective config.
```

## 27.28 New configuration options in DataFusion 54

Crate-verified list of configuration keys that are **new in the 54 line** (all keys take the `datafusion.` prefix in SQL `SET` statements):

| Key | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `execution.sort_pushdown_buffer_capacity` | `1073741824` (1 GiB) | capacity of the `BufferExec` inserted when sort pushdown removes a `SortExec` under a merge; lets the scan run ahead of the merge (respects the memory pool) |
| `execution.hash_join_buffering_capacity` | `0` | bytes of probe-side input a hash join may buffer while the build side materializes (`0` = off; can degrade dynamic-filter effectiveness) |
| `execution.parquet.coerce_int96_tz` | `NULL` | optional timezone applied to coerced INT96 Parquet timestamps (§15.33) |
| `execution.parquet.content_defined_chunking.enabled` | `false` | experimental CDC Parquet writer page-splitting (disables parallel writes) |
| `execution.parquet.content_defined_chunking.min_chunk_size` | `262144` (256 KiB) | CDC minimum chunk size |
| `execution.parquet.content_defined_chunking.max_chunk_size` | `1048576` (1 MiB) | CDC maximum chunk size |
| `execution.parquet.content_defined_chunking.norm_level` | `0` | CDC normalization level (recommended range [-3, 3]) |
| `optimizer.enable_window_topn` | `false` | opt-in window-function Top-N rewrite (§22.29) |
| `optimizer.enable_topk_repartition` | `true` | parallel partial Top-K below the final merge (§22.29) |
| `optimizer.enable_physical_uncorrelated_scalar_subquery` | `true` | physical one-shot execution of uncorrelated scalar subqueries (§20.27) |
| `optimizer.join_reordering` | `true` | statistics-informed join-order selection (§22.29) |
| `optimizer.use_statistics_registry` | `false` | opt-in registry-backed planning statistics (experimental, §22.29) |
| `optimizer.enable_unions_to_filter` | `false` | opt-in `UnionsToFilter` rewrite (§22.29) |
| `sql_parser.enable_subquery_sort_elimination` | `true` | strip irrelevant `ORDER BY` inside subqueries/CTEs |
| `explain.analyze_categories` | `all` | metric categories `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` renders: comma-separated `rows`/`bytes`/`timing`/`uncategorized`, or `none`/`all` |
| CSV `format.quote_style` (CsvOptions) | `necessary` | CSV writer quoting policy: `always`/`necessary`/`non_numeric`/`never` |
| CSV `format.ignore_leading_whitespace` (CsvOptions) | `NULL` | CSV reader: strip leading whitespace in fields |
| CSV `format.ignore_trailing_whitespace` (CsvOptions) | `NULL` | CSV reader: strip trailing whitespace in fields |
| `runtime.file_statistics_cache_limit` | `20M` | memory limit for the CacheManager-owned file-statistics cache (§27.18) |

Explicitly **not** new in 54 — these pre-date it and must not be treated as part of the 53→54 delta: the four `*_dynamic_filter_pushdown` keys, `execution.split_file_groups_by_statistics`, and `execution.spill_compression`. Also note there is **no** `execution.enable_file_stream_work_stealing` key in 54.1.0 (§21.25).

```sql
-- representative usage
SET datafusion.optimizer.enable_window_topn = true;
SET datafusion.runtime.file_statistics_cache_limit = '128M';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.coerce_int96_tz = 'UTC';
```

Agent rules:

```text
Treat this table as the authoritative 54-new key list; do not resurrect phantom keys.
Opt-in keys (enable_window_topn, enable_unions_to_filter, use_statistics_registry,
  hash_join_buffering_capacity, content_defined_chunking.enabled) need plan/behavior tests before production.
Size-valued keys accept K/M/G suffixes in SQL SET form.
```

# DataFusion Advanced — 28) Memory management and spilling

## 28.0 Production-safety mental model

```text id="hqawzy"
SessionContext
  └─ SessionState
      └─ RuntimeEnv
          ├─ MemoryPool
          │   ├─ UnboundedMemoryPool
          │   ├─ GreedyMemoryPool
          │   ├─ FairSpillPool
          │   └─ TrackConsumersPool<...>
          ├─ DiskManager
          │   └─ spill/temp files
          ├─ CacheManager
          └─ ObjectStoreRegistry

ExecutionPlan::execute(partition, TaskContext)
  └─ operator stream
      ├─ MemoryConsumer
      │   └─ MemoryReservation(s)
      ├─ spillable buffers / hash tables / sort runs
      └─ optional spill files via DiskManager
```

DataFusion is a streaming engine, so many operators process one `RecordBatch` at a time, but large-state operators such as sorting, grouping, and joining can require memory proportional to input rows. DataFusion’s memory model intentionally tracks “large” operator state through `MemoryPool`, `MemoryConsumer`, and `MemoryReservation`, while not trying to account every small transient allocation or the normal `RecordBatch` values flowing between operators. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 28.1 Value case

| Risk                                   | DataFusion control                                               |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| process OOM from sort/group/join state | limited `MemoryPool`                                             |
| one operator monopolizes memory        | `FairSpillPool` for spillable operators                          |
| bad OOM diagnostics                    | `TrackConsumersPool` top consumers                               |
| disk exhaustion from spill             | `datafusion.runtime.max_temp_directory_size`                     |
| unknown spill location                 | `datafusion.runtime.temp_directory` / `with_temp_file_path`      |
| oversized spill files                  | `datafusion.execution.max_spill_file_size_bytes` where supported |
| spill disk bloat                       | `datafusion.execution.spill_compression`                         |
| custom operator leaks                  | `MemoryReservation` RAII drop behavior                           |
| concurrent-service instability         | explicit `RuntimeEnv` per resource domain                        |

The current runtime settings expose `datafusion.runtime.memory_limit`, `datafusion.runtime.temp_directory`, and `datafusion.runtime.max_temp_directory_size`; the docs show `memory_limit` defaulting to `NULL`, `temp_directory` defaulting to `NULL`, and `max_temp_directory_size` defaulting to `100G`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 28.2 What DataFusion does and does not track

```text id="t65z8q"
Tracked:
  large operator state
  hash aggregation state
  sort buffers/runs
  spillable reservations
  custom operator buffers when registered
  some join/sort/group intermediate structures

Not fully tracked:
  all Rust allocations
  all Arrow buffers produced transiently
  all DataSourceExec internals
  every RecordBatch flowing between operators
  arbitrary memory used by custom code unless it uses reservations
```

The `MemoryPool` docs state that DataFusion does **not** track and limit all memory: it tracks large memory consumers, while small intermediate memory and batches flowing between operators are assumed to be relatively small; the docs recommend reserving overhead, for example 10%, when configuring a limited pool. ([Docs.rs][1])

Agent rule:

```text id="j1j0pb"
memory_limit is a safety rail, not a complete process RSS cap.
For production services, combine:
  memory pool limit
  temp disk limit
  concurrency/admission control
  OS/container memory limit
  query timeout/result limits
```

---

## 28.3 `MemoryPool`

### Trait role

```rust id="0usloy"
pub trait MemoryPool: Any + Send + Sync + Debug + Display {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;

    fn grow(&self, reservation: &MemoryReservation, additional: usize);
    fn shrink(&self, reservation: &MemoryReservation, shrink: usize);
    fn try_grow(
        &self,
        reservation: &MemoryReservation,
        additional: usize,
    ) -> Result<(), DataFusionError>;
    fn reserved(&self) -> usize;

    fn register(&self, consumer: &MemoryConsumer) { ... }
    fn unregister(&self, consumer: &MemoryConsumer) { ... }
    fn memory_limit(&self) -> MemoryLimit { ... }
}
```

`MemoryPool` tracks and potentially limits memory use across execution operators. Its main operations grow, shrink, try-grow, report reserved memory, and register/unregister memory consumers. `try_grow` is the safe growth method because it returns an error if the limited pool has insufficient capacity. In DataFusion 54 the trait gained `Any` and `Display` supertraits plus a required `name()` method: `Any` makes the trait object effectively `'static`, so a custom pool must own its state (hold `Arc`s rather than borrowed references), and `Display` must render a human-readable pool description for diagnostics. ([Docs.rs][3])

### Pool types

| Pool                    | Behavior                                                  | Use                                                         |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `UnboundedMemoryPool`   | no memory limit                                           | tests, trusted local scripts, default if no pool configured |
| `GreedyMemoryPool`      | fixed limit, first-come-first-served                      | general limited memory, one main spillable operator         |
| `FairSpillPool`         | fixed limit, fair allocation among spillable reservations | multiple spillable operators/partitions likely to spill     |
| `TrackConsumersPool<I>` | wrapper around another pool, tracks top memory consumers  | better OOM diagnostics                                      |

DataFusion docs list `UnboundedMemoryPool` as the default when no pool is configured, `GreedyMemoryPool` as fixed-size first-come-first-served, `FairSpillPool` as fixed-size fair allocation for spillable reservations, and `TrackConsumersPool` as a wrapper that reports largest memory consumers. ([Docs.rs][3])

---

## 28.4 Unbounded vs limited pools

### Unbounded

```rust id="kog413"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::execution::memory_pool::UnboundedMemoryPool;
use datafusion::execution::runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder;

let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_memory_pool(Arc::new(UnboundedMemoryPool::default()))
    .build_arc()?;
```

Use only when the host/container has independent resource enforcement or when data/query size is known and bounded.

### Limited greedy

```rust id="pc6rhe"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::execution::memory_pool::GreedyMemoryPool;
use datafusion::execution::runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder;

let pool_size = 8 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024usize;

let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_memory_pool(Arc::new(GreedyMemoryPool::new(pool_size)))
    .build_arc()?;
```

### Limited via builder convenience

```rust id="g6pbgm"
let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_memory_limit(8 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024, 0.80)
    .build_arc()?;
```

`RuntimeEnvBuilder::with_memory_limit(max_memory, memory_fraction)` sets total DataFusion plan memory to `max_memory * memory_fraction`, defaulting to a `GreedyMemoryPool` wrapped in `TrackConsumersPool` with top 5 consumer reporting; its docs also warn that DataFusion does not yet respect this limit in all cases. ([Docs.rs][4])

Agent rules:

```text id="wrzv9e"
Local experiments:
  unbounded acceptable.

Production service:
  limited pool mandatory.

Multi-tenant:
  separate RuntimeEnv per tenant/resource class if isolation matters.

Memory_fraction:
  leave headroom for untracked allocations, Arrow buffers, runtime, application, OS page cache.
```

---

## 28.5 Greedy vs fair spill policy

### `GreedyMemoryPool`

```rust id="6qgz3t"
let pool = GreedyMemoryPool::new(4 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024);
```

`GreedyMemoryPool` is a fixed-limit, first-come-first-served pool. Its docs say it works well for queries that do not need to spill or have a single spillable operator, and recommend `FairSpillPool` when multiple spillable operators are likely to spill. ([Docs.rs][5])

### `FairSpillPool`

```rust id="j2363y"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::execution::memory_pool::FairSpillPool;

let pool = Arc::new(FairSpillPool::new(4 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024));
```

`FairSpillPool` prevents spillable reservations from using more than an even fraction of available memory after unspillable memory is accounted for; docs note it works best when multiple spillable operators will likely need to spill, but it may cause spills even where enough memory existed if reserved for other operators. ([Docs.rs][6])

### Decision matrix

| Workload                                 | Preferred pool                                                                |       |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| one big sort                             | `GreedyMemoryPool`                                                            |       |
| one big hash/group state                 | `GreedyMemoryPool`                                                            |       |
| many concurrent spillable partitions     | `FairSpillPool`                                                               |       |
| mixed query service with OOM diagnostics | `TrackConsumersPool<GreedyMemoryPool>` or `TrackConsumersPool<FairSpillPool>` |       |
| CLI quick limit                          | CLI `--memory-limit` + `--mem-pool-type greedy                                | fair` |

The CLI exposes `--memory-limit`, `--mem-pool-type greedy|fair`, and `--top-memory-consumers`, so the same policy choice can be tested interactively. ([Apache DataFusion][7])

---

## 28.6 `TrackConsumersPool`

```rust id="dqk186"
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
use datafusion::execution::memory_pool::{
    GreedyMemoryPool,
    TrackConsumersPool,
};

let tracked = TrackConsumersPool::new(
    GreedyMemoryPool::new(1024 * 1024 * 1024),
    NonZeroUsize::new(5).unwrap(),
);
```

`TrackConsumersPool` wraps another `MemoryPool`, tracks memory consumers, and improves `ResourcesExhausted` diagnostics by reporting the top memory consumers; docs say the easiest way to get it is `RuntimeEnvBuilder::with_memory_limit`, which automatically sets tracking with sensible defaults. ([Docs.rs][8])

Agent rules:

```text id="6lbljs"
Always enable top-consumer tracking in services.
Use reported consumer names to locate operator / custom node memory use.
Name custom MemoryConsumers clearly:
  "MyExec[partition=3].hash_table"
  "RemoteApiBuffer[tenant=x]"
Avoid generic names like "buffer".
```

---

## 28.7 `MemoryConsumer` and `MemoryReservation`

### Consumer

```rust id="k7v066"
use datafusion::execution::memory_pool::MemoryConsumer;

let consumer = MemoryConsumer::new("MyOperatorBuffer".to_string())
    .with_can_spill(true);
```

`MemoryConsumer` is a named allocation source registered with a `MemoryPool`. It can be marked as spillable with `with_can_spill`, and `register(pool)` returns a `MemoryReservation` that can grow or shrink memory tracked for that consumer. ([Docs.rs][9])

### Reservation

```rust id="l9p6m3"
let mut reservation = MemoryConsumer::new("MyHashTable".to_string())
    .with_can_spill(true)
    .register(context.memory_pool());

reservation.try_grow(bytes_needed)?;

// allocate / buffer / build state

reservation.shrink(bytes_freed);
```

`MemoryReservation` tracks a number of bytes in a `MemoryPool`, is freed back to the pool on drop, and can grow, shrink, resize, split, and try-grow. `try_grow` returns an error if insufficient capacity remains in the pool. ([Docs.rs][10])

### RAII split pattern

```rust id="xpxm68"
reservation.try_grow(estimated_bytes)?;

// Transfer ownership of a sub-reservation to a buffered structure.
// When that structure drops, its reservation drops too.
let batch_reservation = reservation.split(estimated_bytes);
let buffered = BufferedBatch {
    batch,
    reservation: batch_reservation,
};
```

### Agent rules

```text id="a1zl9d"
Register every large custom operator allocation.
Use try_grow before allocation.
Use shrink/drop immediately after freeing buffers.
Use split/take to tie memory lifetime to buffer lifetime.
Mark consumers spillable only if the operator can actually spill/recover.
Do not reserve memory for normal output batches flowing downstream.
```

---

## 28.8 Runtime memory + spill directory configuration

### Rust

```rust id="p2wxqc"
use datafusion::execution::{
    runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder,
    session_state::SessionStateBuilder,
};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .with_batch_size(8192)
    .with_target_partitions(8);

let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_memory_limit(16 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024, 0.80)
    .with_temp_file_path("/mnt/nvme/datafusion-spill")
    .with_max_temp_directory_size(500 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)
    .build_arc()?;

let state = SessionStateBuilder::new()
    .with_config(config)
    .with_runtime_env(runtime)
    .with_default_features()
    .build();

let ctx = SessionContext::from(state);
```

`RuntimeEnvBuilder` supports `with_memory_limit`, `with_temp_file_path`, and `with_max_temp_directory_size`, and its fields include the disk manager, memory pool, cache manager, and object-store registry. The builder docs state the memory pool defaults to `UnboundedMemoryPool` when no pool is configured. ([Docs.rs][4])

### SQL

```sql id="41n4m8"
SET datafusion.runtime.memory_limit = '16G';
SET datafusion.runtime.temp_directory = '/mnt/nvme/datafusion-spill';
SET datafusion.runtime.max_temp_directory_size = '500G';
```

Runtime config docs state these settings can be set via SQL `SET`; size values support `K`, `M`, and `G` suffixes or `0`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### CLI

```bash id="25j6lw"
datafusion-cli \
  --memory-limit 16g \
  --mem-pool-type fair \
  --top-memory-consumers 5 \
  --disk-limit 500g
```

The CLI exposes memory limit, pool type (`greedy` or `fair`), top memory consumers, and disk limit for spilling queries. ([Apache DataFusion][7])

---

## 28.9 `DiskManager` and spill directory

`DiskManager` manages files generated during query execution, such as spill files created while processing datasets larger than available memory. The execution module lists it as the runtime component responsible for execution-generated files. ([Docs.rs][11])

### Builder surface

```rust id="cu5l94"
use datafusion::execution::disk_manager::DiskManager;

let disk_manager = DiskManager::builder()
    .with_max_temp_directory_size(500 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)
    .build()?;
```

`DiskManagerBuilder` supports `with_mode`, `set_mode`, `with_max_temp_directory_size`, and `set_max_temp_directory_size`; `RuntimeEnvBuilder::with_temp_file_path` is the common high-level way to set where temporary files are created. ([Docs.rs][12])

### Agent rules

```text id="slw7u9"
Use a fast local SSD/NVMe path for spill.
Do not use a slow shared network filesystem unless benchmarked.
Set max_temp_directory_size to prevent disk exhaustion.
Ensure directory exists, is writable, and has correct ownership.
Monitor disk free space outside DataFusion too.
Clean up orphaned spill dirs on process crash via deployment tooling.
```

---

## 28.10 Spill compression

```sql id="656i7k"
SET datafusion.execution.spill_compression = 'uncompressed';
SET datafusion.execution.spill_compression = 'lz4_frame';
SET datafusion.execution.spill_compression = 'zstd';
```

`datafusion.execution.spill_compression` controls compression for spill data written to disk using Arrow IPC Stream format. Valid values are `uncompressed`, `lz4_frame`, and `zstd`; the docs say `lz4_frame` is faster but usually larger, while `zstd` compresses better but costs more CPU. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Policy table

| Spill compression | Use                                                             |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `uncompressed`    | CPU-bound queries, fast/ample local disk                        |
| `lz4_frame`       | balanced default for disk pressure with low CPU overhead        |
| `zstd`            | disk-space or remote/slow-disk pressure; CPU headroom available |

Compressed spill files were introduced for larger-than-memory sorting and grouping; the DataFusion 49 release notes state compressed spill files can reduce intermediate file size and improve performance when reading them back, with CPU/codec tradeoffs. ([Apache DataFusion][13])

---

## 28.11 Max spill file size

```sql id="pwgl9z"
SET datafusion.execution.max_spill_file_size_bytes = '134217728';
```

`datafusion.execution.max_spill_file_size_bytes` defaults to `134217728` bytes. The config docs say operators rotate to a new spill file when this limit is reached to reduce syscall overhead while avoiding very large spill files; currently only `RepartitionExec` supports this spill file rotation feature, so other spilling operators may create spill files larger than the limit. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text id="6h4awv"
Larger spill files:
  fewer files/syscalls
  slower/fewer opportunities for space reclamation

Smaller spill files:
  more files/syscalls
  finer-grained cleanup
  more metadata overhead

Do not assume max_spill_file_size_bytes applies to all operators.
```

---

## 28.12 Sort spilling

### Relevant configs

```sql id="ikxtwk"
SET datafusion.execution.sort_spill_reservation_bytes = '10485760';
SET datafusion.execution.sort_in_place_threshold_bytes = '1048576';
SET datafusion.execution.spill_compression = 'lz4_frame';
```

`sort_spill_reservation_bytes` defaults to `10 MiB` and reserves memory for each spillable sort operation to merge/sort data before writing a spill file; the setting is irrelevant if the sort cannot spill because no `DiskManager` is configured. `sort_in_place_threshold_bytes` defaults to `1 MiB` and controls when sort data is concatenated and sorted in a single `RecordBatch` rather than sorted in batches and merged. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Sort pressure patterns

```text id="itprm9"
ORDER BY huge_table
ORDER BY many wide columns
ORDER BY expression requiring materialization
ORDER BY ... LIMIT N without TopK optimization
global sort after high-cardinality join
```

### Agent rules

```text id="w2dj1v"
Use ORDER BY only when semantically required.
Use ORDER BY + LIMIT for TopK-friendly plans.
Project narrow columns before sort.
Filter before sort.
Set spill directory and memory limit for production sorts.
Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to identify SortExec row counts and spill behavior.
```

---

## 28.13 Group-by / aggregation spilling

Group-by hash aggregation can require state proportional to the number of groups and aggregate-state size. DataFusion’s configuration docs state that under a tight memory limit, DataFusion spills intermediate results to disk; release notes specifically mention compressed spill files for sorting and grouping. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Group pressure patterns

```text id="lh3rcw"
GROUP BY high-cardinality user_id/session_id/request_id
COUNT DISTINCT / array_agg / string_agg large values
many aggregate expressions
wide grouping keys
poor pre-filtering
target_partitions too high under tight memory
```

### Mitigation

```sql id="qs2m6p"
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '4';
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '1024';
SET datafusion.execution.spill_compression = 'lz4_frame';
```

The tuning guide notes that with `FairSpillPool`, memory is divided evenly among partitions, so higher `target_partitions` gives each partition less memory and may trigger out-of-core paths more frequently. It also recommends reducing `target_partitions` and `batch_size` for memory-limited queries. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text id="tc7b1z"
Pre-filter before GROUP BY.
Avoid grouping by unbounded high-cardinality IDs unless needed.
Approximate or pre-aggregate if product semantics allow.
Lower target_partitions when per-partition memory is too small.
Use lz4/zstd spill compression when disk is bottleneck.
```

---

## 28.14 Join memory and spilling

### Hash join

Hash join memory is dominated by build-side hash tables and buffered probe data. DataFusion configuration includes several hash-join-related settings, including hash join buffering, join input reordering, hash join single-partition thresholds, and dynamic InList pushdown thresholds. The config docs also note that `prefer_hash_join=true` favors hash join for speed when sufficient memory is available, while `false` allows sort-merge join when more memory-efficient execution is needed. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```sql id="pokgo5"
SET datafusion.optimizer.prefer_hash_join = 'false';
```

### Sort-merge join

Sort-merge join can be preferable under memory pressure because it avoids building a large hash table, but it may require sorted inputs and can spill sort/buffered runs. The configuration docs explicitly contrast hash join speed with sort-merge join memory efficiency through `prefer_hash_join`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Symmetric hash join / streaming join

```sql id="llac43"
SET datafusion.optimizer.allow_symmetric_joins_without_pruning = 'false';
```

`allow_symmetric_joins_without_pruning` controls whether symmetric hash joins are allowed for unbounded data sources when inputs lack ordering/filtering; the docs warn that without pruning, some join types may only produce output at the end and are not typical stream-processing behavior. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Agent rules

```text id="ux8ofl"
Hash join:
  keep build side small.
  project/filter before join.
  expose stats so optimizer can swap sides.
  consider prefer_hash_join=false under memory pressure.

Sort-merge join:
  prefer when inputs are sorted or memory is tight.
  configure spill directory.

Streaming joins:
  require pruning/window constraints.
  avoid unbounded state.
```

---

## 28.15 Target partitions vs memory pressure

```sql id="xs8g53"
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '1';
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '4';
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '32';
```

More partitions increase CPU/I/O parallelism but divide memory among more operator partitions. The tuning guide says DataFusion defaults toward maximum parallelism, but for very small data `target_partitions=1` reduces repartition overhead, and for memory-limited queries lower `target_partitions` can avoid triggering out-of-core execution too frequently. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Policy:

```text id="rw4ffq"
If OOM:
  lower target_partitions
  lower batch_size
  reduce concurrent queries
  filter/project earlier
  prefer sort-merge over hash join if appropriate

If CPU idle and no spilling:
  increase target_partitions
```

---

## 28.16 Batch size vs memory pressure

```sql id="5o8qjp"
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '1024';
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '8192';
```

Batch size affects per-batch memory, spill-merge behavior, and operator overhead. The config docs state `batch_size` defaults to `8192`, and the tuning guide recommends reducing batch size for memory-limited queries because spill-related merge operations use batch-size-shaped buffers. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text id="4codpa"
Large batch:
  fewer batches
  higher throughput
  more per-batch memory

Small batch:
  lower per-batch memory
  more overhead
  can help tight memory/spill-heavy queries
```

---

## 28.17 Custom operator memory accounting

### Pattern

```rust id="i64dmb"
use datafusion::execution::memory_pool::{MemoryConsumer, MemoryReservation};
use datafusion::execution::TaskContext;

struct BufferedState {
    batches: Vec<RecordBatch>,
    reservation: MemoryReservation,
}

fn new_reservation(context: &TaskContext, name: &str) -> MemoryReservation {
    MemoryConsumer::new(name.to_string())
        .with_can_spill(true)
        .register(context.memory_pool())
}

fn buffer_batch(
    state: &mut BufferedState,
    batch: RecordBatch,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let bytes = batch.get_array_memory_size();

    state.reservation.try_grow(bytes)?;
    state.batches.push(batch);

    Ok(())
}

fn release_one(state: &mut BufferedState) {
    if let Some(batch) = state.batches.pop() {
        let bytes = batch.get_array_memory_size();
        drop(batch);
        state.reservation.shrink(bytes);
    }
}
```

`MemoryConsumer::register(pool)` returns a `MemoryReservation`; reservations can grow, shrink, resize, split, and are freed back to the pool when dropped. `MemoryConsumer::with_can_spill(true)` marks the allocation as spillable. ([Docs.rs][10])

### Agent rules

```text id="ctqzel"
Custom ExecutionPlan that buffers:
  MUST register MemoryConsumer.
  MUST use try_grow before allocation.
  MUST shrink/drop on release.
  SHOULD use with_can_spill(true) only if spill implemented.
  SHOULD expose metrics for buffered rows/bytes/spill bytes.
```

## 28.18 Diagnosing OOM

### First signals

```text id="o7wmw2"
DataFusionError::ResourcesExhausted
TrackConsumersPool top consumers
EXPLAIN ANALYZE operator row counts
large SortExec / AggregateExec / HashJoinExec
spill directory growth
container OOMKilled
OS disk-full errors
```

### CLI diagnostics

```bash id="5cwr7x"
datafusion-cli \
  --memory-limit 4g \
  --mem-pool-type fair \
  --top-memory-consumers 10 \
  --disk-limit 100g
```

CLI flags can limit memory, choose greedy/fair memory-pool type, display top memory consumers on memory exhaustion, and set available disk space for spilling queries. ([Apache DataFusion][7])

### SQL diagnostics

```sql id="eapg0y"
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT ...
```

### Rust diagnostics

```rust id="c5fl50"
let runtime = ctx.runtime_env();
let reserved = runtime.memory_pool.reserved();
eprintln!("reserved_bytes={reserved}");
```

### Agent diagnosis workflow

```text id="24vdx7"
1. Reproduce with memory_limit and top-consumer tracking.
2. Run EXPLAIN to identify candidate operators.
3. Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on bounded sample if full query is too expensive.
4. Check top memory consumers.
5. Check spill directory growth and disk limit errors.
6. Lower target_partitions and batch_size.
7. Add projection/filter before high-state operators.
8. Consider join algorithm/config changes.
9. Increase memory or temp disk only after plan-shape fixes.
```

---

## 28.19 Diagnosing spill-heavy workloads

### Symptoms

```text id="7d4g2z"
query finishes but much slower than expected
spill directory grows rapidly
high disk read/write throughput
low CPU utilization, high I/O wait
many temporary spill files
EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows heavy sort/group/join operator time
```

### Likely causes

```text id="e5z4qz"
memory_limit too low
target_partitions too high
batch_size too high for spill merge buffers
global sort on huge data
high-cardinality GROUP BY
large hash join build side
wide rows before sort/join/group
slow spill disk
spill compression too CPU-heavy or not used when disk-bound
```

### Mitigation matrix

| Symptom                        | Mitigation                                                                      |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| many spills per partition      | increase memory, lower partitions, reduce row width                             |
| disk full                      | increase `max_temp_directory_size`, use compression, reduce intermediate volume |
| CPU idle / I/O wait            | use `lz4_frame`/`zstd`, faster disk, reduce spill volume                        |
| CPU saturated from compression | use `uncompressed` or `lz4_frame`                                               |
| hash join memory               | smaller build side, stats, projection, `prefer_hash_join=false`                 |
| sort spills                    | TopK, filter/project earlier, sort fewer columns, increase memory               |
| group spills                   | pre-aggregate, lower cardinality, reduce grouping key width                     |

---

## 28.20 Spill safety profile

### SQL profile

```sql id="ygcxqj"
SET datafusion.runtime.memory_limit = '16G';
SET datafusion.runtime.temp_directory = '/mnt/nvme/datafusion-spill';
SET datafusion.runtime.max_temp_directory_size = '500G';

SET datafusion.execution.spill_compression = 'lz4_frame';
SET datafusion.execution.max_spill_file_size_bytes = '134217728';
SET datafusion.execution.sort_spill_reservation_bytes = '10485760';

SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '8';
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '4096';
```

### Rust profile

```rust id="agky7u"
use datafusion::execution::{
    memory_pool::{FairSpillPool, TrackConsumersPool},
    runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder,
    session_state::SessionStateBuilder,
};
use std::{num::NonZeroUsize, sync::Arc};

let pool = TrackConsumersPool::new(
    FairSpillPool::new(16 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024),
    NonZeroUsize::new(10).unwrap(),
);

let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_memory_pool(Arc::new(pool))
    .with_temp_file_path("/mnt/nvme/datafusion-spill")
    .with_max_temp_directory_size(500 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)
    .build_arc()?;

let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .with_target_partitions(8)
    .with_batch_size(4096)
    .set_str("datafusion.execution.spill_compression", "lz4_frame");

let state = SessionStateBuilder::new()
    .with_config(config)
    .with_runtime_env(runtime)
    .with_default_features()
    .build();

let ctx = SessionContext::from(state);
```

Agent rules:

```text id="dwhrfl"
Use fair pool for multiple spillable operators/partitions.
Use greedy pool for simpler/one-main-operator workloads.
Use TrackConsumersPool in both cases.
Set disk directory and disk limit explicitly.
Set spill compression based on CPU-vs-disk bottleneck.
```

## 28.21 Query-shape mitigation patterns

### Sort-heavy

Bad:

```sql id="it52lw"
SELECT *
FROM huge_events
ORDER BY event_ts;
```

Better:

```sql id="arfwe2"
SELECT event_id, event_ts, user_id
FROM huge_events
WHERE event_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
ORDER BY event_ts DESC
LIMIT 1000;
```

### Group-heavy

Bad:

```sql id="ckha5r"
SELECT user_id, session_id, request_id, COUNT(*)
FROM huge_events
GROUP BY user_id, session_id, request_id;
```

Better:

```sql id="r5h22d"
SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM huge_events
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22'
GROUP BY user_id;
```

### Join-heavy

Bad:

```sql id="x600tr"
SELECT *
FROM huge_fact f
JOIN huge_dim d
  ON f.key = d.key;
```

Better:

```sql id="omb8ol"
SELECT f.key, f.metric, d.category
FROM huge_fact f
JOIN small_filtered_dim d
  ON f.key = d.key
WHERE d.active = true;
```

Agent rules:

```text id="5jopao"
Filter early.
Project narrow.
Avoid SELECT * before sort/join/group.
Prefer semi/anti for existence.
Prefer TopK over full sort where valid.
Use partition filters for lake tables.
```

---

## 28.26 Anti-pattern inventory

* Relying on `UnboundedMemoryPool` in a shared service.
* Treating `memory_limit` as a complete RSS cap.
* Setting memory limit equal to container memory with no overhead.
* Using high `target_partitions` under tight memory.
* Using large `batch_size` in spill-heavy queries.
* Marking custom consumers `can_spill=true` without implementing spill.
* Buffering custom operator state without `MemoryReservation`.
* Using slow network storage for spill.
* Leaving `max_temp_directory_size` unbounded or implicit.
* Ignoring top memory consumer diagnostics.
* Increasing memory before fixing `SELECT *`, missing filters, or bad join side.
* Using hash join for massive build sides when sort-merge is acceptable.
* Assuming `max_spill_file_size_bytes` applies to every spilling operator.
* Using `zstd` spill compression on CPU-bound workloads without benchmarking.
* Running public SQL with no admission/concurrency control.

## 28.28 Nested-loop join spilling (DataFusion 54)

DataFusion 54 closed the largest remaining "no spill path" gap: `NestedLoopJoinExec` now participates in memory-limited execution. The buffered build (left) side registers a `MemoryConsumer` against the pool; when `try_grow` fails, buffered build batches spill to disk through the `DiskManager`, and the probe phase streams them back in passes instead of aborting with `ResourcesExhausted`.

Prerequisites and mechanics:

* A memory-limited pool (`GreedyMemoryPool`/`FairSpillPool`, typically wrapped in `TrackConsumersPool`) and a configured `DiskManager` (`with_temp_file_path` or default temp dir; `max_temp_directory_size` bounds spill volume).
* Spill files use the Arrow IPC-based spill format and honor `datafusion.execution.spill_compression` (`uncompressed` / `lz4_frame` / `zstd`) — the compression key itself pre-dates 54.
* Changelog-reported coverage: inner/left and right/full join types.
* Under 53 and earlier the documented behavior was a hard OOM error when the build side exceeded the memory budget; capacity planning that relied on "NLJ fails fast" should now watch spill metrics (`spill_count`, `spilled_bytes`) and disk headroom instead.

```rust
use datafusion::execution::runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder;

let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_memory_limit(4 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024, 0.8)   // enables the spill path
    .with_temp_file_path("/mnt/ssd/df-spill")          // DiskManager target
    .build_arc()?;
```

Operator-level view of the join changes (SMJ deferred filtering, `RepartitionExec` coalescing): §23.29.

# DataFusion Advanced — 29) Performance tuning guide

## 29.0 Performance mental model

```text
Performance = build profile × query shape × file/layout quality × optimizer choices × runtime resources

Rust binary:
  --release
  target CPU / SIMD
  LTO / codegen units
  PGO
  allocator

Query plan:
  projection/filter/limit pushdown
  join algorithm and repartitioning
  aggregation cardinality
  sort/top-K shape
  dynamic filters

Data layout:
  Parquet statistics/page index/bloom filters
  partitioning
  file size / row group size
  column width
  small-file count
  object-store latency

Runtime:
  batch_size
  target_partitions
  memory pool
  spill directory
  object-store metadata/listing caches
  Tokio/runtime/thread-pool design
```

DataFusion is a columnar, streaming, multi-threaded, vectorized execution engine; the number of cores used is controlled by `datafusion.execution.target_partitions`, which defaults to the CPU core count, and DataFusion tries to create that many async streams for each `ExecutionPlan` during execution preparation. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 29.1 Always start with build profile

### Wrong benchmark

```bash
cargo run
```

### Baseline benchmark

```bash
cargo run --release
cargo build --release
```

### CPU-local optimized benchmark

```bash
RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native' cargo run --release
RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native' cargo build --release
```

DataFusion’s crate-configuration guide recommends CPU-specific code generation, preferably `target-cpu=native`, so the compiler can use CPU features such as AVX2/AVX512 for operations like filtering, aggregation, and joins. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Release profile: LTO / single codegen unit

```toml
[profile.release]
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
```

LTO plus a single codegen unit can improve performance by giving Rust more opportunity to optimize across crate boundaries, but significantly increases `--release` build time. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### PGO profile

```bash
# 1. Instrumented build
RUSTFLAGS="-C profile-generate=/tmp/pgo-data" cargo build --release

# 2. Run representative workloads
./target/release/your-datafusion-app --run-representative-queries

# 3. Optimized rebuild
RUSTFLAGS="-C profile-use=/tmp/pgo-data" cargo build --release
```

The DataFusion crate-configuration guide says profile-guided optimization can improve DataFusion performance by up to 25% when trained on representative workloads such as TPCH, ClickBench, or production queries. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Build-profile decision table

| Deployment                   | Build profile                           |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| local dev                    | `cargo check`, `cargo test`, debug OK   |
| performance benchmark        | `cargo run --release` minimum           |
| single-machine appliance     | `RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native'`      |
| homogeneous production fleet | `target-cpu=native` or fleet CPU target |
| heterogeneous binaries       | portable CPU target; avoid `native`     |
| latency-critical engine      | release + native + LTO + PGO            |
| CI smoke tests               | debug/test profile acceptable           |
| CI perf regression           | release + pinned CPU/profile            |

Agent rules:

```text
Never compare debug DataFusion timings.
Never use synthetic PGO training if production queries differ.
Do not ship target-cpu=native artifacts to unknown CPUs.
Keep one benchmark matrix:
  default release
  target-cpu=native
  LTO/codegen-units=1
  PGO
```

---

## 29.2 Primary runtime knobs

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '8192';
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '8';
SET datafusion.execution.coalesce_batches = 'true';
```

`batch_size` controls the default batch size while creating new batches, and `target_partitions` controls execution parallelism; the config tuning guide specifically recommends lowering `target_partitions` for very small datasets and lowering both `target_partitions` and `batch_size` under tight memory limits. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Rust

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .with_batch_size(8192)
    .with_target_partitions(num_cpus::get())
    .set_bool("datafusion.execution.coalesce_batches", true);

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);
```

### Tuning effect table

| Setting             | Increase helps                                              | Increase hurts                                            |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `batch_size`        | throughput, vectorization amortization, fewer batch objects | per-batch memory, latency, spill-merge buffers            |
| `target_partitions` | CPU parallelism, large scans, independent files             | small queries, memory per partition, repartition overhead |
| `coalesce_batches`  | small-batch overhead, downstream operator efficiency        | may add small amount of buffering                         |
| `memory_limit`      | safety/isolation when set lower                             | spills/OOM if too low                                     |
| `temp_directory`    | spill performance when fast/local                           | slow if remote/shared disk                                |

---

## 29.3 Small / short queries

### Problem

```text
Symptoms:
  query time dominated by planning, repartitioning, scheduling, file listing
  CPU mostly idle
  EXPLAIN shows many partitions for tiny input
  runtime slower than single-threaded expectation
```

DataFusion defaults toward parallelism, but the tuning guide says very small datasets can be slowed by partitioning/repartitioning overhead; for datasets under roughly 1 MB, it recommends `target_partitions = 1`. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### SQL profile

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '1';
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '1024';
```

### Rust profile

```rust
let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .with_target_partitions(1)
    .with_batch_size(1024);

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);
```

### Query-shape rules

```text
Use LIMIT for exploratory queries.
Avoid ORDER BY unless required.
Avoid DISTINCT unless required.
Avoid repartition-heavy joins/aggregations for tiny control-plane queries.
Prefer in-memory RecordBatch / MemTable for tiny fixtures.
```

### Diagnostics

```sql
EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM tiny_table LIMIT 10;
```

Inspect:

```text
number of partitions
RepartitionExec presence
CoalescePartitionsExec presence
file scan partitioning
sort/join/aggregate operators
```

Agent recommendation:

```text
Small query first fix:
  target_partitions=1

Second fixes:
  reduce batch_size
  use direct in-memory source
  remove unnecessary sort/distinct/join
  avoid remote file listing for tiny repeated calls
```

---

## 29.4 Large scans

### Problem

```text
Symptoms:
  high I/O
  high CPU if decoding/computing
  output row count large
  broad table scan
  many columns or wide rows
```

### Baseline profile

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '0';
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '8192';
SET datafusion.optimizer.repartition_file_scans = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.coalesce_batches = 'true';
```

`target_partitions = 0` resolves to the core-derived default, and DataFusion tries to create that many execution streams per plan during execution preparation. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Query-shape rules

```sql
-- Bad: wide full scan
SELECT *
FROM events;

-- Better: column pruning
SELECT event_id, event_ts, user_id
FROM events;

-- Better: filter pushdown candidate
SELECT event_id, event_ts, user_id
FROM events
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22';
```

### Agent rules

```text
Large scan checklist:
  project only needed columns
  filter early
  use partition columns
  prefer Parquet over CSV/JSON
  avoid row-materialization until final output
  use execute_stream for output
  tune target_partitions to CPU/I/O balance
```

### Diagnostics

```sql
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT event_id, event_ts
FROM events
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22';
```

Inspect:

```text
DataSourceExec rows/bytes
FilterExec presence or pushdown
ProjectionExec placement
RepartitionExec
operator elapsed time
output batch counts
```

---

## 29.5 Parquet-heavy analytics

### Read profile

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.pruning = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.enable_page_index = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.bloom_filter_on_read = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.pushdown_filters = 'false';
```

DataFusion’s Parquet source can use projection/predicate information to skip reading unnecessary data through row group pruning, page pruning via the Parquet PageIndex, and bloom filters when present. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Aggressive selective-scan profile

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.pruning = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.enable_page_index = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.bloom_filter_on_read = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.pushdown_filters = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.reorder_filters = 'true';
```

### Layout rules

```text
Good:
  Parquet
  directory root
  Hive partitions on common low-cardinality filters
  compatible schemas
  page statistics
  row group statistics
  bloom filters for lookup keys
  moderate/large files

Bad:
  CSV/JSON for repeated analytics
  wildcard paths
  mixed schemas
  high-cardinality partition dirs
  many tiny files
  no statistics
```

### Write profile for future reads

```sql
COPY (
  SELECT *
  FROM curated_input
)
TO 's3://bucket/curated/facts/'
STORED AS PARQUET
PARTITIONED BY (event_date, region)
OPTIONS (
  'compression' 'zstd(3)',
  'statistics_enabled' 'page',
  'max_row_group_size' '1048576',
  'bloom_filter_enabled::event_id' 'true',
  'bloom_filter_enabled::user_id' 'true'
);
```

Agent rules:

```text
Parquet read tuning:
  keep pruning/page-index/bloom reads enabled
  enable pushdown_filters only after benchmarking
  avoid SELECT *
  use direct predicates on physical columns
  avoid wrapping filter columns in functions

Parquet write tuning:
  write page statistics
  choose row group size deliberately
  choose compression deliberately
  add bloom filters only on high-value equality keys
```

---

## 29.6 Many small files

### Problem

```text
Symptoms:
  planning/listing time high
  metadata fetch dominates
  object store request count high
  DataSourceExec has many tiny partitions/files
  CPU underutilized or spends time in overhead
```

The config tuning source notes `datafusion.optimizer.repartition_file_min_size` controls the minimum file size at which `ListingTable` attempts repartitioning, but only when DataFusion has accurate statistics and only for listing-table sources. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Config profile

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.meta_fetch_concurrency = '32';
SET datafusion.runtime.metadata_cache_limit = '512M';
SET datafusion.runtime.list_files_cache_limit = '128M';
SET datafusion.runtime.list_files_cache_ttl = '5m';
SET datafusion.optimizer.repartition_file_scans = 'true';
```

### Mitigation hierarchy

```text
Best:
  compact files upstream
  write fewer/larger Parquet files
  use partition directories carefully

Good:
  metadata/listing cache
  increase meta_fetch_concurrency if object store allows it
  use directory roots, not wildcard paths
  prune by partition columns

Last resort:
  adjust repartition_file_min_size
  reduce target_partitions if scheduling overhead dominates
```

### Agent rules

```text
Many small files:
  fix data layout first
  cache metadata/listing for stable prefixes
  use partition filters
  avoid reading wide columns
  compact during ETL
```

---

## 29.7 Highly selective filters

### Good query shape

```sql
SELECT event_id, user_id, event_ts
FROM events
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22'
  AND user_id = 'u123';
```

### Bad query shape

```sql
SELECT *
FROM events
WHERE lower(user_id) = 'u123';
```

### Tuning profile

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.pruning = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.enable_page_index = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.bloom_filter_on_read = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.pushdown_filters = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.reorder_filters = 'true';

SET datafusion.optimizer.enable_dynamic_filter_pushdown = 'true';
SET datafusion.optimizer.enable_topk_dynamic_filter_pushdown = 'true';
SET datafusion.optimizer.enable_join_dynamic_filter_pushdown = 'true';
```

Dynamic filters are generated by operators such as TopK, Join, and Aggregate and pushed into scans; the configuration docs describe using runtime TopK state to skip files whose metadata cannot improve the current result. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Agent rules

```text
For selective filters:
  use direct column predicates
  filter partition columns
  avoid function-wrapped columns
  use equality / IN / range predicates
  write/read Parquet stats and bloom filters
  enable pushdown_filters only after benchmarking
```

---

## 29.8 Joins

### Default join profile

```sql
SET datafusion.optimizer.prefer_hash_join = 'true';
SET datafusion.optimizer.repartition_joins = 'true';
SET datafusion.optimizer.enable_join_dynamic_filter_pushdown = 'true';
```

### Memory-sensitive join profile

```sql
SET datafusion.optimizer.prefer_hash_join = 'false';
SET datafusion.optimizer.repartition_joins = 'true';
```

The configuration docs say `prefer_hash_join=true` favors hash joins for speed when there is sufficient memory, while disabling it allows sort-merge joins when more memory-efficient execution is needed. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Query-shape rules

```sql
-- Existence: prefer SEMI
SELECT *
FROM customers c
LEFT SEMI JOIN orders o
  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

-- Non-existence: prefer ANTI
SELECT *
FROM customers c
LEFT ANTI JOIN orders o
  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

-- Avoid function-wrapped keys
SELECT *
FROM a
JOIN b
  ON a.email_norm = b.email_norm;
```

### Tuning table

| Symptom                   | Likely cause                     | Fix                                                             |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| hash join OOM             | build side too large             | stats, smaller build side, projection, `prefer_hash_join=false` |
| slow nested loop          | no equijoin key                  | add equality key, enable/test piecewise merge for range         |
| too much shuffle          | repartition joins with tiny data | reduce target partitions, disable repartition if measured       |
| skew                      | hot join key                     | pre-aggregate, salting, different layout                        |
| dynamic filter no benefit | source cannot prune              | use Parquet stats/partitions or custom source index             |

### Agent rules

```text
Joins:
  expose equality keys plainly
  filter/project before join
  use SEMI/ANTI for existence
  avoid NATURAL/CROSS unless explicit
  inspect EXPLAIN for HashJoinExec / SortMergeJoinExec / NestedLoopJoinExec
  configure memory + spill path
```

---

## 29.9 Aggregations

### Problem

```text
Memory driven by:
  number of groups
  width of grouping keys
  aggregate state size
  target_partitions
  input row count
```

### Query-shape rules

```sql
-- Bad: high-cardinality wide group
SELECT user_id, session_id, request_id, array_agg(payload)
FROM events
GROUP BY user_id, session_id, request_id;

-- Better: filter and aggregate narrower
SELECT user_id, count(*) AS n
FROM events
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22'
GROUP BY user_id;
```

### Tuning profile

```sql
SET datafusion.optimizer.repartition_aggregations = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '8';
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '8192';
```

### Memory-limited aggregation profile

```sql
SET datafusion.runtime.memory_limit = '8G';
SET datafusion.runtime.temp_directory = '/mnt/nvme/datafusion-spill';
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '4';
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '1024';
SET datafusion.execution.spill_compression = 'lz4_frame';
```

The tuning guide recommends reducing `target_partitions` and `batch_size` under tight memory limits because higher partition counts divide memory more thinly and larger batch sizes can increase spill-merge pressure. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Agent rules

```text
Aggregation:
  filter early
  project grouping keys and aggregate args only
  avoid high-cardinality GROUP BY unless required
  use approximate aggregates if product semantics allow
  configure spill path for large group-by workloads
  inspect group count and spill metrics
```

---

## 29.10 Top-K / `ORDER BY ... LIMIT`

### Preferred shape

```sql
SELECT event_id, event_ts, score
FROM events
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22'
ORDER BY score DESC, event_id ASC
LIMIT 100;
```

### Tuning profile

```sql
SET datafusion.optimizer.enable_topk_repartition = 'true';
SET datafusion.optimizer.enable_topk_dynamic_filter_pushdown = 'true';
SET datafusion.optimizer.enable_dynamic_filter_pushdown = 'true';
SET datafusion.optimizer.enable_sort_pushdown = 'true';
```

### Avoid

```sql
SELECT *
FROM events
ORDER BY event_ts;
```

### Agent rules

```text
Top-K:
  always pair ORDER BY with LIMIT for top-N semantics
  add deterministic tie-breakers
  project narrow columns before sort
  filter before sort
  use dynamic filters for Parquet/layouts with useful stats
  avoid full global sort when top-K is acceptable
```

---

## 29.11 Memory-limited queries

### SQL profile

```sql
SET datafusion.runtime.memory_limit = '8G';
SET datafusion.runtime.temp_directory = '/mnt/nvme/datafusion-spill';
SET datafusion.runtime.max_temp_directory_size = '200G';

SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '4';
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '1024';
SET datafusion.execution.spill_compression = 'lz4_frame';
```

### Rust profile

```rust
use datafusion::execution::{
    runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder,
    session_state::SessionStateBuilder,
};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_memory_limit(8 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024, 0.80)
    .with_temp_file_path("/mnt/nvme/datafusion-spill")
    .with_max_temp_directory_size(200 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)
    .build_arc()?;

let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .with_target_partitions(4)
    .with_batch_size(1024)
    .set_str("datafusion.execution.spill_compression", "lz4_frame");

let state = SessionStateBuilder::new()
    .with_runtime_env(runtime)
    .with_config(config)
    .with_default_features()
    .build();

let ctx = SessionContext::from(state);
```

The tuning guide explicitly recommends lower `target_partitions` and lower `batch_size` under very tight memory limits, because `FairSpillPool` divides memory among partitions and spill merging reads back `batch_size`-sized batches. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Agent rules

```text
Memory-limited:
  reduce target_partitions
  reduce batch_size
  filter/project early
  avoid SELECT *
  prefer sort-merge over hash join where appropriate
  configure fast spill directory
  monitor top memory consumers
```

---

## 29.12 Cloud object storage

### Problem

```text
Latency sources:
  listing files
  fetching metadata/footer
  many small files
  many HTTP requests
  object-store write buffering
  credential/auth round trips
  cold caches
```

### Remote-read profile

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.meta_fetch_concurrency = '32';
SET datafusion.runtime.metadata_cache_limit = '512M';
SET datafusion.runtime.list_files_cache_limit = '128M';
SET datafusion.runtime.list_files_cache_ttl = '5m';

SET datafusion.execution.parquet.metadata_size_hint = '1048576';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.pruning = 'true';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.enable_page_index = 'true';
```

### Remote-write profile

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.objectstore_writer_buffer_size = '10485760';
SET datafusion.execution.minimum_parallel_output_files = '4';
SET datafusion.execution.soft_max_rows_per_output_file = '50000000';
```

### Layout rules

```text
Use:
  s3://bucket/table/
  gs://bucket/table/
  partition=value/ directories
  Parquet
  file compaction
  metadata/listing cache for stable data

Avoid:
  wildcard paths
  millions of tiny objects
  high-cardinality partition directories
  mixed schemas
  arbitrary user-provided LOCATION
```

### Agent rules

```text
Cloud object storage:
  optimize request count, not only CPU
  cache metadata/listings for stable prefixes
  compact small files
  prune by partition columns
  avoid public SQL direct path access
  register object stores/credentials outside SQL where possible
```

## 29.13 Write-heavy workloads

### Parquet write profile

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.compression = 'zstd(3)';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.statistics_enabled = 'page';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.max_row_group_size = '1048576';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.writer_version = '1.0';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.maximum_parallel_row_group_writers = '4';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.maximum_buffered_record_batches_per_stream = '4';
```

### Export SQL

```sql
COPY (
  SELECT event_id, user_id, amount, event_date, region
  FROM clean_events
)
TO 's3://bucket/curated/events/'
STORED AS PARQUET
PARTITIONED BY (event_date, region)
OPTIONS (
  'compression' 'zstd(3)',
  'statistics_enabled' 'page',
  'max_row_group_size' '1048576'
);
```

### DataFrame write

```rust
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

ctx.table("clean_events")
    .await?
    .write_parquet(
        "s3://bucket/curated/events/",
        DataFrameWriteOptions::new()
            .with_partition_by(vec!["event_date".to_string(), "region".to_string()]),
        None,
    )
    .await?;
```

### Write-heavy rules

```text
Parquet:
  prefer zstd for storage/I/O, snappy for compatibility/speed
  write page statistics for future pruning
  tune row group size with memory and scan workload
  avoid high-cardinality partition output
  avoid many tiny files
  use parallel output files for throughput

Object store:
  use directory outputs
  tune writer buffer size
  stage outputs before publishing
  avoid single huge file unless product requires it
```

---

## 29.14 CSV / JSON workloads

### CSV

```text
CSV is parse-heavy, row-oriented, weak for repeated analytics.
Use for import/export/interchange.
Convert to Parquet for repeated scans.
Provide explicit schema.
Set header/delimiter/null behavior.
```

### JSON

```text
JSON is flexible but parse-heavy.
Use for logs/interchange.
Normalize hot fields into typed columns.
Convert to Parquet for repeated analytics.
```

Agent rules:

```text
If query is repeated:
  CSV/JSON -> clean/normalize -> Parquet

If one-time human import/export:
  CSV/JSON acceptable

If nested typed repeated analytics:
  Parquet/Arrow preferred
```

---

## 29.15 Plan-first tuning workflow

### Step 1: Plan

```sql
EXPLAIN
SELECT ...
```

### Step 2: Runtime metrics

```sql
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT ...
```

DataFusion’s explain and optimizer docs recommend `EXPLAIN`/`EXPLAIN VERBOSE` for plan shape and rule effects, and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` for runtime metrics collected by operators. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

### Step 3: Interpret

```text
Look for:
  DataSourceExec: files/partitions/filters/projection
  FilterExec: residual filters not pushed down
  ProjectionExec: width reduction
  RepartitionExec: shuffle/parallelization
  SortExec: global or local sort
  HashJoinExec / SortMergeJoinExec / NestedLoopJoinExec
  AggregateExec partial/final
  CoalesceBatchesExec
  output rows per operator
  elapsed time per operator
```

### Step 4: Change one variable

```text
Change one:
  query shape
  data layout
  config knob
  build profile
  memory/runtime resource
```

### Step 5: Benchmark again

```text
Always compare:
  wall time
  CPU time
  rows read/output
  bytes read
  object-store requests
  spill bytes
  peak memory
  output correctness
```

---

## 29.16 Workload-to-knob index

| Workload          | First knobs                  | Second knobs                                   |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| small/short       | `target_partitions=1`        | lower `batch_size`; avoid repartition          |
| large scan        | projection/filter pushdown   | `target_partitions`; file layout               |
| Parquet analytics | pruning/page index/bloom     | dynamic filters; row groups                    |
| many small files  | compaction                   | metadata/listing cache; meta fetch concurrency |
| selective filters | direct predicates            | bloom/page/pushdown filters                    |
| joins             | stats/build side/repartition | hash vs sort-merge; dynamic join filters       |
| aggregations      | pre-filter/projection        | partitions, spill, batch size                  |
| top-K             | `ORDER BY ... LIMIT`         | top-K dynamic filter pushdown                  |
| memory-limited    | memory/temp dir              | lower partitions/batch size                    |
| object storage    | cache/listing/layout         | metadata size hint, compaction                 |
| write-heavy       | Parquet options              | parallel writers/output file sizing            |
| latency service   | streaming output             | admission control, target partitions           |
| CPU-bound compute | target-cpu/LTO/PGO           | SIMD, allocator                                |
| IO-bound remote   | reduce requests              | caches, pruning, file compaction               |

---

## 29.17 Rust build tuning detail

### Cargo profile variants

```toml
[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
debug = 1
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 16
```

```toml
[profile.release-perf]
inherits = "release"
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
debug = 1
```

### CPU-specific

```bash
RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native' cargo build --release
```

### Portable explicit SIMD target

```bash
RUSTFLAGS='-C target-feature=+avx2' cargo build --release
```

DataFusion’s crate-configuration guide recommends setting `target-cpu` or at least AVX2, preferably `native`, to enable CPU instructions that can speed filtering, aggregation, and joins. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### LTO/codegen tradeoff

```text
lto=true + codegen-units=1:
  better cross-crate optimization
  slower release builds
  useful for production benchmark/profile builds

lto=thin + more codegen units:
  faster builds
  still reasonably optimized
```

### PGO rules

```text
PGO training must represent:
  same file formats
  same SQL shapes
  same UDFs
  same join/aggregate/sort profiles
  same data sizes where possible
```

---

## 29.18 SIMD and Arrow kernels

```text
DataFusion uses Apache Arrow columnar arrays.
CPU-specific code generation helps vectorized kernels and tight loops.
Filtering, joins, aggregates, casts, comparisons, and string/numeric kernels can benefit.
```

The crate-configuration page explicitly says DataFusion can benefit from advanced CPU instructions such as AVX2 and AVX512 for operations like filtering, aggregation, and joins. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
Use target-cpu=native for benchmark on the same host.
Use CPU-feature-gated builds only when deploy fleet supports them.
If deploying containers across mixed nodes, choose conservative CPU target or build variants.
```

---

## 29.19 Service-level performance controls

```text
Query engine config is not enough.
Add service controls:
  max concurrent queries
  queue/admission control
  max rows/bytes output
  max query duration
  per-tenant memory/runtime profile
  object-store credential isolation
  cancellation on client disconnect
```

### Streaming endpoint rule

```rust
let mut stream = df.execute_stream().await?;

while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await {
    let batch = batch?;
    response.write_batch(batch).await?;
}
```

Use `execute_stream` for large/service outputs instead of `collect`, because `collect` buffers all result batches in memory while streaming yields batches incrementally.

---

## 29.20 Benchmark design

### Minimum benchmark dimensions

```text
Build:
  release
  native
  native+LTO
  native+LTO+PGO

Query:
  scan
  filter
  join
  aggregate
  sort/top-K
  write

Data:
  tiny
  moderate
  large
  many files
  selective filters
  nested/wide schema
  object store vs local

Metrics:
  wall time
  CPU utilization
  rows/sec
  bytes/sec
  files/sec
  object-store requests
  peak RSS
  DataFusion reserved memory
  spill bytes/time
```

### Harness pattern

```rust
let start = std::time::Instant::now();

let batches = df.collect().await?;

let elapsed = start.elapsed();
let rows: usize = batches.iter().map(|b| b.num_rows()).sum();

println!("rows={rows}, elapsed_ms={}", elapsed.as_millis());
```

For large results, use streaming and count rows without buffering:

```rust
use futures::StreamExt;

let start = std::time::Instant::now();
let mut rows = 0usize;
let mut stream = df.execute_stream().await?;

while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await {
    rows += batch?.num_rows();
}

println!("rows={rows}, elapsed_ms={}", start.elapsed().as_millis());
```

---

## 29.21 Common performance failure patterns

| Pattern                     | Symptom                               | Fix                                            |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| debug build                 | universally slow                      | `--release`                                    |
| no CPU-specific build       | slower compute kernels                | `target-cpu=native`                            |
| tiny query overparallelized | overhead dominates                    | `target_partitions=1`                          |
| `SELECT *` wide Parquet     | high I/O/CPU                          | projection                                     |
| function-wrapped predicate  | pruning lost                          | normalize/precompute column                    |
| many small files            | request/listing overhead              | compaction/cache                               |
| full sort huge data         | spill/slow                            | TopK or avoid sort                             |
| high-cardinality group      | memory/spill                          | pre-filter/aggregate, reduce key width         |
| hash join OOM               | build too large                       | smaller build, stats, sort-merge               |
| object store cold metadata  | latency high                          | metadata/list cache                            |
| `collect()` in service      | high memory/latency                   | `execute_stream`                               |
| slow writes                 | too few output writers or small files | output file sizing/parallel writers            |
| excessive spills            | memory too low/partitions high        | lower partitions/batch, more memory/spill disk |

## 29.23 Anti-pattern inventory

* Benchmarking debug builds.
* Comparing builds with different CPU targets unknowingly.
* Training PGO on nonrepresentative toy queries.
* Using `target-cpu=native` for heterogeneous deployment binaries.
* Setting `target_partitions` to CPU count for tiny datasets.
* Reading `SELECT *` from wide Parquet.
* Using CSV/JSON as repeated analytics storage.
* Letting object-store paths contain millions of tiny files.
* High-cardinality partition directories.
* Full global `ORDER BY` when top-K is enough.
* `collect()` for arbitrary user/service output.
* Hash join with massive wide build side.
* Enabling experimental optimizer flags globally without benchmarks.
* Enabling Parquet `pushdown_filters` without workload validation.
* Treating object-store latency as a CPU problem.
* Increasing memory before fixing bad query shape/data layout.
* Snapshotting plan/perf across DataFusion upgrades without pinning.

---

## 29.24 Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Build with --release before measuring.
[ ] Test target-cpu=native for CPU-local benchmark.
[ ] Consider LTO/codegen-units=1 for production perf builds.
[ ] Use PGO only with representative workloads.
[ ] Use EXPLAIN before changing configs.
[ ] Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE before declaring bottlenecks.
[ ] Small data: lower target_partitions.
[ ] Memory tight: lower target_partitions and batch_size.
[ ] Large Parquet: project/filter/prune.
[ ] Many small files: compact or cache metadata/listings.
[ ] Selective filters: use direct predicates and Parquet stats/bloom/page index.
[ ] Joins: expose equality keys, stats, smaller build side.
[ ] Aggregations: reduce cardinality and width before grouping.
[ ] Top-K: use ORDER BY + LIMIT with deterministic tie-breakers.
[ ] Cloud object stores: reduce request count and use caches.
[ ] Writes: choose Parquet compression, row group size, partitioning, output file count.
[ ] Services: stream results, cap concurrency, set memory/spill limits.
[ ] Benchmark one change at a time.
```

[1]: https://docs.rs/datafusion/latest/datafusion/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "datafusion - Rust - Docs.rs"
[2]: https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/crate-configuration.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Crate Configuration — Apache DataFusion documentation"
[3]: https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/configs.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Configuration Settings — Apache DataFusion documentation"
[4]: https://datafusion.apache.org/_sources/user-guide/configs.md.txt?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Show Source - Apache DataFusion"
