# DataFusion Advanced — 39) Security and governance

## 39.0 Threat model

```text
Untrusted user input
  ├─ SQL text
  ├─ table names / column names
  ├─ file/object-store locations
  ├─ function calls
  ├─ result-size requests
  ├─ config mutation via SET
  └─ resource-heavy query shapes

Security controls
  ├─ SQL class gating: SQLOptions
  ├─ catalog isolation
  ├─ object-store registry isolation
  ├─ logical-plan validation
  ├─ function allowlist
  ├─ memory/temp/query time limits
  ├─ result limits
  ├─ audit logs
  └─ tenant-scoped RuntimeEnv / SessionContext
```

DataFusion is an embeddable query engine, not a complete database security boundary by itself. `SessionContext` is the main interface for registering sources and executing SQL, and by default `SessionContext::sql` can execute DDL and DML such as `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE VIEW`, and `INSERT INTO`; use `sql_with_options` and application-level plan validation for untrusted SQL. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 39.1 Security responsibility split

| Layer             | DataFusion provides                       | Application must provide                    |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| SQL parsing       | parser, dialect settings, recursion limit | query admission, authn/authz                |
| SQL class gating  | `SQLOptions` for DDL/DML/statements       | endpoint policy                             |
| catalog           | catalog/schema/table traits               | tenant isolation, ACLs, metadata governance |
| file/object store | URL/object-store integration              | credential isolation, path allowlists       |
| execution         | memory pool, temp dir, runtime configs    | quotas, timeouts, concurrency limits        |
| functions         | UDF registration                          | function allowlist, side-effect policy      |
| output            | `RecordBatch` streams                     | row/byte caps, serialization policy         |
| diagnostics       | errors, metrics, plans                    | audit logging, redaction, incident response |

Agent rule:

```text
Treat DataFusion as a query engine inside your trusted boundary.
Do not treat it as a full DBMS authorization, credential, sandbox, or tenant-isolation system unless you implement those layers.
```

---

## 39.2 Accepting user SQL safely

### Read-only SQL executor

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use futures::StreamExt;

pub async fn execute_read_only_sql(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    sql: &str,
    tenant_policy: &TenantPolicy,
    mut sink: impl BatchSink,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(false)
        .with_allow_dml(false)
        .with_allow_statements(false);

    let df = ctx.sql_with_options(sql, options).await?;

    validate_logical_plan(df.logical_plan(), tenant_policy)?;

    let mut stream = df.execute_stream().await?;

    sink.write_schema(stream.schema()).await?;

    while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await {
        let batch = batch?;
        sink.write_batch(batch).await?;
    }

    sink.finish().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

`SQLOptions` describes which SQL statements are allowed. DDL defaults to allowed, DML defaults to allowed, and statement/config SQL such as `SET` also defaults to allowed; therefore public SQL endpoints should explicitly disable all three unless those capabilities are product features. `SessionContext::sql_with_options` validates SQL against these options before returning a `DataFrame`. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Policy matrix

| Endpoint type            |           DDL |           DML | statements / `SET` |      direct paths | recommended                          |
| ------------------------ | ------------: | ------------: | -----------------: | ----------------: | ------------------------------------ |
| public analytics SELECT  |          deny |          deny |               deny |              deny | `sql_with_options` + plan validation |
| internal analyst console |    controlled |    controlled |         controlled |        controlled | authenticated/admin-only             |
| ETL runner               | allow trusted | allow trusted |      allow trusted | allow allowlisted | job identity + audit                 |
| admin migration tool     |         allow |         allow |              allow | allow allowlisted | strong auth + change log             |
| feature validation rule  |          deny |          deny |               deny |              deny | rule result caps                     |

### Agent rules

```text
Never expose ctx.sql(user_sql) directly in public services.
Use sql_with_options for all user SQL.
Disable DDL, DML, and statements for read-only endpoints.
Validate the logical plan after parsing and before execution.
Stream results; avoid collect() for arbitrary user queries.
```

---

## 39.3 DDL / DML governance

### Deny mutation

```rust
let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);
```

### Admin-only mutation

```rust
pub async fn execute_admin_sql(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    principal: &Principal,
    sql: &str,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    require_admin(principal)?;

    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(true)
        .with_allow_dml(true)
        .with_allow_statements(true);

    let df = ctx.sql_with_options(sql, options).await?;

    audit_admin_sql(principal, sql, df.logical_plan())?;

    df.collect().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### DML / DDL risk inventory

```text
DDL risks:
  CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE over arbitrary path
  CREATE TABLE AS SELECT memory consumption
  CREATE VIEW exposing forbidden columns
  DROP TABLE / DROP VIEW removing shared metadata
  CREATE FUNCTION if function factory is enabled

DML/write risks:
  INSERT INTO target table/provider
  COPY query TO file/object-store path
  overwrite/append semantics by provider
  data exfiltration through writable sinks

Statements risks:
  SET memory limits / parser dialect / optimizer flags
  SET timezone / recursion limit
  RESET important service defaults
```

Agent rule:

```text
DDL/DML/admin SQL must have a separate authenticated path, audit trail, path policy, and rollback strategy.
```

---

## 39.4 Preventing arbitrary file reads

### Dangerous in public services

```rust
let ctx = SessionContext::new()
    .enable_url_table(); // do not enable for untrusted SQL
```

`enable_url_table()` permits local file access from SQL such as `SELECT * FROM 'my_file.parquet'`; the docs explicitly call it security-sensitive and say it should only be enabled for systems that intend to permit direct filesystem access from SQL. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Preferred public-service pattern

```rust
pub async fn build_tenant_context(
    tenant: &Tenant,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    // Register only governed, tenant-authorized tables.
    ctx.register_parquet(
        "events",
        tenant.allowed_events_path(),
        ParquetReadOptions::default(),
    )
    .await?;

    Ok(ctx)
}
```

### Direct-path denial policy

```text
Reject:
  SELECT * FROM 'file.parquet'
  SELECT * FROM 's3://arbitrary-bucket/path/'
  CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... LOCATION '/etc/passwd'
  CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... LOCATION 's3://unknown/path/'
```

### Agent rules

```text
Public SQL:
  do not enable_url_table()
  do not expose arbitrary CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE
  do not allow user-provided LOCATION unless allowlisted
  use registered tables and governed catalogs only

Trusted CLI / local admin:
  direct path SQL can be useful
```

---

## 39.5 Object-store credential handling

### Avoid inline secrets in SQL

```sql
-- Avoid in shared logs / public services
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE private_data
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'aws.access_key_id' '...',
  'aws.secret_access_key' '...'
)
LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/';
```

DataFusion CLI docs support explicit S3 credentials in `OPTIONS`, environment/AWS SDK configuration, unsigned public-bucket access, GCS service-account options, and OSS/COS endpoint options; they also document S3 credential precedence as explicit `OPTIONS`, then standard AWS config/environment, then unsigned requests if no credentials are specified. ([datafusion.apache.org][3])

### Preferred Rust object-store registry pattern

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use object_store::aws::AmazonS3Builder;
use url::Url;

pub fn register_tenant_s3(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    tenant: &Tenant,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let store = AmazonS3Builder::new()
        .with_region(tenant.aws_region())
        .with_bucket_name(tenant.bucket())
        .with_access_key_id(tenant.access_key_id())
        .with_secret_access_key(tenant.secret_access_key())
        .build()
        .map_err(|e| datafusion::error::DataFusionError::External(Box::new(e)))?;

    ctx.register_object_store(
        &Url::parse(&format!("s3://{}", tenant.bucket()))?,
        Arc::new(store),
    );

    Ok(())
}
```

### Credential policy

```text
Preferred:
  object-store registry
  runtime/env provider chain
  secret manager
  instance/workload identity
  short-lived credentials
  per-tenant RuntimeEnv/object-store registry

Avoid:
  SQL OPTIONS with long-lived secrets
  logging CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statements containing credentials
  shared object-store registry across tenants with different credentials
  public endpoints that allow user-specified object-store OPTIONS
```

### Unsigned public bucket policy

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE public_dataset
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://public-bucket/path/'
OPTIONS ('aws.skip_signature' 'true');
```

Use unsigned requests only as an explicit public-data policy; do not rely on unsigned fallback for private-data access. The docs also show public S3 access via `aws.SKIP_SIGNATURE` / `aws.skip_signature`. ([datafusion.apache.org][3])

---

## 39.6 Query timeouts and cancellation

DataFusion execution is stream-based, so dropping the stream cancels remaining work. Application code should enforce wall-clock deadlines around planning and stream polling.

### Timeout wrapper

```rust
use futures::StreamExt;
use tokio::time::{timeout, Duration};

pub async fn execute_with_timeout(
    df: DataFrame,
    query_timeout: Duration,
    mut sink: impl BatchSink,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let mut stream = timeout(query_timeout, df.execute_stream())
        .await
        .map_err(|_| datafusion::error::DataFusionError::Execution(
            "query timed out before execution started".to_string(),
        ))??;

    sink.write_schema(stream.schema()).await?;

    loop {
        let next = timeout(query_timeout, stream.next())
            .await
            .map_err(|_| datafusion::error::DataFusionError::Execution(
                "query timed out while producing results".to_string(),
            ))?;

        match next {
            Some(Ok(batch)) => sink.write_batch(batch).await?,
            Some(Err(e)) => return Err(e),
            None => break,
        }
    }

    sink.finish().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Timeout policy

```text
planning_timeout:
  protects parser/planner/optimizer/catalog latency

execution_timeout:
  protects long-running query runtime

idle_batch_timeout:
  protects stream stalls / remote object-store hangs

absolute_deadline:
  protects total request duration

client_disconnect:
  drop stream immediately
```

Agent rules:

```text
DataFusion does not replace application request deadlines.
Wrap planning and streaming in tokio timeouts.
Drop streams on timeout or client disconnect.
Use query_id in timeout errors and audit logs.
```

---

## 39.7 Memory limits and spill governance

### Rust runtime profile

```rust
use datafusion::execution::{
    runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder,
    session_state::SessionStateBuilder,
};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

pub fn secure_runtime_context(
    tenant: &Tenant,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
        .with_memory_limit(tenant.memory_limit_bytes(), 0.80)
        .with_temp_file_path(tenant.spill_dir())
        .with_max_temp_directory_size(tenant.max_spill_bytes())
        .build_arc()?;

    let config = SessionConfig::new()
        .with_target_partitions(tenant.target_partitions())
        .with_batch_size(tenant.batch_size());

    let state = SessionStateBuilder::new()
        .with_runtime_env(runtime)
        .with_config(config)
        .with_default_features()
        .build();

    Ok(SessionContext::from(state))
}
```

Runtime settings can be set through SQL as well: `datafusion.runtime.memory_limit` controls maximum query execution memory, `datafusion.runtime.temp_directory` controls the temp directory path, and `datafusion.runtime.max_temp_directory_size` defaults to `100G` and controls the temporary-file directory size. ([datafusion.apache.org][4])

### Important shared-runtime caveat

```text
If every request creates a new independent RuntimeEnv:
  memory and disk limits are not shared across requests.

If all contexts share one RuntimeEnv:
  memory and disk limits are process-wide for those contexts.
```

The `SessionContext` docs state that by default each new context creates a new `RuntimeEnv`, so resource limits are not enforced across queries run in different contexts unless those contexts share the same `RuntimeEnv`. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Agent rules

```text
Set memory limits for shared services.
Set spill temp directory and max temp size.
Use tenant/workload RuntimeEnv isolation when quotas differ.
Use app-level query concurrency limits; memory pools are not admission control.
Monitor process RSS and spill disk externally too.
```

---

## 39.8 Result limits

### SQL-level cap wrapper

```rust
pub async fn execute_capped_sql(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    sql: &str,
    max_rows: usize,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<Vec<RecordBatch>> {
    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(false)
        .with_allow_dml(false)
        .with_allow_statements(false);

    let df = ctx.sql_with_options(sql, options).await?;

    validate_logical_plan(df.logical_plan(), &Policy::default())?;

    df.limit(0, Some(max_rows))?
        .collect()
        .await
}
```

### Streaming cap

```rust
pub async fn stream_with_row_cap(
    mut stream: datafusion::execution::SendableRecordBatchStream,
    max_rows: usize,
    mut sink: impl BatchSink,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let mut emitted = 0usize;

    sink.write_schema(stream.schema()).await?;

    while let Some(batch) = futures::StreamExt::next(&mut stream).await {
        let batch = batch?;
        emitted += batch.num_rows();

        if emitted > max_rows {
            return Err(datafusion::error::DataFusionError::Execution(format!(
                "result row limit exceeded: max_rows={max_rows}"
            )));
        }

        sink.write_batch(batch).await?;
    }

    sink.finish().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Policy table

| Endpoint          | Result policy                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| interactive UI    | mandatory `LIMIT` or server-side cap |
| API export        | async job + byte/row quota           |
| internal ETL      | job-level output expectations        |
| validation engine | cap examples, separate count         |
| public SQL        | hard row/byte/time cap               |

Agent rules:

```text
LIMIT in user SQL is not enough.
Also enforce server-side row/byte caps.
Do not collect arbitrary user outputs.
Prefer execute_stream for large results.
```

---

## 39.9 SQL parser dialect and recursion limits

### Secure parser profile

```rust
let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .set_str("datafusion.sql_parser.dialect", "generic")
    .set_usize("datafusion.sql_parser.recursion_limit", 50)
    .set_bool("datafusion.sql_parser.enable_ident_normalization", true);
```

```sql
SET datafusion.sql_parser.recursion_limit = '50';
```

DataFusion exposes parser settings including `datafusion.sql_parser.recursion_limit`, which defaults to `50` and limits recursion depth for complex SQL queries. The config docs also document parser settings such as dialect, identifier normalization, string-type mapping, and subquery sort elimination. ([datafusion.apache.org][4])

### Parser governance

```text
dialect:
  choose one product dialect
  document it
  do not let public users SET dialect unless intended

recursion_limit:
  keep bounded
  increase only for trusted workloads
  treat excessive nesting as query complexity risk

identifier normalization:
  keep default unless case-sensitive semantics are product requirement
```

Agent rules:

```text
Parser settings are part of security posture.
Disable SET for public SQL so users cannot alter parser behavior.
Validate query complexity after parsing as well as relying on recursion limits.
```

---

## 39.10 Function allowlists

### Function policy model

```rust
use datafusion::logical_expr::LogicalPlan;

pub struct FunctionPolicy {
    pub allowed_functions: std::collections::HashSet<String>,
    pub denied_functions: std::collections::HashSet<String>,
}

pub fn validate_functions(
    plan: &LogicalPlan,
    policy: &FunctionPolicy,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let mut violations = Vec::new();

    plan.apply_expressions(|expr| {
        for function_name in collect_function_names(expr) {
            let name = function_name.to_ascii_lowercase();

            if policy.denied_functions.contains(&name)
                || !policy.allowed_functions.contains(&name)
            {
                violations.push(name);
            }
        }

        Ok(datafusion::common::tree_node::TreeNodeRecursion::Continue)
    })?;

    if !violations.is_empty() {
        violations.sort();
        violations.dedup();

        return Err(datafusion::error::DataFusionError::Plan(format!(
            "function(s) not allowed: {}",
            violations.join(", ")
        )));
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

### High-risk function classes

```text
volatile:
  random, uuid, current time if deterministic output required

expensive:
  regex over huge text
  levenshtein over huge text
  vector distance cross joins
  unnest over large arrays

diagnostic:
  version
  metadata/cache introspection functions
  arrow_metadata / arrow_field if metadata exposure matters

external:
  async UDFs
  network-calling UDFs
  secret-reading UDFs
```

### Agent rules

```text
Function registration is not the same as function authorization.
Public SQL should have an allowlist.
Do not register side-effecting UDFs into contexts used by untrusted SQL.
Mark volatility correctly.
Audit UDF names, aliases, docs, and argument behavior.
```

---

## 39.11 Catalog isolation

### One catalog/schema per tenant

```text
CatalogProviderList
  ├─ tenant_a_catalog
  │   └─ public
  │       ├─ events
  │       └─ users
  └─ tenant_b_catalog
      └─ public
          ├─ events
          └─ users
```

### Tenant context construction

```rust
pub fn build_tenant_catalog_context(
    tenant: &Tenant,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let ctx = secure_runtime_context(tenant)?;

    let catalog = build_tenant_catalog(tenant)?;
    ctx.register_catalog(tenant.catalog_name(), catalog);

    Ok(ctx)
}
```

### Catalog policy

```text
CatalogProvider:
  controls schemas visible to tenant

SchemaProvider:
  controls table names visible to tenant

TableProvider:
  controls schema, scan, filter/projection pushdown, and data access

information_schema:
  expose only if metadata visibility is allowed
```

The DataFusion configuration docs show default catalog/schema settings and that `information_schema` is disabled by default; exposing information schema can reveal table, column, routine, and configuration metadata, so it should be governed per tenant/security policy. ([datafusion.apache.org][4])

### Agent rules

```text
Do not share one mutable MemoryCatalogProvider across tenants.
Do not rely on table-name prefixes as your only isolation layer.
Use separate catalogs/contexts/runtime envs when credentials or visibility differ.
Filter or disable information_schema for untrusted users.
```

---

## 39.12 Multi-tenant contexts

### Isolation levels

| Level                              | Isolation strength | Use                                     |
| ---------------------------------- | -----------------: | --------------------------------------- |
| shared context, row filters        |               weak | trusted internal users only             |
| shared runtime, per-tenant catalog |             medium | same credentials/resource pool          |
| per-tenant context, shared runtime |             medium | metadata isolation, shared memory limit |
| per-tenant context + runtime       |             strong | separate credentials and quotas         |
| separate process/container         |          strongest | high-risk tenants or strict isolation   |

### Strong tenant builder

```rust
pub async fn build_isolated_tenant_engine(
    tenant: &Tenant,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let ctx = secure_runtime_context(tenant)?;

    register_tenant_object_stores(&ctx, tenant)?;
    register_tenant_catalogs(&ctx, tenant).await?;
    register_tenant_udfs(&ctx, tenant)?;

    Ok(ctx)
}
```

### Agent rules

```text
If credentials differ:
  use separate object-store registries / RuntimeEnv.

If quotas differ:
  use separate RuntimeEnv.

If metadata visibility differs:
  use separate catalog/schema providers.

If user SQL is untrusted:
  use sql_with_options + plan validation per request.
```

---

## 39.13 Logical-plan authorization

### Validator skeleton

```rust
use datafusion::logical_expr::LogicalPlan;
use datafusion::common::tree_node::{TreeNodeRecursion, TreeNode};

pub fn validate_logical_plan(
    plan: &LogicalPlan,
    policy: &TenantPolicy,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    validate_tables(plan, policy)?;
    validate_columns(plan, policy)?;
    validate_functions(plan, policy)?;
    validate_complexity(plan, policy)?;
    validate_no_direct_paths(plan, policy)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Table validation

```rust
pub fn validate_tables(
    plan: &LogicalPlan,
    policy: &TenantPolicy,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let mut denied = Vec::new();

    plan.apply(|node| {
        if let LogicalPlan::TableScan(scan) = node {
            let table = scan.table_name.to_string();

            if !policy.allowed_tables.contains(&table) {
                denied.push(table);
            }
        }

        Ok(TreeNodeRecursion::Continue)
    })?;

    if !denied.is_empty() {
        denied.sort();
        denied.dedup();

        return Err(datafusion::error::DataFusionError::Plan(format!(
            "table access denied: {}",
            denied.join(", ")
        )));
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

### Complexity validation

```text
Reject or cap:
  too many joins
  cross joins
  nested lateral joins
  unbounded ORDER BY
  DISTINCT over wide data
  unbounded unnest
  too many subqueries / CTEs
  direct path scans
  disallowed functions
  missing LIMIT on interactive endpoint
```

Agent rules:

```text
SQLOptions prevents broad statement classes.
Plan validation enforces product-specific authz and complexity.
Run validation before execution.
Repeat validation after rewrites if your application injects/changes plans.
```

---

## 39.14 Row and column security

### Safer: view/provider-level masking

```sql
CREATE VIEW tenant_events AS
SELECT
  event_id,
  event_ts,
  user_id,
  -- omit secret columns
  region
FROM raw_events
WHERE tenant_id = 'tenant_a';
```

### Application-injected filter

```rust
pub fn apply_tenant_filter(
    df: DataFrame,
    tenant: &Tenant,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<DataFrame> {
    df.filter(col("tenant_id").eq(lit(tenant.id.as_str())))
}
```

### Provider-level enforcement

```text
Custom TableProvider::scan:
  always inject tenant predicate
  reject projection of forbidden columns
  expose schema without forbidden columns
  never rely only on user-supplied WHERE clause
```

Agent rules:

```text
Do not trust user SQL to include tenant filters.
Apply row security below or after parsing:
  custom views
  custom TableProvider
  DataFrame-enforced predicates
  logical-plan rewrite

Column security:
  hide columns in schema if possible.
  mask through views/providers if necessary.
```

---

## 39.15 Observability and audit

### Audit event schema

```rust
#[derive(Debug, serde::Serialize)]
pub struct QueryAuditEvent {
    pub query_id: String,
    pub principal_id: String,
    pub tenant_id: String,
    pub sql_hash: String,
    pub statement_class: String,
    pub tables: Vec<String>,
    pub functions: Vec<String>,
    pub started_at_ms: i64,
    pub elapsed_ms: Option<u128>,
    pub rows_returned: Option<usize>,
    pub error_class: Option<String>,
}
```

### Logging rules

```text
Log:
  query_id
  principal
  tenant
  SQL hash
  statement class
  authorized tables
  denied reason
  row count
  elapsed time
  error class
  memory/resource class

Do not log:
  inline credentials
  object-store tokens
  raw access keys
  full raw SQL by default
  sensitive row values
```

### Agent rules

```text
Every denied query should produce an audit event.
Every admin DDL/DML should produce an audit event.
Every resource exhaustion should include query_id and quota class.
Every public error should be sanitized and actionable.
```

## 39.16 Secure endpoint template

```rust
pub async fn secure_sql_endpoint(
    registry: &TenantEngineRegistry,
    request: SqlRequest,
    mut sink: impl BatchSink,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let principal = authenticate(&request)?;
    let tenant = authorize_tenant(&principal, &request.tenant_id)?;

    let ctx = registry.context_for(&tenant)?;

    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(false)
        .with_allow_dml(false)
        .with_allow_statements(false);

    let query_id = new_query_id();

    let df = ctx
        .sql_with_options(&request.sql, options)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.context(format!("planning query_id={query_id}")))?;

    validate_logical_plan(df.logical_plan(), &tenant.policy)
        .map_err(|e| e.context(format!("authorizing query_id={query_id}")))?;

    let df = enforce_result_limit(df, tenant.policy.max_rows)?;

    execute_with_timeout(
        df,
        tenant.policy.query_timeout,
        &mut sink,
    )
    .await
    .map_err(|e| e.context(format!("executing query_id={query_id}")))?;

    Ok(())
}
```

---

## 39.17 Security testing matrix

```text
SQL class gating:
  [ ] CREATE TABLE denied
  [ ] CREATE VIEW denied
  [ ] INSERT denied
  [ ] COPY denied
  [ ] SET denied
  [ ] SELECT allowed

File/object access:
  [ ] direct quoted local path denied
  [ ] direct s3/gs path denied
  [ ] CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE arbitrary LOCATION denied
  [ ] registered allowed table works
  [ ] disallowed table denied

Catalog isolation:
  [ ] tenant A cannot see tenant B tables
  [ ] information_schema disabled or filtered
  [ ] table list matches tenant policy

Function policy:
  [ ] allowed function works
  [ ] denied function fails at validation
  [ ] UDF aliases included in policy
  [ ] volatile/expensive functions policy-tested

Resources:
  [ ] memory limit enforced
  [ ] spill directory limit enforced
  [ ] query timeout cancels stream
  [ ] result row cap enforced
  [ ] concurrency semaphore enforced

Plan validation:
  [ ] cross join policy
  [ ] unbounded ORDER BY policy
  [ ] unnest/cardinality policy
  [ ] missing LIMIT policy
```

---

## 39.18 Deployment hardening checklist

```text
Context/runtime:
  [ ] per-tenant or shared RuntimeEnv chosen intentionally
  [ ] memory_limit set
  [ ] temp_directory set
  [ ] max_temp_directory_size set
  [ ] object stores registered outside user SQL
  [ ] direct URL table disabled for public SQL

SQL:
  [ ] sql_with_options used
  [ ] DDL disabled unless admin endpoint
  [ ] DML disabled unless write endpoint
  [ ] statements disabled unless config endpoint
  [ ] parser dialect fixed
  [ ] recursion limit fixed

Authorization:
  [ ] table allowlist
  [ ] column allowlist/masking
  [ ] row policy
  [ ] function allowlist
  [ ] logical-plan validation

Resources:
  [ ] query timeout
  [ ] result row/byte cap
  [ ] concurrency limits
  [ ] spill disk monitoring
  [ ] memory monitoring

Observability:
  [ ] query IDs
  [ ] SQL hashes
  [ ] audit events
  [ ] sanitized errors
  [ ] EXPLAIN/metrics path for admins
```

---

## 39.19 Anti-pattern inventory

* Public SQL endpoint calling `ctx.sql(user_sql)` directly.
* Relying on `SQLOptions` alone for tenant/table/column authorization.
* Enabling `enable_url_table()` in a multi-tenant or public service.
* Allowing arbitrary `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... LOCATION`.
* Logging raw SQL containing cloud credentials.
* Putting long-lived S3/GCS credentials in SQL `OPTIONS`.
* Sharing one default in-memory catalog across tenants.
* Letting users run `SET datafusion.runtime.memory_limit`.
* Assuming memory limits apply across contexts that do not share `RuntimeEnv`.
* Enforcing row security only by asking users to include `WHERE tenant_id = ...`.
* Registering side-effecting UDFs in public SQL contexts.
* Returning raw internal errors/backtraces to users.
* Using `collect()` for unbounded public query results.
* No query timeout.
* No result limit.
* No audit log for denied queries.

---

## 39.20 Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Treat user SQL as untrusted input.
[ ] Use sql_with_options, not raw ctx.sql, for user SQL.
[ ] Disable DDL, DML, and statements for read-only endpoints.
[ ] Do not enable_url_table for public SQL.
[ ] Register only governed tables/catalogs.
[ ] Register object stores/credentials outside SQL.
[ ] Use per-tenant contexts/runtimes where credentials or quotas differ.
[ ] Validate logical plan for tables, columns, functions, and complexity.
[ ] Enforce row/column policy below user SQL.
[ ] Set parser dialect and recursion limit.
[ ] Use function allowlists.
[ ] Set memory limits, temp directories, and spill quotas.
[ ] Add query timeout and cancellation.
[ ] Add result row/byte limits.
[ ] Add concurrency/admission control.
[ ] Redact SQL/options in logs.
[ ] Audit every denied query and admin mutation.
[ ] Test security controls as first-class integration tests.
```

# DataFusion Advanced — 40) Best practices and anti-patterns

## 40.0 Practical rule map

```text
Best practice classes
  ├─ dependency/version hygiene
  ├─ query interface choice
  ├─ table/source registration
  ├─ file/object-store layout
  ├─ Parquet optimization
  ├─ runtime/resource safety
  ├─ optimizer/rewrite correctness
  ├─ testing and baselines
  ├─ UDF/provider/operator extension safety
  └─ security/governance
```

DataFusion’s top-level crate is the normal entry point for Rust applications: it exposes the high-level APIs and re-exports public dependency types such as Arrow and ObjectStore; the SQL user guide frames `SessionContext` as the high-level SQL entry point after registering data sources as tables. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 40.1 Dependency and type hygiene

### Rule: use `datafusion::arrow` re-exports by default

```rust
use datafusion::arrow::{
    array::{ArrayRef, Int64Array, StringArray},
    datatypes::{DataType, Field, Schema},
    record_batch::RecordBatch,
};
```

Why:

```text
Arrow types are part of DataFusion's public API.
Rust type identity includes crate version.
Two different Arrow versions can produce incompatible RecordBatch/Array/DataType types.
```

The top-level DataFusion crate re-exports Arrow, ObjectStore, and feature-gated Parquet because these types are part of its public API surface; using those re-exports avoids accidental Arrow type mismatches. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Anti-pattern

```rust
// Risky if this `arrow` version differs from DataFusion's Arrow version.
use arrow::record_batch::RecordBatch;
```

### Direct dependency policy

```toml
[dependencies]
datafusion = "=54.1.0"

# Only add if necessary and match DataFusion's Arrow family.
arrow = "=58.4.0"
parquet = "=58.4.0"
```

### Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Prefer datafusion::arrow imports.
[ ] Prefer datafusion::prelude for normal app code.
[ ] Pin datafusion exactly in production.
[ ] If using datafusion-* subcrates directly, align all versions.
[ ] Run cargo tree -d after upgrades.
```

---

## 40.2 Query interface choice

### Rule: prefer DataFrame/Expr API for generated queries

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let df = ctx
    .table("orders")
    .await?
    .filter(
        col("customer_id")
            .eq(lit(customer_id))
            .and(col("amount").gt(lit(0.0))),
    )?
    .select(vec![
        col("order_id"),
        col("amount"),
        (col("amount") * lit(1.08)).alias("amount_with_tax"),
    ])?;
```

DataFrame methods such as `select` and `filter` accept logical `Expr` values, and the expression API is designed for fluent, programmatic expression construction. ([datafusion.apache.org][2])

### Rule: prefer SQL for user-facing query interfaces

```rust
let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);

let df = ctx.sql_with_options(user_sql, options).await?;
```

DataFusion has a full SQL API via `SessionContext`; using SQL is appropriate when query text is the product interface, while lower-level options such as `sql_with_options` are needed for governed endpoints. ([datafusion.apache.org][3])

### Decision table

| Situation                        | Prefer                                     |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| programmatic service filters     | DataFrame + `Expr`                         |
| trusted internal query templates | SQL or DataFrame                           |
| human query authoring            | SQL                                        |
| public SQL endpoint              | SQL + `sql_with_options` + plan validation |
| custom query compiler            | `LogicalPlanBuilder`                       |
| custom runtime source            | `TableProvider`                            |

### Anti-patterns

```text
String-concatenating user literals into SQL.
Using SQL snippets where Expr builders are safer.
Using DataFrame API to emulate complex human-authored SQL when SQL is the product.
Using ctx.sql(user_sql) directly in public endpoints.
```

---

## 40.3 Table registration and schema stability

### Rule: register tables explicitly for stable schemas

```rust
ctx.register_parquet(
    "events",
    "s3://lake/events/",
    ParquetReadOptions::default(),
)
.await?;

let df = ctx.sql("SELECT event_id, event_ts FROM events").await?;
```

`SessionContext` supports creating DataFrames from sources, registering CSV/Parquet/custom data sources as named SQL tables, and executing SQL; explicit registration gives stable names and schema contracts for SQL and DataFrame paths. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Prefer

```text
register_parquet / register_csv / register_json / register_avro / register_arrow
custom TableProvider registration
custom CatalogProvider / SchemaProvider
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE only through trusted/admin paths
```

### Avoid in services

```sql
SELECT * FROM 's3://arbitrary/path/';
SELECT * FROM '/etc/passwd';
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE x STORED AS PARQUET LOCATION 's3://unknown/path/';
```

### Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Register governed tables by name.
[ ] Use stable aliases and schemas.
[ ] Avoid public direct-path SQL.
[ ] Use custom catalogs for tenant/workspace table governance.
[ ] Validate schemas after registration with DESCRIBE / df.schema().
```

---

## 40.4 File and object-store paths

### Rule: avoid wildcards; use directory roots

```sql
-- Preferred
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE t
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/table_root/';

-- Avoid
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE t
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/*.parquet';
```

DataFusion’s datasource docs state wildcards are not supported in file paths and recommend specifying directory roots so DataFusion reads all compatible files under the directory; the same docs show Hive-style partition discovery for paths such as `a=1/b=100/file.parquet`. ([datafusion.apache.org][5])

### Rule: use Hive-style partitions deliberately

```text
s3://lake/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=us/part-000.parquet
s3://lake/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=eu/part-001.parquet
```

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM events
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22'
  AND region = 'us';
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
Wildcard paths.
Directory path intended but no trailing `/` where source treats it as file.
Millions of tiny files.
High-cardinality partition directories.
Mixed schemas in one directory table.
User-supplied arbitrary LOCATION in public SQL.
```

---

## 40.5 Parquet layout and statistics

### Rule: use Parquet for repeated analytics

```text
CSV / JSON:
  ingestion, interchange, debugging

Parquet:
  repeated analytics, lake tables, nested typed data, pruning, compression
```

### Rule: write statistics and partition for future reads

```sql
COPY (
  SELECT *
  FROM clean_events
)
TO 's3://lake/curated/events/'
STORED AS PARQUET
PARTITIONED BY (event_date, region)
OPTIONS (
  'compression' 'zstd(3)',
  'statistics_enabled' 'page',
  'max_row_group_size' '1048576',
  'bloom_filter_enabled::event_id' 'true'
);
```

Parquet tuning knobs include page index, row-group pruning, bloom-filter reads, filter pushdown, compression, row-group size, statistics, writer version, and parallel writer settings; the configuration docs describe these read/write controls and their memory/performance tradeoffs. ([datafusion.apache.org][6])

### Agent rules

```text
Use low/moderate-cardinality partition columns.
Write page statistics for selective scans.
Use bloom filters for high-value equality keys, not low-cardinality booleans.
Tune row group size with workload and memory constraints.
Use zstd for storage/I/O efficiency; snappy for broad compatibility.
```

---

## 40.6 Runtime resource safety

### Rule: set memory and temp directory limits in services

```rust
let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_memory_limit(8 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024, 0.80)
    .with_temp_file_path("/mnt/nvme/datafusion-spill")
    .with_max_temp_directory_size(200 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)
    .build_arc()?;
```

The configuration docs expose runtime memory, temp-directory, and max-temp-directory settings; they also recommend smaller `target_partitions` and `batch_size` under tight memory because spilling reads batches back at the configured batch size and memory is divided among partitions. ([datafusion.apache.org][6])

### SQL equivalent

```sql
SET datafusion.runtime.memory_limit = '8G';
SET datafusion.runtime.temp_directory = '/mnt/nvme/datafusion-spill';
SET datafusion.runtime.max_temp_directory_size = '200G';
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '4';
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '1024';
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
Unbounded memory pool in multi-tenant service.
No temp directory for spill-capable workloads.
Spill directory on slow/unmonitored filesystem.
High target_partitions under tight memory.
collect() for arbitrary public query results.
No query concurrency limit.
```

---

## 40.7 Tune `target_partitions` for workload size

### Small queries

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '1';
```

For very small datasets, the configuration guide recommends `target_partitions = 1` to avoid repartitioning overhead. ([datafusion.apache.org][7])

### Large scans

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '0'; -- CPU-derived default
```

### Memory-limited workloads

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '4';
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '1024';
```

### Rule table

| Workload                     | `target_partitions` stance                               |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| tiny data / short query      | `1`                                                      |
| large local Parquet scan     | CPU/core-derived default or measured value               |
| cloud object-store scan      | enough to overlap I/O; avoid tiny task explosion         |
| memory-tight group/join/sort | lower partitions                                         |
| high concurrency service     | lower per-query partitions + app-level admission control |
| batch ETL                    | higher partitions if memory/disk allows                  |

### Anti-pattern

```text
Assuming more partitions always improves performance.
It can increase scheduling, repartition, memory fragmentation, and spill pressure.
```

---

## 40.8 Explainability and regression baselines

### Rule: add `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` baselines for important workloads

```sql
EXPLAIN FORMAT INDENT
SELECT ...;

EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT ...;
```

`EXPLAIN` shows the logical and physical plans without running the query, while `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` executes it and includes runtime metrics collected by operators; DataFusion metrics expose where time is spent and how rows/bytes flow through the pipeline. ([datafusion.apache.org][8])

### Baseline inventory

```text
Correctness:
  result rows
  schema
  nullability
  deterministic order

Plan:
  DataSourceExec
  FilterExec residuals
  RepartitionExec count
  join algorithm
  SortExec / TopK
  AggregateExec partial/final

Metrics:
  elapsed_compute
  output_rows
  output_batches
  output_bytes
  spill bytes
  files/row groups pruned
```

### Agent rules

```text
Use EXPLAIN before tuning.
Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE before declaring a bottleneck.
Pin DataFusion version for exact plan snapshots.
Use semantic plan assertions where possible.
Compare result + plan + metrics, not timing alone.
```

---

## 40.9 Optimizer rewrites

### Rule: preserve expression names in optimizer rewrites

```rust
// Conceptual rewrite
// old output expression: 1 + 2
// simplified value:      3
// output name must remain compatible:
lit(3i64).alias("Int64(1) + Int64(2)");
```

DataFusion identifies columns using string names, so optimizer rewrites must preserve expression names; the optimizer guide explicitly says rewritten expressions should typically be aliased back to the original display name. ([datafusion.apache.org][9])

### Custom optimizer checklist

```text
[ ] Same results.
[ ] Same output schema.
[ ] Same output expression names.
[ ] Aliases preserved.
[ ] Volatile expressions not duplicated/reordered.
[ ] Transformed::no returned for no-op.
[ ] plan.check_invariants() passes.
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
Changing output field names during simplification.
Dropping aliases.
Matching functions only by string name when UDFs can override names.
Duplicating volatile/random/time expressions.
Returning "changed" when rule did nothing.
```

---

## 40.10 UDF extension safety

### Rule: test UDFs with Arrow nulls, empty arrays, and type coercion cases

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::arrow::array::{ArrayRef, Int64Array};
use datafusion::logical_expr::ColumnarValue;

let input = ColumnarValue::Array(
    Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![Some(1), None, Some(3)])) as ArrayRef
);
```

DataFusion’s UDF guide covers scalar, window, aggregate, table, and async scalar UDFs; scalar UDFs are vectorized over Arrow arrays, and Arrow arrays can contain null values represented naturally from `Option<T>` values. ([datafusion.apache.org][10])

### Required UDF test matrix

```text
Scalar UDF:
  [ ] ColumnarValue::Array
  [ ] ColumnarValue::Scalar
  [ ] empty arrays
  [ ] null inputs
  [ ] all-null inputs
  [ ] wrong arity
  [ ] wrong datatype
  [ ] return type inference
  [ ] SQL invocation
  [ ] DataFrame invocation

UDAF:
  [ ] update_batch
  [ ] state
  [ ] merge_batch
  [ ] evaluate empty/all-null input

UDTF:
  [ ] bad argument count/type
  [ ] schema stability
  [ ] pushdown over returned provider
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
panic!/unwrap! in UDFs.
Ignoring ColumnarValue::Scalar.
Returning arrays with wrong length.
Wrong volatility.
Not testing null propagation.
Doing blocking network I/O in sync scalar UDFs.
```

---

## 40.11 SQL vs DataFrame anti-injection policy

### Safer generated filter

```rust
df.filter(
    col("customer_id").eq(lit(customer_id))
)?;
```

### Risky SQL concatenation

```rust
let sql = format!("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = {customer_id}");
```

### Better SQL endpoint boundary

```rust
let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);

let df = ctx.sql_with_options(user_sql, options).await?;
validate_logical_plan(df.logical_plan(), &policy)?;
```

Agent rules:

```text
Generated application logic:
  DataFrame/Expr.

Human-authored SQL:
  SQL + sql_with_options + logical-plan validation.

Never:
  SQL-concatenate untrusted identifiers/literals.
  Expose direct path SQL to untrusted users.
```

---

## 40.12 Catalog and governance

### Rule: isolate tenants with catalogs/contexts/runtimes when visibility or credentials differ

```text
Tenant A:
  SessionContext
    RuntimeEnv A
    ObjectStoreRegistry A
    CatalogProvider A

Tenant B:
  SessionContext
    RuntimeEnv B
    ObjectStoreRegistry B
    CatalogProvider B
```

### Agent rules

```text
Shared context is acceptable only when:
  users are trusted
  catalogs are immutable
  all users have same visibility
  statements/DDL/DML are disabled or controlled

Per-tenant context/runtime is required when:
  credentials differ
  quotas differ
  table visibility differs
  function allowlists differ
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
One mutable MemoryCatalogProvider for all tenants.
Row security only by asking users to include WHERE tenant_id = ...
Information_schema exposed without metadata policy.
Object-store credentials embedded in SQL.
```

---

## 40.13 Result and execution safety

### Rule: stream large results

```rust
use futures::StreamExt;

let mut stream = df.execute_stream().await?;

while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await {
    let batch = batch?;
    sink.write_batch(batch).await?;
}
```

### Rule: collect only bounded results

```rust
let batches = df
    .limit(0, Some(1000))?
    .collect()
    .await?;
```

### Safety controls

```text
[ ] query timeout
[ ] row cap
[ ] byte cap
[ ] memory limit
[ ] spill directory quota
[ ] concurrency semaphore
[ ] cancellation on disconnect
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
collect() on arbitrary public SQL.
No LIMIT or server-side cap in interactive endpoints.
No timeout.
No admission control.
```

---

## 40.14 Object-store and remote-data practices

### Good

```text
s3://lake/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=us/part-000.parquet
```

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE events
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://lake/events/';
```

### Bad

```text
s3://lake/events/*.parquet
s3://lake/events/user_id=<millions>/...
s3://lake/events/mixed_schema_files/
```

### Remote profile

```sql
SET datafusion.runtime.metadata_cache_limit = '512M';
SET datafusion.runtime.list_files_cache_limit = '128M';
SET datafusion.runtime.list_files_cache_ttl = '5m';
SET datafusion.execution.meta_fetch_concurrency = '32';
```

DataFusion’s CLI-specific cache functions document that listing table file lists are cached in `ListFilesCache`, and subsequent queries against the same table can reuse cached file-listing information instead of relisting files. ([datafusion.apache.org][11])

### Anti-patterns

```text
Treating cloud-object latency as a CPU problem.
No metadata/listing cache for stable remote prefixes.
Huge number of tiny objects.
High-cardinality partition directories.
Raw secrets in SQL OPTIONS.
```

---

## 40.15 Testing practices

### Rule: use exact vs unordered assertions intentionally

```rust
// Deterministic order required.
assert_batches_eq!(expected, &batches);

// Order-independent comparison.
assert_batches_sorted_eq!(expected, &batches);
```

### Rule: add `ORDER BY` for exact row-order tests

```sql
SELECT id, score
FROM scored
ORDER BY score DESC, id ASC
LIMIT 10;
```

### Rule: use typed assertions for floats/nested/nullability

```rust
let field = batch.schema().field_with_name("amount")?;
assert_eq!(field.data_type(), &DataType::Float64);
assert!(field.is_nullable());
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
Exact row-order assertions without ORDER BY.
Pretty-table equality for floats.
No schema/nullability checks.
Only testing success paths.
No SQLLogicTests for public SQL surfaces.
No EXPLAIN baseline for performance-critical queries.
```

---

## 40.16 Custom provider/operator practices

### Rule: choose the highest-level extension that works

```text
Need custom row-wise function:
  UDF

Need table-like data source:
  TableProvider

Need file-like source:
  FileFormat/FileSource/ListingTable path

Need custom relational semantics:
  LogicalPlan::Extension + physical planner

Need custom runtime algorithm:
  ExecutionPlan
```

### Custom `TableProvider` rules

```text
schema():
  cheap, stable, correct

scan():
  planning only; no heavy I/O

supports_filters_pushdown():
  Exact only if exact
  Inexact for pruning/candidate reduction
  Unsupported when not handled

RecordBatchStream:
  every batch matches schema
  stream cancellation safe
```

### Custom `ExecutionPlan` rules

```text
PlanProperties truthful.
DisplayAs implemented.
ExecutionPlan::metrics implemented.
MemoryReservation used for buffered state.
execute() returns stream quickly.
stream polling does the work.
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
Fetching remote data in TableProvider::scan.
Blocking Tokio worker threads in stream poll.
Claiming exact pushdown for approximate filters.
Reporting ordering/partitioning that is not guaranteed.
No metrics/display for production custom operators.
```

---

## 40.17 Configuration practices

### Service baseline

```rust
let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .with_batch_size(8192)
    .with_target_partitions(num_cpus::get())
    .set_str("datafusion.execution.time_zone", "UTC")
    .set_str("datafusion.sql_parser.dialect", "generic")
    .set_usize("datafusion.sql_parser.recursion_limit", 50);
```

The `SessionConfig` docs state it customizes `SessionContext` and accepts namespaced keys such as `datafusion.execution.batch_size` and other built-in `datafusion.*` options. ([Docs.rs][12])

### Rule table

| Setting             | Best practice                                       |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `time_zone`         | set explicitly, usually UTC                         |
| `target_partitions` | tune by workload                                    |
| `batch_size`        | default for throughput; lower under memory pressure |
| parser dialect      | set explicitly for product SQL                      |
| parser recursion    | keep bounded for public SQL                         |
| memory limit        | set in services                                     |
| temp dir            | set in services                                     |
| explain settings    | enable schema/statistics in debug profiles          |

### Anti-patterns

```text
Letting public users run SET.
Relying on default timezone.
Using one config profile for tiny interactive queries and batch ETL.
No SHOW ALL/config capture in regression baselines.
```

---

## 40.18 Security practices

### Rule: public SQL requires layered controls

```text
Layer 1:
  sql_with_options disables DDL/DML/statements

Layer 2:
  logical-plan validation checks tables, columns, functions, complexity

Layer 3:
  runtime limits: memory/temp/time/result/concurrency

Layer 4:
  catalog/object-store/function isolation

Layer 5:
  audit logs and sanitized errors
```

### Minimum public SQL endpoint

```rust
let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);

let df = ctx.sql_with_options(user_sql, options).await?;
validate_logical_plan(df.logical_plan(), &tenant_policy)?;
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
Public ctx.sql(user_sql).
enable_url_table in public service.
DDL/DML allowed by default.
Function registry includes side-effecting UDFs.
No tenant-specific catalog/object-store isolation.
No row/byte/time cap.
```

---

## 40.19 Deployment practices

### CLI / local tool

```text
Allow:
  direct paths
  DDL/DML/SET
  rich EXPLAIN
  local configs

Require:
  version capture
  input/output paths explicit
```

### Public service

```text
Deny:
  direct paths
  DDL
  DML
  SET
  arbitrary LOCATION
  unapproved functions

Require:
  per-tenant policy
  memory/temp/time/result/concurrency caps
  streaming output
  audit
```

### Batch ETL

```text
Allow:
  trusted DDL/DML/COPY
  large memory/spill profile
  job-scoped staging paths

Require:
  output validation
  row/file counts
  staging + publish
  retry/idempotency policy
```

---

## 40.20 Final anti-pattern inventory

```text
Dependency:
  importing mismatched arrow crate types
  mixing datafusion-* versions

Query building:
  SQL string concatenation for untrusted values
  using SQL where Expr builders are safer
  using DataFrame API where user SQL is the product

Sources:
  arbitrary direct path SQL in public services
  object-store wildcards
  mixed schemas in table directory
  CSV/JSON as repeated analytics storage

Parquet:
  no stats/page index for selective workloads
  high-cardinality partitions
  many tiny files
  bloom filters on low-value columns

Runtime:
  no memory limit
  no spill directory
  no query timeout
  no result cap
  high partitions under tight memory
  collect() on unbounded results

Optimizer/extensions:
  changed expression names in rewrites
  unsafe volatile expression rewrites
  exact pushdown lies
  custom exec without metrics/display/memory accounting

Testing:
  no null tests
  no empty-array UDF tests
  no schema/nullability assertions
  exact row-order tests without ORDER BY
  no EXPLAIN ANALYZE baselines

Security:
  ctx.sql(user_sql) in public endpoint
  SET allowed to untrusted users
  raw credentials in SQL OPTIONS/logs
  shared tenant catalog/runtime with different visibility/credentials
```

[ ] Use datafusion::arrow re-exports.

### SMARTREF Planning And Runtime Boundary

`smartref_planning` is the non-executing compiler for SQL, PlanSpecV2, logical
plan imports, and Delta write handoffs. `smartref_runtime` owns sessions,
runtime environment, provider registry, plan cache, streams, and handoff
execution. Boundary layers must call the compiler/runtime instead of invoking
DataFusion planning or execution APIs as independent authority.
